docs.title: Welcome
docs.text:
Step-by-Step Introduction to the [Vue.js] Web Framework

created by Anthropic’s AI Claude at the request of Serge Tahé - September 2026

This document is a translation of the original French version, generated using an automated tool. Some expressions or technical terms may not fully reflect the original meaning.

This course shows, step by step, how to write a web application with the Vue.js 3 framework: a single-page application (SPA) whose pages are built in the browser from the JSON data of a server.

It starts with 20 small examples, each focused on a single concept: a Vite project, reactivity (ref, reactive, computed, watch), directives, events, forms and their validation; components (props, events, v-model, slots, life cycle, composables, provide / inject); routing with vue-router, its parameters and navigation guards; shared state with Pinia stores; internationalization with vue-i18n; and finally talking to the server (fetch, Vite proxy, httpOnly cookie, API access layer, server errors).

The server is treated as a black box: it is the JSON server of the RdvMedecins application, written with NestJS. You install it, study its API and query it with 48 curl examples, without having to read its code.

Then comes a complete case study: the Vue.js client of RdvMedecins, an appointment-booking application for a medical practice, in which every file is commented, followed by its deployment.

This course follows the NestJS course, in which the server builds the pages. The same pages are written with other frameworks in the Angular, React and Flutter courses. The course A Vue.js/NestJS Client/Server Example studies both the server and the client.

All courses by Serge Tahé

docs.title: 13.1. Installation of Node.js
docs.text:
[Node.js] can be downloaded from nodejs.org: select version LTS (long-term support), preferably 22 ([Vite] 7 requires at least version 20.19). The [Windows] installer also installs [npm]. Verify the installation in a console:

node --version
npm --version

To run multiple versions of [Node.js] on the same machine, you can use [nvm-windows] (under [Windows]) or [nvm] (under [Linux] and [macOS]).

The examples and case study do not require the installation of any global tools: [Vite], [TypeScript], [vue-tsc] (and, for the server, the [nest] tool) are part of each project’s dependencies, installed by [npm install].

docs.title: 13.2. Installing Visual Studio Code
docs.text:
[Visual Studio Code] is downloaded via code.visualstudio.com. For the [.vue] files, install the Vue (Official) extension (editor Vue.volar) from the Extensions panel (Ctrl+Shift+X): syntax highlighting, code completion, type checking ([TypeScript]) in templates, and navigation to the definition of a component or prop.

Open a project via the File / Open Folder menu (the [exemples-vuejs] folder, for example), and open a console within it via the Terminal / New Terminal menu.

docs.title: 13.3. The Vue.js devtools extension
docs.text:
The Vue.js devtools extension can be installed from the extension store for [Chrome], [Edge], or [Firefox]. It adds a “View” tab to the browser’s developer tools (F12), which displays:

  • the page component tree, and, for each component, its props and state ([ref], [reactive], [computed]);
  • the [Pinia] panels and their contents;
  • the router's routes and the current route;
  • A timeline of events emitted by the components.

You can modify a piece of data there and watch the page update: an excellent way to understand responsiveness.

docs.title: 13.4. Installing MySQL with Laragon
docs.text:
The JSON server requires [MySQL] (or [MariaDB]). [Laragon] (laragon.org) installs one under [Windows], ready to use, along with the [HeidiSQL] administration tool. After installation:

  • the “Start All” button launches the [MySQL] server on port 3306;
  • the user [root] has no password: these are the default values from the server’s [.env.example] file;
  • in [HeidiSQL] (the “Database” button), the File / Run SQL menu item runs the [database/dbrdvmedecins2.sql] script.

In [Linux] or [macOS], install [MySQL] or [MariaDB] using the system’s package manager, and run the script using the command-line client: [mysql -u root -p < database/dbrdvmedecins2.sql].

docs.title: 13.5. Installing curl
docs.text:
[curl] is included with [Windows] versions 10 and 11, [macOS], and most distributions of [Linux]. Check its version:

curl --version

The option [--json], used in this document, has been available since version 7.82 (2022). If you are using an older version, replace [--json @fichier] with [-H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @fichier], or install a recent version starting with curl.se.

In [PowerShell], you must enter [curl.exe], not [curl]: In [PowerShell], [curl] is an alias for another command ([Invoke-WebRequest]), which does not include the options from [curl]. The command prompt ([cmd]) does not have this issue.

docs.title: 10. Case Study: The Vue.js client for the RdvMedecins application
10.1. The Problem
docs.text:
The [RdvMedecins] application allows users to schedule appointments at a doctor’s office. The [NestJS] course wrote it as a HTML application, in which the server generated the pages. Here we are writing the client [Vue.js]: the MÊMES pages, generated in the browser from the JSON data on the server described in the chapter “The RdvMedecins Server: A Black Box.”

The client must provide everything that the HTML application provided:

  • a login page, protected by a CAPTCHA, with the option to create a patient account;
  • a doctor’s schedule for a given day, with appointment booking (patient selection window) and cancellation;
  • for the administrator, management of doctors and clients (list, add, edit, delete);
  • for the patient, a personal dashboard (showing upcoming appointments, which they can cancel) and account management;
  • two languages: French and English;
  • unique URLs ([/agenda?idMedecin=1&jour=...]), which can be reloaded, bookmarked, and navigated using the browser’s Back/Forward buttons.

docs.title: 10.2. Installation and Execution
docs.text:
The JSON server must be installed and running (see previous chapter). To use the client in a browser, you do not need the CAPTCHA test mode: you can leave PAS blank in the server’s [.env] file.

In a console window open to the [rdvmedecins-vuejs] folder:

npm install
npm run dev

Then open http://localhost:5173 in a browser. The demo accounts are listed on the login page (password = login).

The [Vite] server in the examples also uses port 5173. If this port is already in use, [Vite] will take another one (5174...) and display it in the console: you must then open that address.

docs.title: 10.5.2. vite.config.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// vite.config.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
//    - npm run de  v : development server at http://localhost:5173;
//                      /api/... requests are forwarded to the JSON server
//                      (port 8080) via the proxy: the page and API have the same
//                      origin; the token cookie is passed normally;
//    - npm run build: the compiled application is in dist/. To deploy it
//                      production, copy the CONTENU from dist/ to the
//                      client/ folder on the JSON server, which then serves it itself
//                      (see the "Deployment" chapter).
// =========================================================================

import { defineConfig } from 'vite';
import vue from '@vitejs/plugin-vue';

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [vue()],
  server: {
    port: 5173,
    proxy: {
       '/api': 'http://localhost:8080',
    },
  },
   // npm run preview: serves dist/ (after npm run build), using the same proxy
  preview: {
    port: 4173,
    proxy: {
       '/api': 'http://localhost:8080',
    },
  },
});
  • lines 21–23: the proxy for requests from [/api] to the server JSON;
  • lines 26–31: the same proxy for [npm run preview].

An important detail: the application uses “clean” addresses ([/agenda], [/mon-espace]). If you reload the page [/agenda], the browser requests [/agenda] from the server for [Vite]. Since the server cannot find a file with that name, it returns [index.html] (this is its default behavior for a single-page application); the application launches, and its router displays the calendar page.

docs.title: 10.6.2. src/main.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// main.ts - application startup
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
//    1. Bootstrap (CSS) and our few styles;
//    2. Pinia (stores), vue-i18n (languages), the router;
//    3. Handling a 401 response from any request:
//       The session has expired—the user is logged out and redirected to the
//       login page, with a message;
//    4. Display in <div id="app">.
// =========================================================================

import { createApp } from 'vue';
import { createPinia } from 'pinia';
import 'bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css';
import './styles.css';
import App from './App.vue';
import { i18n } from './i18n';
import { router } from './router';
import { quandNonAuthentifie } from './api/client-http';
import { useSessionStore } from './stores/session';
import { useMessagesStore } from './stores/messages';

const app = createApp(App);
app.use(createPinia());
app.use(i18n);
app.use(router);

quandNonAuthentifie(() => {
  useSessionStore().oublier();
  useMessagesStore().flash('erreur', 'ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED');
  router.push({ name: 'login' });
});

app.mount('#app');
  • Lines 24–26: the three extensions: caches, languages, and the router. [Pinia] must be installed; AVANT is the router: the router guard uses a cache;
  • Lines 28–32: What to do when any request receives a 401 response (session expired, account deleted, etc.): forget the user, prepare the message “Your session has expired” for the next page, and redirect to the login page. This response is declared UNE times here; the function [quandNonAuthentifie] is described with [client-http.ts].

docs.title: 10.6.3. src/App.vue
docs.text:
<!--
  =========================================================================
  App.vue - le composant racine : le GABARIT commun à toutes les pages
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  L'équivalent de views/layout.hbs de l'application HTML :
    - la barre de navigation ;
    - un message de succès en HAUT ;
    - la page courante (<RouterView>) ;
    - la zone d'erreur en BAS ;
    - la fenêtre de confirmation, une fois pour toute l'application.

  :key="String(route.name)" sur <RouterView> : quand on passe d'une route à
  une AUTRE (de /medecins à /clients, par exemple), le composant de la page
  est recréé ; quand seule la query change (/agenda?jour=...), il est
  conservé, et c'est lui qui suit l'URL.
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { RouterView, useRoute } from 'vue-router';
import BarreNavigation from './components/BarreNavigation.vue';
import MessageSucces from './components/MessageSucces.vue';
import ZoneErreur from './components/ZoneErreur.vue';
import FenetreConfirmation from './components/FenetreConfirmation.vue';

const route = useRoute();
</script>

<template>
  <div class="container py-4">
    <BarreNavigation />
    <MessageSucces />
    <RouterView :key="String(route.name)" />
    <ZoneErreur />
  </div>
  <FenetreConfirmation />
</template>

The template common to all pages, equivalent to [views/layout.hbs]:

  • line 30: the navigation bar;
  • line 31: a success message at the top;
  • line 32: the current page. The [:key] attribute: when a component’s key changes, [Vue.js] destroys it and creates a new one. With the route as the key (NOM), switching from [/medecins] to [/clients] (two different routes, displayed by the same component) recreates the page, which reloads its data. When only the [query] changes (to [/agenda?jour=...]), the page is retained, and it is this page that follows its URL;
  • line 33: the error area, at the bottom;
  • line 35: the confirmation window, displayed once for the entire application.

The styles for the HTML application, with one addition:

  • Line 28: The error area, which “sticks” to the bottom of the window, may overlap a button (a confirmation window in the center of a short page, for example); it contains nothing clickable, and a click passes right through it.

docs.title: 10.7.1. src/api/types.ts
docs.text:
The JSON objects of the API, described in the chapter on the black box, translated into [TypeScript] interfaces:

// =========================================================================
// api/types.ts - the JSON objects exchanged with the server
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The translation, into TypeScript interfaces, of the API described in Chapter
// "The Server, a Black Box." The compiler thus verifies that the client
// uses only fields that actually exist.
// =========================================================================

export type Role = 'ADMIN' | 'DOCTOR' | 'USER';

// POST /api/auth/login, GET /api/auth/me, PUT /api/my-account
export interface Utilisateur {
  login: string;
  nom: string; // display name: "Marie PELISSIER"
  role: Role;
}

// GET /api/captcha
export interface Captcha {
  id: string;
  svg: string;
}

// a title, a first name, a last name
export interface Identite {
  titre: string;
  prenom: string;
  nom: string;
}

// a doctor or a client: GET /api/doctors, GET /api/clients/:id...
export interface Personne extends Identite {
  id: number;
  version: number; // optimistic lock: to be sent back with a modification
  login?: string; // only for ADMIN
}

// what is sent to create/modify a person (ADMIN)
export interface DonneesPersonne extends Identite {
  login: string; // '' = default value (creation) or unchanged (modification)
  password: string; // same as above
  version?: number;
}

export interface Creneau {
  id: number;
  hdebut: number;
  mdebut: number;
  hfin: number;
  mfin: number;
}

// an appointment entry, with the DROITS for the logged-in user
export interface CreneauAgenda extends Creneau {
  libre: boolean;
  patient: Identite | null; // null: available, or occupied by another patient
  moi: boolean; // the logged-in patient’s appointment
  reservable: boolean;
  idRv: number | null; // indicates whether the user can cancel
}

// GET /api/agenda?idMedecin=...&day=...
export interface Agenda {
  medecin: Personne;
  jour: string; // "yyyy-MM-dd"
  creneaux: CreneauAgenda[];
  info: string | null; // translation key (patient who already has an appointment)
}

// GET /api/my-account
export interface MonEspace {
  patient: Identite;
  rendezVous: { id: number; jour: string; creneau: Creneau; medecin: Personne }[];
}

// GET /api/my-account
export interface MonCompte extends Identite {
  login: string;
  version: number;
}

// PUT /api/my-account
export interface ModificationMonCompte extends Identite {
  login: string;
  password: string; // '' = unchanged
  confirmation: string;
  motDePasseActuel: string;
  version: number;
}

// POST /api/registration
export interface Inscription extends Identite {
  login: string;
  password: string;
  confirmation: string;
}
  • line 32: one interface can extend another: a [Personne] is a [Identite] that additionally has an ID, a version, and, for the ADMIN, a login;
  • Line 54: An entry in the calendar: a time slot, plus the permissions of the logged-in user;
  • lines 39 and following: what the client ENVOIE sends to the server.

docs.title: 10.7.2. src/api/client-http.ts
docs.text:
The [requete] function from Example 19 ([commun/api.ts]), with centralized handling of the 401 response:

// =========================================================================
// api/client-http.ts - the function that sends TOUTES requests to API
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Reuse of examples from commun/api.ts, with a new feature: centralized handling
// Centralized handling of the 401 response.
//
// A 401 can occur at any time: the token has expired (2 hours), the
// account has been deleted, the server has restarted with a different
// secret key... Rather than handling this case in each component, we
// notify the UNE function, registered at startup (see main.ts), which forgets
// the user and redirects to the login page.
// =========================================================================

export class ErreurApi extends Error {
  constructor(
    public readonly statusCode: number, // 0: the server did not respond
    public readonly cle: string, // translation key: 'ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN'
    public readonly params: Record<string, string> = {},
    public readonly champs: Record<string, string> = {}, // error in each field
  ) {
    super(cle);
    this.name = 'ErreurApi';
  }
}

// The function called for every 401 response (see main.ts)
let surNonAuthentifie: (erreur: ErreurApi) => void = () => {};

export function quandNonAuthentifie(fonction: (erreur: ErreurApi) => void): void {
  surNonAuthentifie = fonction;
}

type Methode = 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'DELETE';

export interface OptionsRequete {
   // public routes (login, CAPTCHA, etc.) and GET /api/auth/moi
   // handle the 401 responses themselves: no automatic redirection
  ignorer401?: boolean;
}

export async function requete<T>(methode: Methode, url: string, corps?: unknown, options: OptionsRequete = {}): Promise<T> {
  let reponse: Response;
  try {
    reponse = await fetch(`/api${url}`, {
      method: methode,
      headers: corps !== undefined ? { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Accept: 'application/json' } : { Accept: 'application/json' },
      body: corps !== undefined ? JSON.stringify(corps) : undefined,
    });
  } catch {
    throw new ErreurApi(0, 'ERRORS.SERVER_UNREACHABLE');
  }

   // read as text and then converted: an empty response, or one that is not
   // JSON (server down: the Vite proxy responds), does not
   // cause the application to crash
  const texte = await reponse.text();
  let donnees: unknown = null;
  try {
    donnees = texte ? JSON.parse(texte) : null;
  } catch {
    donnees = null;
  }

  if (reponse.ok) {
    return donnees as T;
  }

  const e = (donnees ?? {}) as { cle?: string; params?: Record<string, string>; champs?: Record<string, string> };
  const erreur = new ErreurApi(
    reponse.status,
     // no key: it wasn’t our server that responded, but a proxy
     // (Vite: 500 with no body; nginx: 502, 504...)
    e.cle ?? (reponse.status >= 500 ? 'ERRORS.SERVER_UNREACHABLE' : 'ERRORS.SERVER_ERROR'),
    e.params,
    e.champs,
  );
  if (reponse.status === 401 && !options.ignorer401) {
    surNonAuthentifie(erreur);
  }
  throw erreur;
}
  • lines 14–23: a request error: code HTTP, message key, parameters, error for each field;
  • line 27: the function to be called for each 401 response. It does nothing initially; [main.ts] provides one, via [quandNonAuthentifie]. Why not call the router directly here? Because the API access layer should know nothing about the pages: it signals the error, and the application decides;
  • lines 35–39: some requests expect a 401 and handle it themselves: an incorrect password ([POST /api/auth/login] responds with a 401), or the question “who is logged in?” ([GET /api/auth/moi], 401 if no one is logged in). For these, there is no automatic redirection;
  • Line 46: The header [Accept] tells the server the desired response format;
  • line 50: no response at all;
  • line 73: a response without a key does not come from our server: when the JSON server is down, the proxy responds (the one for [Vite] returns a 500 error with no body; a production proxy like [nginx] returns a 502 or 504);
  • lines 77–79: an unexpected 401: we notify the application, then reject the promise as we would for any error.

docs.title: 10.7.3. src/api/rdvmedecins.api.ts
docs.text:
A function per route in API:

// =========================================================================
// api/rdvmedecins.api.ts - one function per route from API
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The client’s “data access layer”: components call these
// functions, which are typed, without knowing anything about URL, fetch, or JSON. If the API
// changes, only this file changes.
// =========================================================================

import { requete } from './client-http';
import type {
  Agenda,
  Captcha,
  DonneesPersonne,
  Inscription,
  ModificationMonCompte,
  MonCompte,
  MonEspace,
  Personne,
  Utilisateur,
} from './types';

// /api/doctors or /api/clients: both are managed the same way
export type TypePersonnes = 'medecins' | 'clients';

type Vide = Record<string, never>;

export const rdvApi = {
   // ------------------------------------------------ login (public routes)
  captcha: () => requete<Captcha>('GET', '/captcha', undefined, { ignorer401: true }),
  moi: () => requete<Utilisateur>('GET', '/auth/moi', undefined, { ignorer401: true }),
  connecter: (login: string, password: string, captchaId: string, captcha: string) =>
    requete<Utilisateur>('POST', '/auth/login', { login, password, captchaId, captcha }, { ignorer401: true }),
  deconnecter: () => requete<Vide>('POST', '/auth/logout', {}, { ignorer401: true }),

   // ------------------------------------------------ account creation (public)
  accesInscription: (captchaId: string, captcha: string) =>
    requete<Vide>('POST', '/inscription/acces', { captchaId, captcha }, { ignorer401: true }),
  etatAccesInscription: () => requete<{ valide: boolean }>('GET', '/inscription/acces', undefined, { ignorer401: true }),
  inscrire: (donnees: Inscription) => requete<{ login: string }>('POST', '/inscription', donnees, { ignorer401: true }),

   // ------------------------------------------------ calendar and appointments
   // idMedecin null: for a logged-in doctor, SON calendar
  agenda: (idMedecin: number | null, jour: string) => {
    const params = new URLSearchParams({ jour });
    if (idMedecin !== null) {
      params.set('idMedecin', String(idMedecin));
    }
    return requete<Agenda>('GET', `/agenda?${params}`);
  },
  reserver: (jour: string, idCreneau: number, idClient: number | null) =>
    requete<{ id: number }>('POST', '/rendez-vous', { jour, idCreneau, idClient: idClient ?? undefined }),
  annulerRv: (idRv: number) => requete<Vide>('DELETE', `/rendez-vous/${idRv}`),

   // ------------------------------------------------ doctors and clients
  lister: (type: TypePersonnes) => requete<Personne[]>('GET', `/${type}`),
  lire: (type: TypePersonnes, id: number) => requete<Personne>('GET', `/${type}/${id}`),
  ajouter: (type: TypePersonnes, donnees: DonneesPersonne) => requete<Personne>('POST', `/${type}`, donnees),
  modifier: (type: TypePersonnes, id: number, donnees: DonneesPersonne) =>
    requete<Personne>('PUT', `/${type}/${id}`, donnees),
  supprimer: (type: TypePersonnes, id: number) => requete<Vide>('DELETE', `/${type}/${id}`),

   // ------------------------------------------------ the patient portal
  monEspace: () => requete<MonEspace>('GET', '/mon-espace'),
  monCompte: () => requete<MonCompte>('GET', '/mon-compte'),
  modifierMonCompte: (donnees: ModificationMonCompte) => requete<Utilisateur>('PUT', '/mon-compte', donnees),
  supprimerMonCompte: (motDePasseActuel: string) => requete<Vide>('DELETE', '/mon-compte', { motDePasseActuel }),
};
  • line 23: doctors and clients are handled the same way; only the address changes: [/api/medecins] or [/api/clients];
  • line 25: the type of an empty object, [{}];
  • Lines 29–33: the connection routes, which handle their own 401 ([ignorer401]);
  • lines 43–49: if no doctor is available, the parameter [idMedecin] is omitted; if a doctor is available, the server returns SON (appointment schedule);
  • lines 50–51: [idClient ?? undefined]: [null] becomes [undefined], and [JSON.stringify] omits the properties of [undefined]: a patient does not send [idClient];
  • lines 55–60: the five operations on individuals, defined by their type;
  • line 66: a DELETE query can also have a body.

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// i18n.ts - French and English
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The dictionaries locales/fr.json and locales/en.json are those from the course
// NestJS (i18n/*.json), supplemented with a few client-specific keys
// (ERRORS.SERVER_UNREACHABLE...). The JSON server returns only CLÉS
// ('ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN'): these are the same as those in the dictionaries.
//
// The selected language is stored in localStorage (a preference, not
// sensitive data); otherwise, the browser’s language is used.
// =========================================================================

import { createI18n } from 'vue-i18n';
import fr from './locales/fr.json';
import en from './locales/en.json';

export type Langue = 'fr' | 'en';
export const LANGUES: Langue[] = ['fr', 'en'];
const CLE_STOCKAGE = 'rdvmedecins.langue';

function langueDeDepart(): Langue {
  try {
    const memorisee = localStorage.getItem(CLE_STOCKAGE);
    if (memorisee === 'fr' || memorisee === 'en') {
      return memorisee;
    }
  } catch {
     // localStorage unavailable (strict private browsing...): too bad
  }
  return navigator.language.toLowerCase().startsWith('en') ? 'en' : 'fr';
}

export const i18n = createI18n({
  legacy: false,
  locale: langueDeDepart(),
  fallbackLocale: 'fr',
  messages: { fr, en },
   // no warning in the console for a key translated by fallback
  fallbackWarn: false,
  missingWarn: false,
});

// change language: the entire application is immediately re-translated
export function changerLangue(langue: Langue): void {
  i18n.global.locale.value = langue;
  document.documentElement.lang = langue;
  try {
    localStorage.setItem(CLE_STOCKAGE, langue);
  } catch {
     // not important
  }
}

document.documentElement.lang = i18n.global.locale.value;
  • lines 21–31: the stored language, otherwise the browser’s language. Access to [localStorage] is protected by [try / catch]: some browsers, in incognito mode, block it;
  • lines 39–40: no warning in the console when a key is missing or comes from the fallback dictionary;
  • lines 44–52: change language: [i18n.global.locale] is the language for the entire application; the page’s [lang] attribute is also updated, and the selection is saved.

docs.title: 10.9.1. src/stores/session.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// stores/session.ts - Is QUI logged in?
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The Pinia store for the session: the logged-in user (or null), and
// is what we infer from this (is it ADMIN? a patient?).
//
// The token JWT itself is not PAS here: it is in a cookie httpOnly that
// is handled only by the browser. The store keeps only the DESCRIPTION from
// the user, returned by the server ({ login, name, role }).
//
// At startup (and after a F5), the store is empty: `verifier()` sends a
// the server, just once, to determine who is connected (GET /api/auth/moi).
// =========================================================================

import { computed, ref } from 'vue';
import { defineStore } from 'pinia';
import { rdvApi } from '../api/rdvmedecins.api';
import type { Role, Utilisateur } from '../api/types';

export const useSessionStore = defineStore('session', () => {
  const utilisateur = ref<Utilisateur | null>(null);
   // Has the question “Who is logged in?” already been asked of the server?
  let verification: Promise<void> | null = null;

  const connecte = computed(() => utilisateur.value !== null);
  const role = computed<Role | null>(() => utilisateur.value?.role ?? null);
  const estAdmin = computed(() => role.value === 'ADMIN');
  const estPatient = computed(() => role.value === 'USER');
   // ADMIN and DOCTOR: schedule and cancel appointments for any patient
  const estGestionnaire = computed(() => role.value === 'ADMIN' || role.value === 'DOCTOR');

   // The home page for each role, immediately after logging in
  const pageAccueil = computed(() => (estPatient.value ? '/mon-espace' : '/agenda'));

   // called by the router guard before CHAQUE navigation; does not query
   // the server only the first time (the connection is maintained and reused)
  function verifier(): Promise<void> {
    verification ??= rdvApi
      .moi()
      .then((u) => {
        utilisateur.value = u;
      })
      .catch(() => {
        utilisateur.value = null; // 401: Unauthorized; or server unreachable
      });
    return verification;
  }

  async function connecter(login: string, password: string, captchaId: string, captcha: string): Promise<void> {
    utilisateur.value = await rdvApi.connecter(login, password, captchaId, captcha);
  }

   // the user has changed their name or login (PUT /api/my-account)
  function mettreAJour(u: Utilisateur): void {
    utilisateur.value = u;
  }

  async function deconnecter(): Promise<void> {
    try {
      await rdvApi.deconnecter();
    } finally {
      oublier();
    }
  }

   // without making a request to the server: session expired, account deleted
  function oublier(): void {
    utilisateur.value = null;
  }

  return {
    utilisateur,
    connecte,
    role,
    estAdmin,
    estPatient,
    estGestionnaire,
    pageAccueil,
    verifier,
    connecter,
    mettreAJour,
    deconnecter,
    oublier,
  };
});
  • Line 21: the logged-in user, as described by the server. The token itself isn’t there—it’s in a cookie that only the browser handles;
  • lines 25–30: what is inferred from this, used by the pages and the navigation bar;
  • line 33: the home page for each role: “My Space” for a patient, the calendar for others;
  • lines 37–47: the question “Who is logged in?”, asked of the server only PREMIÈRE times. The promise is kept in [verification]: subsequent calls reuse it (the operator [??=] only assigns a value if the variable is [null] or [undefined]). It cannot fail: an error (401, server unreachable) means “no one”;
  • lines 49–51: the login. If it fails, [rdvApi.connecter] rejects its promise with a [ErreurApi], which passes through this function to the login page;
  • line 54: After making changes to their account, the patient may have changed their name;
  • lines 58–64: [finally]: the user is forgotten, even if the server did not respond;
  • line 67: without making any request to the server (session expired, account deleted).

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// stores/messages.ts - messages displayed to the user
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Same layout as the HTML application:
//    - a SUCCÈS is displayed as HAUT on the page (green banner);
//    - a ERREUR appears as BAS, on a light pink background (the “sticky” area).
// A message is a translation CLÉ (plus its settings): it is therefore re-translated
// on its own if the user changes the language.
//
// "Flash" messages: an action that ends with a page change
// page (booking, adding a doctor, etc.) places its message using flash();
// it will be displayed on the page SUIVANTE, then disappear upon navigation
// (see router.afterEach in router.ts). On the server side, this was the
// role of the short-lived cookie "rdvmedecins_flash".
// =========================================================================

import { ref } from 'vue';
import { defineStore } from 'pinia';
import { ErreurApi } from '../api/client-http';

export interface Message {
  cle: string;
  params?: Record<string, string>;
}

export const useMessagesStore = defineStore('messages', () => {
  const succes = ref<Message | null>(null);
  const erreur = ref<Message | null>(null);
   // the messages to be displayed on the next page
  let enAttente: { succes: Message | null; erreur: Message | null } | null = null;

  function afficherSucces(cle: string, params?: Record<string, string>): void {
    succes.value = { cle, params };
    erreur.value = null;
  }

  function afficherErreur(cle: string, params?: Record<string, string>): void {
    erreur.value = { cle, params };
    succes.value = null;
  }

   // a ErreurApi -> the page message; any other error is a
   // client-side issue, which is logged (browser console)
  function afficherErreurApi(e: unknown): void {
    if (!(e instanceof ErreurApi)) {
      throw e;
    }
    afficherErreur(e.cle, e.params);
  }

  function effacer(): void {
    succes.value = null;
    erreur.value = null;
  }

   // for the page SUIVANTE
  function flash(type: 'succes' | 'erreur', cle: string, params?: Record<string, string>): void {
    enAttente ??= { succes: null, erreur: null };
    enAttente[type] = { cle, params };
  }

   // called after each page view (router.afterEach)
  function nouvellePage(): void {
    succes.value = enAttente?.succes ?? null;
    erreur.value = enAttente?.erreur ?? null;
    enAttente = null;
  }

  return { succes, erreur, afficherSucces, afficherErreur, afficherErreurApi, effacer, flash, nouvellePage };
});
  • lines 21–24: A message consists of a translation CLÉ and its parameters. It therefore automatically translates itself if the user changes languages;
  • lines 27–28: the success message (displayed at the top) and the error message (at the bottom) for the current page;
  • lines 44–49: a [ErreurApi] becomes the page’s message. Any other error is a CLIENT anomaly (a programming error): it is allowed to be logged and will be displayed in the browser console;
  • lines 57–60: a message for the SUIVANTE page. An action that results in a page change (booking, adding a doctor, logging in after creating an account) displays this message before navigating to the next page;
  • lines 63–67: called after each page navigation (see [router.ts]): messages from the previous page disappear, and pending messages appear. In the HTML application, this was the role of the short-lived cookie [rdvmedecins_flash].

docs.title: 10.10.1. src/composables/useConfirmation.ts
docs.text:
The composable from Example 12, with three differences:

// =========================================================================
// composables/useConfirmation.ts - “Are you sure?”
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Taken from Example 12: confirm(key) opens the confirmation window
// (components/FenetreConfirmation.vue, placed once in App.vue) and
// returns a promise resolved to true (Yes) or false (No). The message is
// a translation CLÉ: the window translates it into the current language.
//
//      if (await confirm('AGENDA.CANCEL_CONFIRM')) { ... }
// =========================================================================

import { readonly, ref } from 'vue';
import { useMessagesStore } from '../stores/messages';

const cleMessage = ref<string | null>(null); // null: window closed
let repondre: ((oui: boolean) => void) | null = null;

export function useConfirmation() {
  function confirmer(cle: string): Promise<boolean> {
    repondre?.(false); // Is there still an open question? It defaults to "no"
     // a new question: the messages from the previous action are out of date
    useMessagesStore().effacer();
    cleMessage.value = cle;
    return new Promise<boolean>((resolve) => {
      repondre = resolve;
    });
  }

  function reponse(oui: boolean): void {
    cleMessage.value = null;
    const r = repondre;
    repondre = null;
    r?.(oui);
  }

  return { cleMessage: readonly(cleMessage), confirmer, reponse };
}
  • line 19: the message is a translation CLÉ: the window translates it into the current language;
  • line 20: an open question (unlikely scenario) receives the answer “no”;
  • line 22: a new question renders the messages from the previous action obsolete.

docs.title: 10.10.2. src/composables/useFormatage.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// composables/useFormatage.ts - display of people, times, and days
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The server sends data BRUTES (start_hour: 8, start_minute: 0; day:
// "2026-10-05"); the formatting, which depends on the language, is the responsibility
// the client. jourLong() uses the current language from view-i18n.
// =========================================================================

import { useI18n } from 'vue-i18n';
import type { Creneau, Identite } from '../api/types';

// "Ms. Alice DURAND"
export function libelle(p: Identite): string {
  return `${p.titre} ${p.prenom} ${p.nom}`;
}

// "8:05" rather than "8:5"
export function heure(h: number, m: number): string {
  return `${h}:${String(m).padStart(2, '0')}`;
}

// "8:00 - 8:20"
export function horaire(c: Creneau): string {
  return `${heure(c.hdebut, c.mdebut)} - ${heure(c.hfin, c.mfin)}`;
}

// today’s date, in the "yyyy-MM-dd" format (the same as <input type="date"> and API)
export function aujourdhui(): string {
  const d = new Date();
  return `${d.getFullYear()}-${String(d.getMonth() + 1).padStart(2, '0')}-${String(d.getDate()).padStart(2, '0')}`;
}

// true if [jour] is a valid date in the yyyy-MM-dd format
export function estUneDateValide(jour: unknown): jour is string {
  if (typeof jour !== 'string' || !/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(jour)) {
    return false;
  }
  const date = new Date(`${jour}T00:00:00Z`);
  return !isNaN(date.getTime()) && date.toISOString().slice(0, 10) === jour;
}

export function useFormatage() {
  const { locale } = useI18n();

   // "Monday, October 5, 2026" / "Monday 5 October 2026"
  function jourLong(jour: string): string {
    return new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale.value === 'en' ? 'en-GB' : 'fr-FR', {
      dateStyle: 'full',
      timeZone: 'UTC', // "2026-10-05T00:00:00Z" must remain 5, regardless of the time zone
    }).format(new Date(`${jour}T00:00:00Z`));
  }

  return { libelle, heure, horaire, jourLong };
}

The server sends raw data ([hdebut: 8, mdebut: 0], [jour: "2026-10-05"]); formatting this data, which depends on the language, is the client’s responsibility:

  • lines 13–39: ordinary, non-reactive functions, exported one by one;
  • lines 42–54: a composable, because [jourLong] requires the language COURANTE, which it obtains via [useI18n()]. When the language changes, a template that displays [jourLong(...)] is recalculated;
  • line 49: [new Date("2026-10-05T00:00:00Z")] is midnight UTC; displayed in the Paris time zone, it would still be October 5, but in New York, it would be October 4! We therefore request a display in the UTC time zone.

docs.title: 10.10.3. src/composables/useFormulaire.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// composables/useFormulaire.ts - errors in a form sent to the server
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// All forms in the application follow the same pattern as
// Example 20: no rules are checked in the browser (they
// are handled in UN one place only—the server), and in case of rejection:
//    - the error for each field (ErreurApi.champs) is displayed below the field,
//      outlined in red;
//    - the general message (ErreurApi.cle) is displayed at the bottom of the page.
// This composable combines this status and these actions.
// =========================================================================

import { ref } from 'vue';
import { ErreurApi } from '../api/client-http';
import { useMessagesStore } from '../stores/messages';

export function useFormulaire() {
  const messages = useMessagesStore();
  const erreurs = ref<Record<string, string>>({}); // field -> message key
  const params = ref<Record<string, string>>({}); // message parameters ({min}...)
  const envoiEnCours = ref(false);

  function effacerErreurs(): void {
    erreurs.value = {};
    params.value = {};
  }

   // executes the send; returns true if successful. In case of ErreurApi, the
   // errors are displayed and false is returned.
  async function envoyer(action: () => Promise<void>): Promise<boolean> {
    effacerErreurs();
    envoiEnCours.value = true;
    try {
      await action();
      return true;
    } catch (e) {
      if (e instanceof ErreurApi) {
        erreurs.value = e.champs;
        params.value = e.params;
      }
      messages.afficherErreurApi(e);
      return false;
    } finally {
      envoiEnCours.value = false;
    }
  }

  return { erreurs, params, envoiEnCours, envoyer, effacerErreurs };
}

All forms in the application follow the approach shown in Example 20: no rules are validated in the browser; the server validates everything, and any errors are displayed below the fields. This composable groups together the state and common actions:

  • lines 19–21: the error for each field, the message parameters, and a submission indicator (the button is disabled during submission to prevent double-clicking);
  • lines 30–46: executes the submission (a function provided by the page); if [ErreurApi] occurs, clears the field errors, displays the general message at the bottom of the page, and returns [false].

docs.title: 10.11. The router
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// router.ts - the application’s pages and their access permissions
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The MÊMES URLs that the application HTML (/login, /agenda, /doctors,
// /my-space...), but these are now routes in the CLIENT:
// createWebHistory generates “clean” URLs without the # symbol. The browser
// only sends a request to the server for the very first page; after that,
// the router changes the address and the displayed component.
//
// The flip side of the coin: if the user reloads /agenda (F5), the
// browser does indeed request /agenda from the server, which must then
// return index.html (This is easily done in development; in production, see
// web/client-spa.ts from the server JSON).
//
// Each route carries metadata (meta):
//    - titl  e: translation key for the tab title;
//    - publi c: accessible without being logged in;
//    - role  s : authorized roles (none = all logged-in roles);
//    - typ   e : 'doctors' or 'clients' for pages shared by both.
//
// RAPPEL: these controls are simply a CONFORT (do not display a page
// unnecessary). Data protection is ensured by the server, which
// verifies the token and role for the CHAQUE request.
// =========================================================================

import { createRouter, createWebHistory } from 'vue-router';
import type { Role } from './api/types';
import type { TypePersonnes } from './api/rdvmedecins.api';
import { i18n } from './i18n';
import { useSessionStore } from './stores/session';
import { useMessagesStore } from './stores/messages';
import { rdvApi } from './api/rdvmedecins.api';
import ConnexionView from './views/ConnexionView.vue';
import AgendaView from './views/AgendaView.vue';

declare module 'vue-router' {
  interface RouteMeta {
    titre: string;
    public?: boolean;
    roles?: Role[];
    type?: TypePersonnes;
  }
}

// the management routes for doctors ET and clients (ADMIN), following the same model
function routesPersonnes(type: TypePersonnes, titre: string, titreAjout: string, titreModif: string) {
  const roles: Role[] = ['ADMIN'];
  return [
    { path: `/${type}`, name: type, component: () => import('./views/PersonnesView.vue'), meta: { titre, roles, type } },
    {
      path: `/${type}/ajouter`,
      name: `${type}-ajouter`,
      component: () => import('./views/PersonneFormulaireView.vue'),
      meta: { titre: titreAjout, roles, type },
    },
    {
      path: `/${type}/:id(\\d+)/modifier`, // (\\d+): the ID must be a number
      name: `${type}-modifier`,
      component: () => import('./views/PersonneFormulaireView.vue'),
      props: (route: { params: { id?: string | string[] } }) => ({ id: Number(route.params.id) }),
      meta: { titre: titreModif, roles, type },
    },
  ];
}

export const router = createRouter({
  history: createWebHistory(),
  routes: [
     // "/": to /login, which in turn redirects to the role’s home page if the user is logged in
    { path: '/', redirect: '/login' },
    { path: '/login', name: 'login', component: ConnexionView, meta: { titre: 'LOGIN.TITLE', public: true } },
    { path: '/agenda', name: 'agenda', component: AgendaView, meta: { titre: 'AGENDA.PAGE_TITLE' } },
    ...routesPersonnes('medecins', 'MEDECINS.TITLE', 'MEDECINS.ADD', 'MEDECINS.EDIT'),
    ...routesPersonnes('clients', 'CLIENTS.TITLE', 'CLIENTS.ADD', 'CLIENTS.EDIT'),
    {
      path: '/inscription',
      name: 'inscription',
      component: () => import('./views/InscriptionView.vue'),
      meta: { titre: 'INSCRIPTION.TITLE', public: true },
       // a PROPRE token for the route: without a passcode (CAPTCHA solved on the
       // login page), return to the login page
      beforeEnter: async () => {
        const { valide } = await rdvApi.etatAccesInscription().catch(() => ({ valide: false }));
        if (!valide) {
          useMessagesStore().flash('erreur', 'ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT');
          return { name: 'login' };
        }
        return true;
      },
    },
    {
      path: '/mon-espace',
      name: 'mon-espace',
      component: () => import('./views/EspacePatientView.vue'),
      meta: { titre: 'ESPACE.TITLE', roles: ['USER'] },
    },
    {
      path: '/mon-compte',
      name: 'mon-compte',
      component: () => import('./views/MonCompteView.vue'),
      meta: { titre: 'MON_COMPTE.TITLE', roles: ['USER'] },
    },
    {
      path: '/interdit',
      name: 'interdit',
      component: () => import('./views/ErreurView.vue'),
      props: { code: 403 },
      meta: { titre: 'ERROR_PAGE.TITLE' },
    },
    {
      path: '/:pathMatch(.*)*',
      name: 'introuvable',
      component: () => import('./views/ErreurView.vue'),
      props: { code: 404 },
      meta: { titre: 'ERROR_PAGE.TITLE', public: true },
    },
  ],
});

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// the guard GLOBAL, before each navigation
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
router.beforeEach(async (vers) => {
  const session = useSessionStore();
   // the first time (startup, F5): the server is asked who is logged in
  await session.verifier();

  if (vers.meta.public) {
     // already logged in: the login page is no longer needed
    if (vers.name === 'login' && session.connecte) {
      return session.pageAccueil;
    }
    return true;
  }
  if (!session.connecte) {
     // the requested page is cached to return to it after logging in
    return { name: 'login', query: { redirect: vers.fullPath } };
  }
  if (vers.meta.roles && !vers.meta.roles.includes(session.role!)) {
    return { name: 'interdit' };
  }
  return true;
});

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// After each navigation: "flash" messages, tab title
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
router.afterEach((vers, depuis) => {
   // A navigation that changes only the query (/agenda?...) remains a
   // new “page”: as with the HTML app, the messages from the
   // previous page disappear, and the flash messages appear
  if (vers.fullPath !== depuis.fullPath) {
    useMessagesStore().nouvellePage();
  }
  document.title = `${i18n.global.t(vers.meta.titre)} - ${i18n.global.t('APP.TITLE')}`;
});
  • lines 36–43: metadata for our routes: the tab title (a translation key), public access, authorized roles, and user type;
  • Lines 46–64: the three doctor management routes (list, add, edit), and the same three for clients, generated by a function. The pages are loaded on demand ([() => import(...)]): a patient will never download the doctor management code;
  • Line 57: [(\d+)]: A regular expression restricts the parameter [id] to numbers. [/medecins/abc/modifier] does not match this route: the “page not found” page is displayed;
  • line 60: the component’s [id] property, converted to a number;
  • line 67: “clean” addresses, without [#];
  • line 70: the address [/] leads to [/login], which in turn leads to the role’s home page when logged in;
  • lines 82–89: a PROPRE guard on a route, executed before entering it: without a pass (captcha solved on the login page), account creation redirects to the login page with a message;
  • line 107: [props] can also be a static object: the same error page is used for 403 and 404 errors;
  • Lines 123–143: The guard GLOBAL, before each navigation:
    • [await session.verifier()]: The first time (on startup, F5), the server is queried to determine who is logged in. The guard is [async]: navigation waits for the response;
    • a public page is always accessible; however, the login page, for a logged-in user, redirects to their home page;
    • not logged in: login page, while retaining the requested page;
    • invalid role: 403 page;
  • lines 148–156: after each navigation: the messages flash, and the tab title is translated. [i18n.global.t]: outside a component, the [i18n] object is used directly.

  titre, menus selon le rôle, FR / EN, rôle, nom, déconnexion.
  "Médecins" et "Clients" n'apparaissent que pour l'ADMIN : un simple
  confort d'affichage, la vraie protection étant celle du serveur.
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { RouterLink, useRouter } from 'vue-router';
import { useI18n } from 'vue-i18n';
import { useSessionStore } from '../stores/session';
import { changerLangue, LANGUES } from '../i18n';

const { t, locale } = useI18n();
const session = useSessionStore();
const router = useRouter();

async function seDeconnecter(): Promise<void> {
  await session.deconnecter().catch(() => {}); // even if the server does not respond
  router.push({ name: 'login' });
}
</script>

<template>
  <nav class="navbar navbar-expand-sm navbar-dark bg-primary rounded mb-4 px-3">
    <span class="navbar-brand mb-0">{{ t('APP.TITLE') }}</span>

    <ul v-if="session.connecte" class="navbar-nav me-auto">
      <li v-if="session.estPatient" class="nav-item">
         <!-- active-class: the Bootstrap class of the menu on the displayed page -->
        <RouterLink class="nav-link" active-class="active" to="/mon-espace">{{ t('APP.MENU_MY_SPACE') }}</RouterLink>
      </li>
      <li class="nav-item">
        <RouterLink class="nav-link" active-class="active" to="/agenda">{{ t('APP.MENU_AGENDA') }}</RouterLink>
      </li>
      <template v-if="session.estAdmin">
        <li class="nav-item">
          <RouterLink class="nav-link" active-class="active" to="/medecins">{{ t('APP.MENU_DOCTORS') }}</RouterLink>
        </li>
        <li class="nav-item">
          <RouterLink class="nav-link" active-class="active" to="/clients">{{ t('APP.MENU_PATIENTS') }}</RouterLink>
        </li>
      </template>
    </ul>
    <div v-else class="me-auto"></div>

    <div class="d-flex align-items-center gap-2">
       <!-- FR / EN: no request to the server; the page is re-translated locally -->
      <div class="btn-group btn-group-sm" role="group" :aria-label="t('APP.LANGUAGE')">
        <button
          v-for="l in LANGUES"
          :key="l"
          type="button"
          class="btn"
          :class="locale === l ? 'btn-light' : 'btn-outline-light'"
          :aria-pressed="locale === l"
          @click="changerLangue(l)"
        >
          {{ l.toUpperCase() }}
        </button>
      </div>

      <template v-if="session.utilisateur">
        <span class="badge text-bg-light text-primary">{{ session.utilisateur.role }}</span>
        <span class="text-white">{{ session.utilisateur.nom }}</span>
        <button type="button" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-light" @click="seDeconnecter">{{ t('APP.LOGOUT') }}</button>
      </template>
    </div>
  </nav>
</template>
  • lines 21–24: logout, followed by the login page. [.catch(() => {})]: even if the server does not respond, the client disconnects;
  • line 31: the menus only appear once logged in, depending on the role: “My Account” for a patient, “Doctors” and “Clients” for the ADMIN. This is simply for display convenience; true security is provided by the server;
  • line 34: the menu on the displayed page is assigned the class [active];
  • lines 53–63: the FR / EN buttons. [:aria-pressed] indicates to screen readers which button is pressed;
  • line 66: the role, the name, and the logout function.

docs.title: 10.12.2. src/components/MessageSucces.vue and ZoneErreur.vue
