docs.title: 8. Communicating with the server
docs.text: The examples in this chapter query the server JSON [RdvMedecins]: It must be running ([npm run start:dev] in the [rdvmedecins-nestjs-json] folder) on port 8080, at the same time as the [Vite] server used in the examples, on port 5173.

docs.title: 8.1.1. The Vite proxy
docs.text:
The example page comes from http://localhost:5173 (the [Vite] server); API is located at http://localhost:8080. To a browser, these are two different origins (the port is part of the origin). However, for security reasons, a browser does not allow a page to read responses from another origin unless the server explicitly permits it (the mechanism known as CORS). And [fetch] does not send cookies (and therefore not the token) to another origin unless asked to do so ([credentials: 'include']) ET that the server accepts it, again via CORS.

Rather than opening the server to other origins, we route requests from API through the Vite server. This is the proxy declared in [vite.config.ts]:

server: {
  port: 5173,
  proxy: {
     '/api': 'http://localhost:8080',
  },
},

The browser sends [GET http://localhost:5173/api/captcha]; [Vite] forwards the request to [http://localhost:8080/api/captcha], then sends the response back to the browser. From the browser’s perspective, the page and API have the same origin:

In production, there will no longer be a [Vite]: the JSON server itself will serve the compiled client files (see the “Deployment” chapter). The page and API will still share the same origin.

docs.title: 8.1.2. The request
docs.text:
<!--
  =========================================================================
  17-fetch/src/App.vue - une première requête HTTP vers le serveur
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Le serveur JSON RdvMedecins doit être lancé (port 8080). On lui demande
  un captcha : GET /api/captcha -> { "id": "...", "svg": "<svg ...>" }.

    - fetch(url) : la fonction du navigateur qui envoie une requête HTTP.
      Elle renvoie une PROMESSE : on attend la réponse avec await ;
    - reponse.ok : vrai pour un code 2xx ; reponse.json() lit le corps
      JSON (encore une promesse) ;
    - l'adresse est RELATIVE (/api/captcha) : la requête part vers le
      serveur de la page, Vite (port 5173), qui la transmet au serveur JSON
      (port 8080) grâce à son proxy (cf. vite.config.ts) ;
    - trois états à afficher : en cours, réussi, en erreur.
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { onMounted, ref } from 'vue';

// what GET returns for /api/captcha
interface Captcha {
  id: string;
  svg: string;
}

const captcha = ref<Captcha | null>(null);
const enCours = ref(false);
const erreur = ref<string | null>(null);
const nbRequetes = ref(0);

async function charger(): Promise<void> {
  enCours.value = true;
  erreur.value = null;
  try {
    const reponse = await fetch('/api/captcha');
    nbRequetes.value++;
    if (!reponse.ok) {
       // the server responded, but with an error (4xx, 5xx) — or is it
       // Vite returns a 502/504 because the server JSON is down
      throw new Error(`le serveur a répondu ${reponse.status} ${reponse.statusText}`);
    }
    captcha.value = (await reponse.json()) as Captcha;
  } catch (e) {
     // fetch itself fails when no response is received (network down...)
    erreur.value = e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e);
    captcha.value = null;
  } finally {
    enCours.value = false;
  }
}

// On the first page load, a CAPTCHA is loaded
onMounted(charger);
</script>

<template>
  <div class="container py-4" style="max-width: 640px">
    <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Exemple 17 - une première requête HTTP</h1>
    <div class="card p-3">
      <p v-if="enCours" class="text-muted">Chargement...</p>
      <div v-else-if="erreur" class="alert alert-danger mb-3">
        Impossible d'obtenir un captcha : {{ erreur }}.<br>
        Le serveur JSON RdvMedecins est-il lancé (port 8080) ?
      </div>
      <template v-else-if="captcha">
         <!-- v-html: inserts a string like HTML (here, the image SVG).
             À n'utiliser QUE pour un contenu sûr : ce SVG est fabriqué par
             NOTRE serveur. Avec une saisie d'utilisateur, v-html ouvrirait
             la porte à l'injection de scripts ({{ }} échappe, lui, tout). -->
        <div class="captcha mb-2" v-html="captcha.svg"></div>
        <p class="small text-muted">id : <code>{{ captcha.id }}</code></p>
      </template>
      <button class="btn btn-primary align-self-start" :disabled="enCours" @click="charger">Autre image</button>
      <p class="small text-muted mt-2 mb-0">{{ nbRequetes }} requête(s) réussie(s) - ouvrez l'onglet Réseau des outils de développement (F12).</p>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
/* :deep(svg): the rule matches the <svg> inserted by v-html, which "scoped" would otherwise ignore */
.captcha :deep(svg) {
  border: 1px solid #dee2e6;
  border-radius: 0.375rem;
}
</style>
  • line 22: the format of the response from [GET /api/captcha];
  • lines 27–29: the three states of a request: in progress, successful (the CAPTCHA), and error;
  • line 36: [fetch(url)], the browser function that sends a request HTTP. It returns a response promise; [await] suspends the function [async] until the promise resolves, without blocking the page. The address is relative: the request is sent to the page’s server, [Vite], which forwards it;
  • Line 38: [fetch] does not report an error for PAS when the server returns a 404 or 500 response: it did receive a response. It is up to us to test [reponse.ok] (true for a 2xx code). If the JSON server is down, [Vite] responds with a 5xx error;
  • line 43: [reponse.json()] reads the body and converts it into an object (yet another promise). [as Captcha] informs [TypeScript] of the object’s format: the compiler cannot verify what the server will send;
  • line 44: [fetch] itself fails when no response is received (network down);
  • line 48: in any case, the request is no longer in progress;
  • line 54: on the first display, a CAPTCHA is loaded;
  • line 71: [v-html] inserts a string like HTML (here, the image SVG). Do not use QUE for secure content: this SVG is generated by the NOTRE server. With user-entered data, [v-html] could allow scripts to be injected into the page; the [{{ }}] tokens, on the other hand, bypass everything;
  • Line 82: [:deep(...)]: A [scoped] rule normally only affects elements in the template; the [<svg>] inserted by [v-html] is not part of it.

In the browser’s developer tools (F12), the Network tab shows the request [captcha], sent to [localhost:5173], and its response JSON.

docs.title: 8.2. Example 18: Login, Cookie, and Session
docs.text:
<!--
  =========================================================================
  18-connexion/src/App.vue - se connecter au serveur RdvMedecins
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    1. au démarrage : GET /api/auth/moi - sommes-nous déjà connectés ?
       (après un F5, le client a tout oublié ; le serveur, lui, lit le cookie) ;
    2. connexion : POST /api/auth/login, corps JSON { login, password,
       captchaId, captcha }. En cas de succès, le serveur dépose le cookie
       httpOnly du jeton JWT : notre code ne le voit JAMAIS (essayez
       document.cookie dans la console : il n'y est pas) ;
    3. requête protégée : GET /api/medecins. Le navigateur y joint le cookie
       tout seul (même origine) ;
    4. déconnexion : POST /api/auth/logout - le serveur efface le cookie.

  Un cookie appartient à une machine (localhost) et à un chemin (/api) : il
  est donc commun à TOUS les exemples. Une fois connecté ici, les exemples 19 et 20
  le sont aussi.
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { onMounted, reactive, ref } from 'vue';

interface Utilisateur {
  login: string;
  nom: string;
  role: 'ADMIN' | 'DOCTOR' | 'USER';
}
interface Medecin {
  id: number;
  titre: string;
  prenom: string;
  nom: string;
}
// the form of TOUTES the errors in API
interface ErreurApi {
  statusCode: number;
  cle: string;
  params?: Record<string, string>;
}

// the few messages this example needs (Example 20 will use vue-i18n)
const MESSAGES: Record<string, string> = {
  'LOGIN.ERROR': 'Login ou mot de passe incorrect.',
  'ERRORS.WRONG_CAPTCHA': "Les caractères recopiés ne correspondent pas à l'image.",
  'ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS': 'Trop de tentatives infructueuses. Réessayez plus tard.',
};

const utilisateur = ref<Utilisateur | null>(null);
const medecins = ref<Medecin[]>([]);
const captcha = ref<{ id: string; svg: string } | null>(null);
const saisie = reactive({ login: 'admin', password: '', captcha: '' });
const erreur = ref<string | null>(null);
const pret = ref(false); // Is the initial verification complete?

async function chargerCaptcha(): Promise<void> {
  captcha.value = await (await fetch('/api/captcha')).json();
  saisie.captcha = '';
}

// 1. Who is logged in? 200 -> the user; 401 -> no one
async function verifierSession(): Promise<void> {
  const reponse = await fetch('/api/auth/moi');
  if (reponse.ok) {
    utilisateur.value = await reponse.json();
    await chargerMedecins();
  } else {
    await chargerCaptcha();
  }
  pret.value = true;
}

// 2. The login
async function seConnecter(): Promise<void> {
  erreur.value = null;
  const reponse = await fetch('/api/auth/login', {
    method: 'POST',
     // The server rejects (415) a POST that is not in JSON
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      login: saisie.login,
      password: saisie.password,
      captchaId: captcha.value?.id,
      captcha: saisie.captcha,
    }),
  });
  if (reponse.ok) {
    utilisateur.value = await reponse.json();
    saisie.password = '';
    await chargerMedecins();
    return;
  }
   // An error: the JSON body specifies which one; each image is served only once
  const e = (await reponse.json()) as ErreurApi;
  erreur.value = `${reponse.status} - ${MESSAGES[e.cle] ?? e.cle}`;
  await chargerCaptcha();
}

// 3. A protected request
async function chargerMedecins(): Promise<void> {
  const reponse = await fetch('/api/medecins');
  medecins.value = reponse.ok ? await reponse.json() : [];
}

// 4. Logout
async function seDeconnecter(): Promise<void> {
  await fetch('/api/auth/logout', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: '{}' });
  utilisateur.value = null;
  medecins.value = [];
  await chargerCaptcha();
}

onMounted(() => {
  verifierSession().catch(() => {
    erreur.value = 'Le serveur JSON RdvMedecins est-il lancé (port 8080) ?';
    pret.value = true;
  });
});
</script>

<template>
  <div class="container py-4" style="max-width: 640px">
    <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Exemple 18 - connexion au serveur</h1>
    <p v-if="!pret" class="text-muted">Vérification de la session...</p>

     <!-- logged in -->
    <div v-else-if="utilisateur" class="card p-3">
      <p>Connecté : <strong>{{ utilisateur.nom }}</strong> ({{ utilisateur.login }}),
        rôle <span class="badge text-bg-primary">{{ utilisateur.role }}</span></p>
      <h2 class="h6">GET /api/medecins</h2>
      <ul>
        <li v-for="m in medecins" :key="m.id">{{ m.titre }} {{ m.prenom }} {{ m.nom }}</li>
      </ul>
      <p class="small text-muted">Rechargez la page (F5) : vous restez connecté.</p>
      <button class="btn btn-outline-secondary align-self-start" @click="seDeconnecter">Se déconnecter</button>
    </div>

     <!-- not logged in: the form -->
    <form v-else class="card p-3" @submit.prevent="seConnecter">
      <div class="mb-2">
        <label class="form-label" for="login">Login</label>
        <input id="login" v-model="saisie.login" class="form-control" autocomplete="username">
      </div>
      <div class="mb-2">
        <label class="form-label" for="password">Mot de passe</label>
        <input id="password" v-model="saisie.password" type="password" class="form-control" autocomplete="current-password">
      </div>
      <div class="mb-3">
        <label class="form-label" for="captcha">Recopiez les caractères de l'image</label>
        <div class="d-flex align-items-center gap-3 mb-2">
          <div v-if="captcha" v-html="captcha.svg"></div>
          <a href="#" class="small" @click.prevent="chargerCaptcha">Autre image</a>
        </div>
        <input id="captcha" v-model="saisie.captcha" class="form-control" autocomplete="off">
      </div>
      <button class="btn btn-primary">Se connecter</button>
      <p class="small text-muted mt-2 mb-0">Comptes : admin, pelissier, martin... (mot de passe = login).</p>
    </form>

    <div v-if="erreur" class="alert alert-danger mt-3">{{ erreur }}</div>
  </div>
</template>
  • line 35: the format of all errors in API;
  • line 42: the few messages required by this example, in French; Example 20 will use [vue-i18n];
  • Lines 61–69: On startup, [GET /api/auth/moi]: Are we already logged in? After reloading the page (F5), the [Vue.js] application has forgotten everything; the server, however, reads the cookie. 200: the user; 401: no one;
  • lines 73–96: the connection:
    • line 76: [fetch(url, options)]: the method, headers, and body;
    • line 78: the server rejects a POST that is not in JSON format;
    • line 79: the body, converted to JSON text;
    • line 87: if successful, the server has set the token cookie. Our code does not see it JAMAIS: type [document.cookie] into the browser console; it is not there ([HttpOnly]);
    • line 93: if the request fails, the body explains why. We display the message and request a new image: each image is used only once;
  • lines 99–102: a protected request. We don’t need to do anything to authenticate: the browser automatically includes the cookie because the request is going to the same origin as the page (by default, [fetch] sends cookies with same-origin requests);
  • lines 105–110: logout—the server deletes the cookie. The body ['{}'] is included so that the request is a POST JSON.

The login form:

With an incorrectly entered CAPTCHA (the server is in test mode: any CAPTCHA accepts the response [test]):

Logged in:

Reload the page (F5): you remain logged in. Next, open Example 19: you’re logged in there as well. A cookie belongs to a machine (here, [localhost]) and a path (here, [/api]), which are common to all examples.

docs.title: 8.3. Example 19: An Access Layer for API
docs.text:
Example 18 repeated the same steps with every call to [fetch]: the prefix [/api], the header [Content-Type], [JSON.stringify], the test for [reponse.ok], and reading the error body. We group them into a single function, in the [commun] folder (shared by examples 19 and 20):

// =========================================================================
// shared/api.ts - UNE function for all requests to API
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// In Example 18, each call to `fetch` repeated the same steps:
// /api prefix, Content-Type header, JSON.stringify, reponse.ok test,
// reading the error body... We’ll group them together here, once and for all:
//
//    const doctors = await api.get<Doctor[]>('/doctors');
//    await api.post('/appointments', { day, idCreneau, idClient });
//
//    - if successful, the promise returns the body JSON, TYPÉ;
//    - if the operation fails, it is REJETÉE with a ErreurApi, which contains the
//      translation key sent by the server (and, if any, its
//      parameters and the error for each field).
// Used in Examples 19 and 20; the case study follows the same principle.
// =========================================================================

export class ErreurApi extends Error {
  constructor(
    public readonly statusCode: number, // 0: the server did not respond
    public readonly cle: string, // e.g., 'ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN'
    public readonly params: Record<string, string> = {},
    public readonly champs: Record<string, string> = {},
  ) {
    super(cle);
    this.name = 'ErreurApi';
  }
}

type Methode = 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'DELETE';

export async function requete<T>(methode: Methode, url: string, corps?: unknown): Promise<T> {
  let reponse: Response;
  try {
    reponse = await fetch(`/api${url}`, {
      method: methode,
       // a body -> from JSON (the server rejects POST, which is not a body)
      headers: corps !== undefined ? { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } : {},
      body: corps !== undefined ? JSON.stringify(corps) : undefined,
    });
  } catch {
     // no response (network down...)
    throw new ErreurApi(0, 'ERRORS.SERVER_UNREACHABLE');
  }

   // the body is read as text and then converted: an empty response, or
   // which is not JSON (JSON server is down: Vite is responding instead),
   // should not cause the application to crash
  const texte = await reponse.text();
  let donnees: unknown = null;
  try {
    donnees = texte ? JSON.parse(texte) : null;
  } catch {
    donnees = null;
  }

  if (!reponse.ok) {
    const e = (donnees ?? {}) as { cle?: string; params?: Record<string, string>; champs?: Record<string, string> };
    throw new ErreurApi(reponse.status, e.cle ?? 'ERRORS.SERVER_UNREACHABLE', e.params, e.champs);
  }
  return donnees as T;
}

// shortcuts, which are more readable in practice
export const api = {
  get: <T>(url: string) => requete<T>('GET', url),
  post: <T>(url: string, corps: unknown = {}) => requete<T>('POST', url, corps),
  put: <T>(url: string, corps: unknown) => requete<T>('PUT', url, corps),
  delete: <T>(url: string, corps?: unknown) => requete<T>('DELETE', url, corps),
};
  • Lines 18–27: An error class that contains the server’s response: the code HTTP, the message key, its parameters, and the error for each field. The code 0 means “no response”;
  • line 32: a generic function: [T] is the type of the body expected in case of success. [requete<Personne[]>('GET', '/medecins')] returns a [Promise<Personne[]>];
  • line 38: a body, and only in this case, accompanied by the header JSON;
  • lines 49–55: the body is read as text and then converted. An empty response, or one that is not JSON (server down: [Vite] responds with text), should not cause the application to crash;
  • lines 57–60: a failure results in a [ErreurApi]: the promise returned by [requete] is rejected. The calling code catches this via [try / catch];
  • lines 65–70: shorthand, more readable: [api.get<T>(url)], [api.post<T>(url, corps)]... [api.post] sends the body [{}] by default.

The object types of JSON from API, described in the previous chapter:

// =========================================================================
// common/types.ts—JSON objects exchanged with API RdvMedecins
// (see the chapter on the black box, which describes each route)
// =========================================================================

export type Role = 'ADMIN' | 'DOCTOR' | 'USER';

// POST /api/auth/login, GET /api/auth/moi
export interface Utilisateur {
  login: string;
  nom: string;
  role: Role;
}

// GET /api/captcha
export interface Captcha {
  id: string;
  svg: string;
}

// a doctor or a client (GET /api/doctors, GET /api/clients...)
export interface Personne {
  id: number;
  version: number;
  titre: string;
  prenom: string;
  nom: string;
  login?: string; // only for ADMIN
}

export interface Identite {
  titre: string;
  prenom: string;
  nom: string;
}

// a row from GET /api/agenda
export interface CreneauAgenda {
  id: number;
  hdebut: number;
  mdebut: number;
  hfin: number;
  mfin: number;
  libre: boolean;
  patient: Identite | null;
  moi: boolean;
  reservable: boolean;
  idRv: number | null;
}

// GET /api/calendar?idMedecin=...&day=...
export interface Agenda {
  medecin: Personne;
  jour: string;
  creneaux: CreneauAgenda[];
  info: string | null;
}

A connection component, rewritten with [api.ts] and reduced to a bar:

<!--
  =========================================================================
  commun/BarreConnexion.vue - connexion / déconnexion, en une barre
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Le composant de l'exemple 18, réduit à une barre et réécrit avec
  commun/api.ts. Il émet 'change' avec l'utilisateur connecté (ou null)
  chaque fois que celui-ci change - y compris au démarrage, après avoir
  interrogé GET /api/auth/moi.
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { onMounted, reactive, ref } from 'vue';
import { api, ErreurApi } from './api';
import type { Captcha, Utilisateur } from './types';

const emit = defineEmits<{ change: [utilisateur: Utilisateur | null] }>();

const utilisateur = ref<Utilisateur | null>(null);
const captcha = ref<Captcha | null>(null);
const saisie = reactive({ login: 'admin', password: '', captcha: '' });
const erreur = ref<string | null>(null);

async function nouveauCaptcha(): Promise<void> {
  captcha.value = await api.get<Captcha>('/captcha');
  saisie.captcha = '';
}

function changer(u: Utilisateur | null): void {
  utilisateur.value = u;
  emit('change', u);
}

onMounted(async () => {
  try {
    changer(await api.get<Utilisateur>('/auth/moi'));
  } catch {
    changer(null); // 401: No one is logged in
    await nouveauCaptcha().catch(() => (erreur.value = 'Le serveur JSON est-il lancé (port 8080) ?'));
  }
});

async function seConnecter(): Promise<void> {
  erreur.value = null;
  try {
    const u = await api.post<Utilisateur>('/auth/login', {
      login: saisie.login,
      password: saisie.password,
      captchaId: captcha.value?.id,
      captcha: saisie.captcha,
    });
    saisie.password = '';
    changer(u);
  } catch (e) {
    erreur.value = e instanceof ErreurApi ? `${e.statusCode} ${e.cle}` : String(e);
    await nouveauCaptcha();
  }
}

async function seDeconnecter(): Promise<void> {
  await api.post('/auth/logout');
  changer(null);
  await nouveauCaptcha();
}
</script>

<template>
  <div class="alert alert-secondary d-flex flex-wrap align-items-center gap-2 py-2">
    <template v-if="utilisateur">
      <span>Connecté : <strong>{{ utilisateur.nom }}</strong> <span class="badge text-bg-primary">{{ utilisateur.role }}</span></span>
      <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary ms-auto" @click="seDeconnecter">Se déconnecter</button>
    </template>
    <form v-else class="d-flex flex-wrap align-items-center gap-2 w-100" @submit.prevent="seConnecter">
      <input v-model="saisie.login" class="form-control form-control-sm w-auto" placeholder="login" autocomplete="username">
      <input v-model="saisie.password" type="password" class="form-control form-control-sm w-auto" placeholder="mot de passe" autocomplete="current-password">
      <div v-if="captcha" class="captcha" v-html="captcha.svg"></div>
      <input v-model="saisie.captcha" class="form-control form-control-sm w-auto" placeholder="captcha" autocomplete="off" size="8">
      <button class="btn btn-sm btn-primary">Se connecter</button>
      <span v-if="erreur" class="text-danger small">{{ erreur }}</span>
    </form>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
/* The CAPTCHA image, scaled down to fit in the bar */
.captcha :deep(svg) {
  display: block;
  height: 32px;
  width: auto;
}
</style>
  • Line 16: The component sends [change] with the logged-in user (or [null]) every time it changes, including at startup;
  • line 35: with [api.ts], a request fits on one line; in case of failure (401), it switches to [catch];
  • Line 54: [instanceof] distinguishes an error in API from another anomaly.

Above [api.ts], a function per route from API:

// =========================================================================
// 19-service-api/src/rdvmedecins.service.ts - the access layer to API
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A typed function per route in API. The components are not aware of
// the URL, fetch, or the JSON format: they call functions.
// This is the client-side equivalent of the server-side DAO layer: if the API
// changes (a URL, a field name), only this file is modified.
// =========================================================================

import { api } from '../../commun/api';
import type { Agenda, Personne } from '../../commun/types';

export const rdvmedecins = {
  getMedecins: () => api.get<Personne[]>('/medecins'),
  getClients: () => api.get<Personne[]>('/clients'),
   // URLSearchParams generates "?idMedecin=1&jour=2030-01-15" by encoding the necessary data
  getAgenda: (idMedecin: number, jour: string) =>
    api.get<Agenda>(`/agenda?${new URLSearchParams({ idMedecin: String(idMedecin), jour })}`),
  reserver: (jour: string, idCreneau: number, idClient?: number) =>
    api.post<{ id: number }>('/rendez-vous', { jour, idCreneau, idClient }),
  annuler: (idRv: number) => api.delete<Record<string, never>>(`/rendez-vous/${idRv}`),
};

This is the client-side equivalent of the server’s DAO layer: the components are not aware of URL, [fetch], or the JSON format; they call typed functions. If API changes, only this file changes.

  • Line 18: [URLSearchParams] generates the string [idMedecin=1&jour=2030-01-15] by encoding the characters that need to be encoded.

The page:

<!--
  =========================================================================
  19-service-api/src/App.vue - un agenda, avec la couche d'accès à l'API
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Connectez-vous (barre du haut), choisissez un médecin et un jour : l'agenda
  s'affiche. ADMIN et DOCTOR peuvent réserver pour un patient et annuler ;
  un patient (martin...) réserve pour lui-même. Chaque action se termine par
  un rechargement de l'agenda : c'est le SERVEUR qui fait foi.
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, ref, watch } from 'vue';
import BarreConnexion from '../../commun/BarreConnexion.vue';
import { ErreurApi } from '../../commun/api';
import type { Agenda, CreneauAgenda, Personne, Utilisateur } from '../../commun/types';
import { rdvmedecins } from './rdvmedecins.service';

const utilisateur = ref<Utilisateur | null>(null);
const medecins = ref<Personne[]>([]);
const clients = ref<Personne[]>([]);
const idMedecin = ref<number | null>(null);
const jour = ref(demain());
const agenda = ref<Agenda | null>(null);
const idClient = ref<number | null>(null);
const message = ref<{ type: 'success' | 'danger'; texte: string } | null>(null);

const gestionnaire = computed(() => utilisateur.value !== null && utilisateur.value.role !== 'USER');

function demain(): string {
  const d = new Date(Date.now() + 24 * 3600 * 1000);
  return `${d.getFullYear()}-${String(d.getMonth() + 1).padStart(2, '0')}-${String(d.getDate()).padStart(2, '0')}`;
}

function horaire(c: CreneauAgenda): string {
  const hm = (h: number, m: number) => `${h}:${String(m).padStart(2, '0')}`;
  return `${hm(c.hdebut, c.mdebut)} - ${hm(c.hfin, c.mfin)}`;
}

// an error from API becomes a message (its key, for lack of a dictionary here)
function signaler(e: unknown): void {
  message.value = { type: 'danger', texte: e instanceof ErreurApi ? `${e.statusCode} ${e.cle}` : String(e) };
}

// Login/logout: we (re)load what this role is authorized to view
async function surConnexion(u: Utilisateur | null): Promise<void> {
  utilisateur.value = u;
  agenda.value = null;
  medecins.value = [];
  clients.value = [];
  if (u === null) {
    return;
  }
  try {
    medecins.value = await rdvmedecins.getMedecins();
     // the patient list: only for ADMIN and DOCTOR (a USER would receive a 403)
    clients.value = gestionnaire.value ? await rdvmedecins.getClients() : [];
  } catch (e) {
    signaler(e);
  }
}

async function chargerAgenda(): Promise<void> {
  if (idMedecin.value === null) {
    return;
  }
  try {
    agenda.value = await rdvmedecins.getAgenda(idMedecin.value, jour.value);
  } catch (e) {
    agenda.value = null;
    signaler(e);
  }
}

// The calendar is based on the doctor and the day selected
watch([idMedecin, jour], () => {
  message.value = null;
  chargerAgenda();
});

async function reserver(c: CreneauAgenda): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await rdvmedecins.reserver(jour.value, c.id, gestionnaire.value ? (idClient.value ?? undefined) : undefined);
    message.value = { type: 'success', texte: `Créneau ${horaire(c)} réservé.` };
  } catch (e) {
    signaler(e);
  }
  await chargerAgenda();
}

async function annuler(c: CreneauAgenda): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await rdvmedecins.annuler(c.idRv as number);
    message.value = { type: 'success', texte: `Rendez-vous de ${horaire(c)} annulé.` };
  } catch (e) {
    signaler(e);
  }
  await chargerAgenda();
}
</script>

<template>
  <div class="container py-4">
    <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Exemple 19 - une couche d'accès à l'API</h1>
    <BarreConnexion @change="surConnexion" />

    <template v-if="utilisateur">
      <div class="row g-2 mb-3">
        <div class="col-sm-5">
          <select v-model="idMedecin" class="form-select">
            <option :value="null" disabled>-- choisir un médecin --</option>
            <option v-for="m in medecins" :key="m.id" :value="m.id">{{ m.titre }} {{ m.prenom }} {{ m.nom }}</option>
          </select>
        </div>
        <div class="col-sm-3"><input v-model="jour" type="date" class="form-control"></div>
        <div v-if="gestionnaire" class="col-sm-4">
          <select v-model="idClient" class="form-select">
            <option :value="null">-- patient à inscrire --</option>
            <option v-for="c in clients" :key="c.id" :value="c.id">{{ c.titre }} {{ c.prenom }} {{ c.nom }}</option>
          </select>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div v-if="message" class="alert" :class="`alert-${message.type}`">{{ message.texte }}</div>
       <!-- Info: The key sent by the server when a patient already has an upcoming appointment -->
      <div v-if="agenda?.info" class="alert alert-info">{{ agenda.info }}</div>

      <table v-if="agenda" class="table table-sm align-middle">
        <caption class="caption-top">Agenda du {{ agenda.jour }} - {{ agenda.medecin.titre }} {{ agenda.medecin.prenom }} {{ agenda.medecin.nom }}</caption>
        <tbody>
          <tr v-for="c in agenda.creneaux" :key="c.id">
            <td>{{ horaire(c) }}</td>
            <td>
              <span v-if="c.libre" class="badge text-bg-success">Libre</span>
              <span v-else-if="c.patient" class="badge" :class="c.moi ? 'text-bg-primary' : 'text-bg-secondary'">
                {{ c.patient.titre }} {{ c.patient.prenom }} {{ c.patient.nom }}
              </span>
              <span v-else class="badge text-bg-secondary">Réservé</span>
            </td>
            <td class="text-end">
               <!-- the buttons are based on the permissions calculated by the server -->
              <button v-if="c.reservable" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-success" @click="reserver(c)">Réserver</button>
              <button v-if="c.idRv !== null" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger" @click="annuler(c)">Annuler</button>
            </td>
          </tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </template>
  </div>
</template>
  • Line 27: ADMIN or DOCTOR;
  • lines 45–60: Each time a user logs in or out, the content that this role is authorized to view is (re)loaded. A patient would receive a 403 error for the client list: we don’t even request it;
  • line 75: [watch] can monitor multiple sources: the calendar is reloaded when the doctor OU changes the day;
  • Lines 80–87: a reservation, followed by QUOI, QU, IL, and ARRIVE, and a refresh of the calendar. The server’s record is final: if the time slot has been taken by someone else in the meantime, the refreshed calendar will show it;
  • lines 141 and 142: the buttons reflect the permissions calculated by the server;
  • line 137: a booked slot for which the server has not assigned a patient (as seen by a patient).

Logged in as [admin], select a doctor, a patient, and book a time slot:

Book a second appointment slot for the same patient: the server refuses. Since there is no dictionary in this example, the raw key is displayed:

docs.title: 8.4. Example 20: Errors Returned by the Server
docs.text:
Last example before the case study: customer management, handled by the ADMIN form. This form performs no validation in the browser: everything is sent to the server, which validates the data and, in case of rejection, responds with the error for each field. Example 06 showed the alternative approach; this one has a significant advantage: the rules exist only in UN one place—the server—and the client cannot overlook them. The trade-off: a round trip to the server before displaying the errors.

The dictionaries use the server’s error codes:

{
  "FORM": {
    "TITRE_AJOUT": "Ajouter un client",
    "TITRE_MODIF": "Modifier un client",
    "TITRE": "Titre",
    "PRENOM": "Prénom",
    "NOM": "Nom",
    "LOGIN": "Login",
    "PASSWORD": "Mot de passe",

    "ANNULER": "Annuler",

    "SUPPRIMER": "Supprimer",

import { createApp } from 'vue';
import { createI18n } from 'vue-i18n';
import 'bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css';
import App from './App.vue';
import fr from './locales/fr.json';
