createApp(App).use(i18n).mount('#app');

The page:

<!--
  =========================================================================
  20-erreurs-serveur/src/App.vue - afficher les erreurs du SERVEUR
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  La gestion des clients (compte admin). Ce formulaire ne fait
  VOLONTAIREMENT aucune validation dans le navigateur : tout est envoyé au
  serveur, qui répond, en cas de refus, par une erreur JSON :

    400 { cle: 'ERRORS.INVALID_FORM', champs: { nom: 'ERRORS.LASTNAME_REQUIRED' } }
    409 { cle: 'ERRORS.PATIENT_ALREADY_EXISTS', champs: { prenom: ..., nom: ... } }
    409 { cle: 'ERRORS.CONCURRENT_UPDATE' }         (verrou optimiste)

  Le client traduit chaque clé (vue-i18n) et place chaque message sous son
  champ, le message général en bas du formulaire. Essayez : un nom vide, un
  titre modifié dans les outils de développement, un homonyme (Alice DURAND),
  un login déjà pris (martin), la même fiche modifiée dans deux onglets...
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, reactive, ref } from 'vue';
import { useI18n } from 'vue-i18n';
import BarreConnexion from '../../commun/BarreConnexion.vue';
import { api, ErreurApi } from '../../commun/api';
import type { Personne, Utilisateur } from '../../commun/types';
// The confirmation window from Example 12, reused as-is
import FenetreConfirmation from '../../12-confirmation/src/components/FenetreConfirmation.vue';
import { useConfirmation } from '../../12-confirmation/src/composables/useConfirmation';

const { t, locale } = useI18n();
const { confirmer } = useConfirmation();

const utilisateur = ref<Utilisateur | null>(null);
const clients = ref<Personne[]>([]);
const estAdmin = computed(() => utilisateur.value?.role === 'ADMIN');

// the form: idEdite === null -> create, otherwise update
const idEdite = ref<number | null>(null);
const saisie = reactive({ titre: 'Mr', prenom: '', nom: '', login: '', password: '', version: 0 });
// errors returned by the server
const erreurChamps = ref<Record<string, string>>({});
const erreurPage = ref<ErreurApi | null>(null);
const succes = ref<string | null>(null);

async function surConnexion(u: Utilisateur | null): Promise<void> {
  utilisateur.value = u;
  clients.value = [];
  if (u?.role === 'ADMIN') {
    await recharger();
  }
}

async function recharger(): Promise<void> {
  clients.value = await api.get<Personne[]>('/clients');
}

function nouveau(): void {
  idEdite.value = null;
  Object.assign(saisie, { titre: 'Mr', prenom: '', nom: '', login: '', password: '', version: 0 });
  effacerErreurs();
}

function editer(c: Personne): void {
  idEdite.value = c.id;
   // the VERSION read from the record is sent back with the update: if someone
   // has modified the record in the meantime, the server will respond with a 409 CONCURRENT_UPDATE
  Object.assign(saisie, { titre: c.titre, prenom: c.prenom, nom: c.nom, login: c.login ?? '', password: '', version: c.version });
  effacerErreurs();
}

function effacerErreurs(): void {
  erreurChamps.value = {};
  erreurPage.value = null;
  succes.value = null;
}

// an error message, in the current language, with its parameters
function texte(e: ErreurApi): string {
  return t(e.cle, e.params);
}

async function enregistrer(): Promise<void> {
  effacerErreurs();
  const corps = { ...saisie };
  try {
    const client =
      idEdite.value === null
        ? await api.post<Personne>('/clients', corps)
        : await api.put<Personne>(`/clients/${idEdite.value}`, corps);
    const message = t(idEdite.value === null ? 'FORM.AJOUTE' : 'FORM.MODIFIE', {
      nom: `${client.prenom} ${client.nom}`,
      login: client.login ?? '',
    });
    nouveau(); // form cleared, messages deleted...
    succes.value = message; // ... except this one
    await recharger();
  } catch (e) {
    if (!(e instanceof ErreurApi)) {
      throw e;
    }
     // the error for each field, and the general message
    erreurChamps.value = e.champs;
    erreurPage.value = e;
  }
}

async function supprimer(c: Personne): Promise<void> {
  const nom = `${c.prenom} ${c.nom}`;
  if (!(await confirmer(t('FORM.CONFIRMER_SUPPRESSION', { nom })))) {
    return;
  }
  effacerErreurs();
  try {
    await api.delete(`/clients/${c.id}`);
    succes.value = t('FORM.SUPPRIME', { nom });
  } catch (e) {
    erreurPage.value = e instanceof ErreurApi ? e : null;
  }
  await recharger();
}
</script>

<template>
  <div class="container py-4">
    <div class="d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center mb-3">
      <h1 class="h3 mb-0">Exemple 20 - les erreurs renvoyées par le serveur</h1>
      <select v-model="locale" class="form-select form-select-sm w-auto">
        <option value="fr">FR</option>
        <option value="en">EN</option>
      </select>
    </div>
    <BarreConnexion @change="surConnexion" />
    <p v-if="utilisateur && !estAdmin" class="alert alert-warning">{{ t('FORM.ADMIN_SEULEMENT') }}</p>

    <div v-if="estAdmin" class="row g-4">
      <div class="col-lg-6">
        <table class="table table-sm align-middle">
          <tbody>
            <tr v-for="c in clients" :key="c.id">
              <td>{{ c.titre }} {{ c.prenom }} {{ c.nom }}</td>
              <td><code>{{ c.login }}</code></td>
              <td class="text-end text-nowrap">
                <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary me-1" @click="editer(c)">{{ t('FORM.MODIFIER') }}</button>
                <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger" @click="supprimer(c)">{{ t('FORM.SUPPRIMER') }}</button>
              </td>
            </tr>
          </tbody>
        </table>
      </div>

      <div class="col-lg-6">
        <form class="card p-3" novalidate @submit.prevent="enregistrer">
          <h2 class="h5">{{ idEdite === null ? t('FORM.TITRE_AJOUT') : t('FORM.TITRE_MODIF') }}</h2>
          <div class="mb-2">
            <label class="form-label" for="titre">{{ t('FORM.TITRE') }}</label>
             <!-- a "Dr" option that the server will reject: to view ERRORS.INVALID_TITLE -->
            <select id="titre" v-model="saisie.titre" class="form-select" :class="{ 'is-invalid': erreurChamps.titre }">
              <option>Mr</option><option>Mme</option><option>Melle</option><option>Dr</option>
            </select>
            <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ erreurChamps.titre && t(erreurChamps.titre) }}</div>
          </div>
          <div class="row g-2 mb-2">
            <div class="col-sm-6">
              <label class="form-label" for="prenom">{{ t('FORM.PRENOM') }}</label>
              <input id="prenom" v-model="saisie.prenom" class="form-control" :class="{ 'is-invalid': erreurChamps.prenom }">
              <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ erreurChamps.prenom && t(erreurChamps.prenom) }}</div>
            </div>
            <div class="col-sm-6">
              <label class="form-label" for="nom">{{ t('FORM.NOM') }}</label>
              <input id="nom" v-model="saisie.nom" class="form-control" :class="{ 'is-invalid': erreurChamps.nom }">
              <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ erreurChamps.nom && t(erreurChamps.nom) }}</div>
            </div>
          </div>
          <div class="row g-2 mb-3">
            <div class="col-sm-6">
              <label class="form-label" for="login">{{ t('FORM.LOGIN') }}</label>
              <input id="login" v-model="saisie.login" class="form-control" :class="{ 'is-invalid': erreurChamps.login }">
              <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ erreurChamps.login && t(erreurChamps.login) }}</div>
            </div>
            <div class="col-sm-6">
              <label class="form-label" for="password">{{ t('FORM.PASSWORD') }}</label>
              <input id="password" v-model="saisie.password" type="password" class="form-control" autocomplete="new-password"
                     :class="{ 'is-invalid': erreurChamps.password }">
              <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ erreurChamps.password && t(erreurChamps.password) }}</div>
            </div>
          </div>
          <div class="d-flex gap-2">
            <button class="btn btn-primary">{{ t('FORM.ENREGISTRER') }}</button>
            <button type="button" class="btn btn-secondary" @click="nouveau">{{ t('FORM.ANNULER') }}</button>
          </div>
          <div v-if="succes" class="alert alert-success mt-3 mb-0">{{ succes }}</div>
           <!-- the general message and the status HTTP, to understand -->
          <div v-if="erreurPage" class="alert alert-danger mt-3 mb-0">
            {{ texte(erreurPage) }} <span class="small text-muted">({{ erreurPage.statusCode }} {{ erreurPage.cle }})</span>
          </div>
        </form>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <FenetreConfirmation />
</template>
  • Line 26: the confirmation window from Example 12, reused as-is—a well-designed component is reusable;
  • lines 40 and 41: the errors returned by the server: the error for each field, and the general message;
  • lines 62–68: to modify a record, copy its values into the form, including the version number: it will be saved with the modification (optimistic locking);
  • lines 77–79: the error message, in everyday language, along with its parameters;
  • lines 81–102: [POST] for a creation, [PUT] for a modification. If the request is rejected, the returned errors are stored; the template handles the rest;
  • line 157: a title that the server will reject, to see [ERRORS.INVALID_TITLE];
  • lines 164 and 165: a rejected field is highlighted in red, and its translated error code is displayed below it;
  • line 126: changing the language also re-translates the error messages already displayed: only the keys have been retained.

An incorrectly filled-out form:

A duplicate name (Alice DURAND already exists): the server returns a 409 response and identifies the first name and last name fields:

The same error, in English:

Also try editing the same record in two tabs: the second record receives [ERRORS.CONCURRENT_UPDATE].

docs.title: 12. Conclusion
docs.text:
We have written the [Vue.js] client for the [RdvMedecins] application. For the user, it provides the same pages as the HTML application from the [NestJS] course; for the developer, everything has changed:

  • the server no longer generates pages. It exposes a API JSON, whose contract (routes, body, codes, and error keys) was sufficient to write the client without ever reading its code;
  • the pages, language, formatting, messages, and navigation have moved to the browser;
  • Security, however, has not changed: it is still the server that authenticates (cookie [HttpOnly]), verifies roles and management rules, and decides what a patient is authorized to see. The client simply displays what the server sends it.

The same server JSON could serve other clients: a mobile app, a client named [Angular] or [React], or a script. That is the whole point of separating the client from the server with a API.

The [Vue.js] concepts covered in this course (components, responsiveness, router, stores, composables) are common to all [Vue.js] applications. To learn more:

  • the official documentation, in French: https://fr.vuejs.org;
  • tests: [Vitest] for unit tests of components and composables, [Playwright] for end-to-end tests (this is the tool used to create the screenshots in this document);
  • [Nuxt], the framework built on top of [Vue.js], which can also generate pages on the server side: this would then partially replicate the architecture of the [NestJS] course.

docs.title: 11. Deployment
docs.text:
In development, two servers work together: [Vite] (the client) and the server JSON (the API). In production, there is only one:

1. Build the client. In the [rdvmedecins-vuejs] folder:

npm run build

The console displays (excerpt):

> rdvmedecins-vuejs@1.0.0 build
> vue-tsc --noEmit && vite build

vite v7.3.6 building client environment for production...
✓ 96 modules transformed.
dist/index.html                                    0.90 kB │ gzip:  0.53 kB
dist/assets/index-C2BH5lpe.css                   231.34 kB │ gzip: 30.87 kB
dist/assets/ErreurView-WmT0JIzD.js                 0.55 kB │ gzip:  0.40 kB
dist/assets/PersonnesView-CSo0V33J.js              2.04 kB │ gzip:  0.99 kB
dist/assets/EspacePatientView-UadQ9HRE.js          2.21 kB │ gzip:  1.09 kB
dist/assets/InscriptionView-B3-HHgam.js            2.59 kB │ gzip:  1.22 kB
dist/assets/PersonneFormulaireView-DEIiSHDx.js     2.67 kB │ gzip:  1.34 kB
dist/assets/MonCompteView-BRleWR-E.js              3.92 kB │ gzip:  1.54 kB
dist/assets/index-BkCBbbGt.js                    196.28 kB │ gzip: 70.71 kB
✓ built in 2.15s

The [dist/] folder contains the entire application: a page named [index.html], a stylesheet, and optimized [JavaScript] files (the code from [Vue.js], the router, [Pinia]... and ours). The pages loaded on demand ([() => import(...)]) each have their own file. The name of each file contains a hash of its contents ([index-BkCBbbGt.js]): a new version will have a different name, and a browser will never be able to cache an outdated version.

You can verify this version using [npm run preview] (http://localhost:4173).

2. Upload it to the server. Copy CONTENU from the [dist/] folder to the [client/] folder at the root of the server JSON ([rdvmedecins-nestjs-json/client/index.html], [rdvmedecins-nestjs-json/client/assets/...]), then restart the server. It displays:

[Nest] LOG [RdvMedecins] client Vue.js servi depuis .../rdvmedecins-nestjs-json/client
[Nest] LOG [RdvMedecins] serveur JSON démarré : http://localhost:8080/api

The complete application is then available at http://localhost:8080. The server serves the client’s files and returns [index.html] for any other address outside of [/api]: reloading the [/agenda] page works (it is the client’s router that displays it). For the curious reader, it is the file [src/web/client-spa.ts] on the server that performs this task.

3. In a live production environment, don’t forget the server file [.env]:

  • a long, random [JWT_SECRET];
  • an empty [CAPTCHA_TEST];
  • [COOKIE_SECURE=true] if the site is served via HTTPS (it must be: passwords are being transmitted);
  • [TRUST_PROXY=true] if the server is behind a proxy ([nginx]...), so that the attempt limit sees the clients’ actual IP address.

We then launch the compiled server: [npm run build], followed by [npm run start:prod].

docs.title: 2.1. Example 01: The Structure of a Vue.js Application
2.1.1. The package.json file
docs.text:
The [package.json] file in the examples folder declares the libraries used and the project commands:

{
  "name": "exemples-vuejs",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "Les petits exemples du cours [Introduction étape par étape au framework Vue.js] - une seule installation pour tous",
  "private": true,
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "vite",
    "build": "vue-tsc --noEmit && vite build",
    "verifier": "vue-tsc --noEmit"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "bootstrap": "^5.3.8",
    "pinia": "^3.0.4",
    "vue": "^3.5.22",
    "vue-i18n": "~11.3.2",
    "vue-router": "^4.6.3"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@types/node": "^22.10.0",
    "@vitejs/plugin-vue": "^6.0.1",
    "@vue/tsconfig": "^0.8.1",
    "typescript": "~5.9.3",
    "vite": "^7.1.12",
    "vue-tsc": "^3.1.3"
  }
}

Let’s go over this file:

  • Line 6: The [JavaScript] files in the project are ES modules ([import] / [export]), the standard format of [JavaScript], which is supported by browsers such as [Node.js];
  • Lines 7–11: the project commands, launched by [npm run <nom>]:
    • [npm run dev] starts the development server for [Vite];
    • [npm run verifier] has the [TypeScript] types of all files, including [.vue], verified by the [vue-tsc] tool;
    • [npm run build] checks the types and then builds the production version of the examples;
  • Lines 12–18: the libraries the application needs in the browser: [Vue.js] itself, its router ([vue-router]), [Pinia] for shared state, [vue-i18n] for languages, and [Bootstrap] for formatting;
  • lines 19–26: the development tools: [Vite] and its extension for files [.vue], the compiler [TypeScript], and [vue-tsc]. They are not part of the application delivered to users.

The prefix [^] of a version ([^3.5.22]) allows [npm] to install a newer version of the same major version (3.x.y); the prefix [~] ([~11.3.2]) allows only hotfixes (11.3.x). The [vue-i18n] version is intentionally locked to series 11.3: subsequent versions require [Node.js] 22.

docs.title: 2.1.2. The vite.config.ts file
docs.text:
[Vite] is the tool that runs a [Vue.js] application during development and then builds it for production. Its configuration, common to all examples:

// =========================================================================
// vite.config.ts - the Vite configuration, common to the TOUS examples.
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Vite is both:
//    - a development server (npm run dev): it compiles on the fly the
//      .vue and .ts files requested by the browser, and reloads the page
//      (or just the modified component) with every save;
//    - a build tool (npm run build): it generates, in the dist/ directory,
//      optimized .js and .css files to be deployed to a web server.
//
// Each example is a small, standalone application with its own
// index.html: 01-first-application/index.html, 02-responsiveness/index.html...
// A single server quickly serves them all: http://localhost:5173/ displays the
// the table of contents (index.html for this folder), http://localhost:5173/01-premiere-application/
// the first example, etc.
// =========================================================================

import { existsSync, readdirSync } from 'node:fs';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { resolve } from 'node:path';
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';
import vue from '@vitejs/plugin-vue';

const racine = fileURLToPath(new URL('.', import.meta.url));

// the example folders: those whose names begin with two digits
const exemples = readdirSync(racine).filter((d) => /^\d\d-/.test(d) && existsSync(resolve(racine, d, 'index.html')));

export default defineConfig({
   // the plugin that teaches Vite to compile .vue files
  plugins: [vue()],

  server: {
    port: 5173,
     // PROXY: any browser request to /api/... is forwarded by
     // Vite to the JSON RdvMedecins server (port 8080), and the response is then sent back
     // to the browser. From the browser’s perspective, the page and API therefore originate from
     // (http://localhost:5173): no CORS to configure, and the cookie for
     // token JWT circulates normally (see the chapter on the black box).
    proxy: {
       '/api': 'http://localhost:8080',
    },
  },

   // `npm run build`: an entry page, for example, plus the table of contents
  build: {
    rollupOptions: {
      input: Object.fromEntries([
        ['sommaire', resolve(racine, 'index.html')],
        ...exemples.map((d) => [d, resolve(racine, d, 'index.html')]),
      ]),
    },
  },
});
  • line 31: the extension that instructs [Vite] to compile the [.vue] files. A browser cannot read a [.vue] file: when it requests one, [Vite] converts it on the fly into a standard [JavaScript] file;
  • line 34: the development server’s port;
  • lines 40–41: the proxy, which will only be used starting with Example 17: any request from the browser to an address beginning with [/api] is forwarded to the server JSON [RdvMedecins], on port 8080. We’ll come back to this;
  • Lines 27 and 46–53: [npm run build] must know all the entry pages for the application. It is provided with the index and the [index.html] file for each folder whose name begins with two digits.

docs.title: 2.1.3. The files tsconfig.json and env.d.ts
docs.text:
{
  "extends": "@vue/tsconfig/tsconfig.dom.json",
  "compilerOptions": {
    "types": ["vite/client"],
    "noUnusedLocals": true,
    "noUnusedParameters": true
  },
  "include": ["*/src/**/*.ts", "*/src/**/*.vue", "commun/**/*.ts", "commun/**/*.vue", "env.d.ts"]
}
  • Line 2: We use the [TypeScript] configuration recommended for [Vue.js] ([@vue/tsconfig] package): modern code, strict mode, type checking in the browser (DOM);
  • Line 4: Types specific to [Vite] (such as when importing a [.css] or [.svg] file);
  • Lines 5–7: An unused variable or parameter is reported as an error;
  • line 8: the files to be checked: those in the [src] folders from the examples and the [commun] folder.

The file [env.d.ts] contains only one directive, which makes the same types as in [Vite] visible in the editor:

// Vite-specific types (importing .css files, import.meta.env...)
/// <reference types="vite/client" />

docs.title: 2.1.4. The page index.html
docs.text:
Each example has its own HTML page. The page for Example 01:

<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>Exemple 01 - une première application</title>
</head>
<body>
   <!-- The Vue.js application is displayed in this element (see src/main.ts) -->
  <div id="app"></div>
  <script type="module" src="./src/main.ts"></script>
</body>
</html>

This is the only page the browser will load. It is almost empty:

  • line 10: the element in which [Vue.js] will display the application;
  • line 11: the application program. [Vite] compiles it and sends it to the browser as [JavaScript].

docs.title: 2.1.5. The entry point: main.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 01-first-application/src/main.ts - the application's entry point
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// index.html loads this file (<script type="module" src="./src/main.ts">).
// It builds the application Vue.js from its component RACINE (App.vue)
// and displays it in the <div id="app"> element on the page.
// =========================================================================

import { createApp } from 'vue';
// the Bootstrap stylesheet: Vite inserts it into the page
import 'bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css';
import App from './App.vue';

// createApp(App): an application whose root component is App;
// mount('#app'): its rendering HTML replaces the content of <div id="app">
createApp(App).mount('#app');
  • Line 9: the function in [Vue.js] that creates an application;
  • line 11: a stylesheet, [CSS], is imported just as a module would be. [Vite] inserts it into the page;
  • line 12: the root component of the application, defined in the file [App.vue];
  • line 16: the application is created from this component, then “mounted” in the [<div id="app">] element: the HTML produced by [App.vue] replaces its content.

docs.title: 2.1.6. The root component: App.vue
docs.text:
<!--
  =========================================================================
  01-premiere-application/src/App.vue - un premier composant
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Un fichier .vue (Single File Component) regroupe les trois facettes d'un
  composant :
    - <script setup> : les données et le code du composant (TypeScript) ;
    - <template>     : le HTML à afficher, avec des {{ ... }} ;
    - <style>        : son CSS (ici "scoped" : il ne s'applique qu'à lui).
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';

// "ordinary" data: the template can display it
const titre = 'Bienvenue dans Vue.js';
const langages = ['TypeScript', 'HTML', 'CSS'];

// ref(...): a RÉACTIVE data item. When its value (.value) changes, Vue updates
// updates the parts of the page that display it
const compteur = ref(0);
const heure = ref(new Date().toLocaleTimeString());

// a function called by the button in the template
function incrementer(): void {
  compteur.value++;
  heure.value = new Date().toLocaleTimeString();
}
</script>

<template>
  <div class="container py-4">
     <!-- {{ expression }}: the value of the expression, inserted into the page -->
    <h1 class="h3">{{ titre }}</h1>
    <p>Cette page est fabriquée dans le navigateur, par Vue.js, à partir de trois fichiers : index.html, main.ts et App.vue.</p>
    <p>On y écrit du {{ langages.join(', ') }} ({{ langages.length }} langages).</p>

     <!-- @click: the function to call when clicked (see example 04) -->
    <button class="btn btn-primary" @click="incrementer">Cliquez-moi</button>
     <!-- in the template, no .value: Vue "unpacks" the refs on its own -->
    <p class="mt-3 compteur">Vous avez cliqué {{ compteur }} fois (dernier clic : {{ heure }}).</p>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
/* "scoped": this rule applies only to elements of the CE component */
.compteur {
  font-weight: bold;
  color: #0d6efd;
}
</style>

A [.vue] file (Single File Component, or SFC) combines the three facets of a component:

  • lines 12–29: the component code, in [TypeScript] ([lang="ts"]). With [setup], all variables and functions declared at the top level of the script are directly usable in the template;
    • lines 16–17: two ordinary data items;
    • line 21: [ref(0)] creates a reactive data item with an initial value of 0. Its value is read and modified via its property [value]. When it changes, [Vue.js] updates all locations on the page where it is displayed;
    • lines 25–27: a function that modifies two reactive data fields. It does not alter the page: [Vue.js] will update it;
  • lines 31–43: the component’s HTML:
    • line 34: the [{{ expression }}] syntax (the “mustaches”) inserts the value of a [TypeScript] expression into the page. It is escaped: if [titre] contained [<b>], [<b>] would be displayed without the tag being interpreted;
    • line 36: the expression can be anything: a method call, a calculation;
    • line 39: clicking the button calls the function [incrementer] (see example 04);
    • line 41: in the template, you write [compteur], not [compteur.value]: [Vue.js] automatically “unpacks” the [ref];
  • lines 45–51: the component’s CSS. With [scoped], its rules apply only to elements of the CE component: [Vite] adds a unique attribute to its elements ([data-v-xxxx]) and includes it in the selectors.

docs.title: 2.1.7. Execution
docs.text:
With the [Vite] server running ([npm run dev]), open the URL http://localhost:5173/01-premiere-application/ and click the button three times:

Two experiments to try:

  • Edit the title text in [App.vue] and save the file: the page updates immediately, without reloading, and the counter retains its value. This is the hot swap of modules (HMR, [Hot Module Replacement]) from [Vite];
  • View the page’s source code (Ctrl-U): it contains only the page [index.html], which is almost empty. The displayed HTML was generated by [Vue.js] within the browser. To view it, use the developer tools inspector (F12, Elements tab) or the [Vue.js devtools] extension, which also displays the components and their data.

docs.title: 2.2. Example 02: Responsiveness
docs.text:
Responsiveness is at the heart of [Vue.js]. This example calculates the price TTC of an item:

<!--
  =========================================================================
  02-reactivite/src/App.vue - ref, reactive, computed, watch
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Un petit calculateur de prix TTC :
    - ref      : une valeur réactive simple (un nombre, une chaîne...) ;
    - reactive : un OBJET réactif (toutes ses propriétés le sont) ;
    - computed : une valeur CALCULÉE à partir d'autres, recalculée
                 automatiquement quand elles changent ;
    - watch    : du code exécuté quand une valeur change (un "effet").
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, reactive, ref, watch } from 'vue';

// ref: its value is read and written using .value (in the TypeScript code)
const quantite = ref(1);

// reactive: an object whose properties are read and written directly
const article = reactive({
  libelle: 'Stylo',
  prixHT: 2.5,
  tauxTVA: 20, // in %
});

// computed: never assigned directly, always recalculated. The view knows
// which data it depends on (quantity, article.prixHT, article.tauxTVA):
// it recalculates it when any of these values change, and only in that case
const totalHT = computed(() => quantite.value * article.prixHT);
const montantTVA = computed(() => (totalHT.value * article.tauxTVA) / 100);
const totalTTC = computed(() => totalHT.value + montantTVA.value);

// a euro amount formatter, in the French style (1,234.50 €)
const euros = new Intl.NumberFormat('fr-FR', { style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' });

// watch: every time the total TTC changes, a record is kept
const historique = ref<string[]>([]);
watch(totalTTC, (nouveau, ancien) => {
  historique.value.unshift(`${euros.format(ancien)} -> ${euros.format(nouveau)}`);
  historique.value = historique.value.slice(0, 5); // the last 5
});

function reinitialiser(): void {
  quantite.value = 1;
  article.prixHT = 2.5;
  article.tauxTVA = 20;
}
</script>

<template>
  <div class="container py-4">
    <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Exemple 02 - la réactivité</h1>
    <div class="row g-4">
      <div class="col-md-6">
        <div class="card p-3">
           <!-- v-model links a field to data, in both directions (see example 05) -->
          <label class="form-label">Article</label>
          <input v-model="article.libelle" class="form-control mb-2">
          <label class="form-label">Prix unitaire HT</label>
          <input v-model.number="article.prixHT" type="number" step="0.1" min="0" class="form-control mb-2">
          <label class="form-label">Quantité</label>
          <input v-model.number="quantite" type="number" min="0" class="form-control mb-2">
          <label class="form-label">Taux de TVA</label>
          <select v-model.number="article.tauxTVA" class="form-select mb-3">
            <option :value="5.5">5,5 %</option>
            <option :value="10">10 %</option>
            <option :value="20">20 %</option>
          </select>
          <button class="btn btn-outline-secondary" @click="reinitialiser">Réinitialiser</button>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="col-md-6">
        <div class="card p-3">
          <h2 class="h5">{{ quantite }} x {{ article.libelle }}</h2>
          <table class="table mb-0">
            <tbody>
              <tr><td>Total HT</td><td class="text-end">{{ euros.format(totalHT) }}</td></tr>
              <tr><td>TVA ({{ article.tauxTVA }} %)</td><td class="text-end">{{ euros.format(montantTVA) }}</td></tr>
              <tr class="fw-bold"><td>Total TTC</td><td class="text-end">{{ euros.format(totalTTC) }}</td></tr>
            </tbody>
          </table>
        </div>
        <div class="card p-3 mt-3">
          <h2 class="h6">Historique du total TTC (watch)</h2>
          <ul class="mb-0">
            <li v-for="(ligne, i) in historique" :key="i">{{ ligne }}</li>
          </ul>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>
  • line 17: [ref] accepts a simple value (number, string, boolean);
  • lines 20–24: [reactive] makes an entire object reactive: each of its properties is reactive. They are read and written directly ([article.prixHT]), without [.value];
  • lines 29–31: [computed] defines a value calculated from other values. [Vue.js] stores the data read during the calculation ([quantite], [article.prixHT]...) and only recalculates when one of them changes. It is never assigned a value: it is read ([totalHT.value]);
  • line 34: [Intl.NumberFormat], the number formatting tool integrated into [JavaScript]: [2.5] becomes “2.50 €”;
  • lines 38–41: [watch] executes code whenever data changes, receiving both the new and old values. It is used for actions such as saving data, sending a request, or writing to the browser’s storage... To display a derived value, we prefer [computed];
  • lines 43–46: Simply modify the data; all fields, totals, and the history will update accordingly;
  • lines 58–64: [v-model] links each field to a data point, in both directions (see example 05);
  • line 77: In the template, a [computed] is used in the same way as a [ref], without [.value];
  • line 86: a repeated list for each element of the [historique] array (see example 03).

docs.title: 2.3. Example 03: Directives
docs.text:
A directive is a special template attribute, prefixed by [v-], that defines the behavior of the element to which it is applied.

<!--
  =========================================================================
  03-directives/src/App.vue - les directives de base
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Une DIRECTIVE est un attribut spécial du template, préfixé par v- :
    - v-bind:attr="expr" (abrégé :attr="expr") : la valeur d'un attribut
      HTML calculée par une expression ; :class et :style acceptent des
      objets et des tableaux ;
    - v-if / v-else-if / v-else : l'élément n'existe dans la page que si
      la condition est vraie ;
    - v-show : l'élément existe toujours, il est seulement caché (display:none) ;
    - v-for="x in liste" : l'élément est répété pour chaque x, avec une
      clé :key unique qui permet à Vue de suivre chaque ligne.
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, ref } from 'vue';
// Import an image: Vite provides its URL (and, in production, an optimized copy
// optimized copy of the file, with a unique name)
import urlLogo from './assets/medecin.svg';

// An interface TypeScript describes the format of the objects in the list
interface Medecin {
  id: number;
  titre: string;
  prenom: string;
  nom: string;
  specialite: string;
  disponible: boolean;
}

const medecins = ref<Medecin[]>([
  { id: 1, titre: 'Mme', prenom: 'Marie', nom: 'PELISSIER', specialite: 'généraliste', disponible: true },
  { id: 2, titre: 'Mr', prenom: 'Paul', nom: 'TATOU', specialite: 'pédiatre', disponible: false },
  { id: 3, titre: 'Melle', prenom: 'Sophie', nom: 'DUPONT', specialite: 'généraliste', disponible: true },
]);

const filtre = ref(''); // search text
const seulementDisponibles = ref(false);
const afficherAide = ref(true);

// the displayed list: a computed field, recalculated when the filter changes
const medecinsAffiches = computed(() =>
  medecins.value.filter(
    (m) =>
      (!seulementDisponibles.value || m.disponible) &&
      `${m.prenom} ${m.nom} ${m.specialite}`.toLowerCase().includes(filtre.value.trim().toLowerCase()),
  ),
);
</script>

<template>
  <div class="container py-4">
    <h1 class="h3 mb-3">
       <!-- :src: the value of the src attribute is that of the variable urlLogo -->
      <img :src="urlLogo" alt="logo" width="32" height="32">
      Exemple 03 - les directives
    </h1>

    <div class="d-flex flex-wrap gap-3 align-items-center mb-3">
      <input v-model="filtre" class="form-control w-auto" placeholder="rechercher...">
      <label class="form-check-label">
        <input v-model="seulementDisponibles" type="checkbox" class="form-check-input"> disponibles seulement
      </label>
      <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" @click="afficherAide = !afficherAide">
        {{ afficherAide ? "Cacher l'aide" : "Montrer l'aide" }}
      </button>
    </div>

     <!-- v-show: the paragraph remains on the page, but is simply hidden -->
    <p v-show="afficherAide" class="alert alert-info">
      Tapez un nom ou une spécialité. Les médecins indisponibles sont grisés.
    </p>

     <!-- v-if / v-else-if / v-else: only one of the three blocks exists at a time -->
    <p v-if="medecins.length === 0" class="text-muted">Aucun médecin.</p>
    <p v-else-if="medecinsAffiches.length === 0" class="text-warning">Aucun médecin ne correspond à « {{ filtre }} ».</p>
    <table v-else class="table">
      <thead>
        <tr><th>#</th><th>Doctor</th><th>Specialty</th><th>Status</th></tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
         <!-- v-for: one row per doctor; (m, index) also provides the rank.
             :key="m.id" : l'identité de chaque ligne, pour que Vue sache
             quelle ligne ajouter, déplacer ou supprimer quand la liste change -->
        <tr v-for="(m, index) in medecinsAffiches" :key="m.id" :class="{ 'text-muted': !m.disponible }">
          <td>{{ index + 1 }}</td>
          <td>{{ m.titre }} {{ m.prenom }} {{ m.nom }}</td>
          <td>{{ m.specialite }}</td>
          <td>
             <!-- :class with an array: multiple classes, including one that is calculated -->
            <span :class="['badge', m.disponible ? 'text-bg-success' : 'text-bg-secondary']">
              {{ m.disponible ? 'disponible' : 'indisponible' }}
            </span>
          </td>
        </tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>

     <!-- :style with an object: calculated properties CSS -->
    <p :style="{ fontSize: 12 + medecinsAffiches.length * 2 + 'px' }">
      {{ medecinsAffiches.length }} médecin(s) affiché(s) - la taille de ce texte en dépend.
    </p>
  </div>
</template>
  • Line 23: An interface [TypeScript] describes the format of the objects in the list; [ref<Medecin[]>(...)] specifies the data type;
  • line 20: an image is imported as a module. [Vite] provides its address; in production, it will create a copy with a unique name (which changes with its content: browsers will never keep an old version in the cache);
  • line 43: the displayed list, filtered by the input and the checkbox;
  • line 56: [v-bind:src="expression"], abbreviated to [:src="expression"], assigns the value of an expression to the attribute [src]. Without the colon, [src="urlLogo"] would refer to a file named “urlLogo”;
  • line 71: [v-show] hides the element ([display: none]) when the condition is false. The element remains on the page;
  • Lines 76–78: [v-if], [v-else-if], and [v-else]: Only one of these three elements exists on the page at any given time. We choose [v-show] for an element that is frequently shown and hidden, and [v-if] otherwise;
  • Line 86: [v-for] repeats the element for each doctor; [index] is its rank (starting at 0). The attribute [:key="m.id"] gives each row an identity: when the list changes, [Vue.js] knows which rows to add, delete, or move, instead of rebuilding everything from scratch. A key must be unique and stable: we use the object’s identifier, never its rank;
  • line 86: [:class] with an object: the class [text-muted] is added if the condition is true;
  • line 92: [:class] with an array: multiple classes, including a calculated one;
  • line 101: [:style] with an object of calculated properties [CSS] (in [camelCase]).

With a filter that returns no results, the [v-else-if] paragraph is displayed:

docs.title: 2.4. Example 04: Events
docs.text:
<!--
  =========================================================================
  04-evenements/src/App.vue - réagir aux actions de l'utilisateur
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  v-on:evenement="gestionnaire" (abrégé @evenement="gestionnaire") :
    - @click="f"          appelle f(evenementNatif) ;
    - @click="f(3, $event)" appelle f avec des arguments ; $event est
                          l'événement natif du navigateur ;
    - modificateurs : @submit.prevent (empêche l'envoi classique du
      formulaire), @keyup.enter (seulement la touche Entrée), @click.stop...
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';

interface Tache {
  id: number;
  libelle: string;
  faite: boolean;
}

const taches = ref<Tache[]>([
  { id: 1, libelle: 'Installer Node.js', faite: true },
  { id: 2, libelle: 'Lire le chapitre sur les événements', faite: false },
]);
const nouvelle = ref('');
const journal = ref<string[]>([]);
let prochainId = 3;

function tracer(message: string): void {
  journal.value.unshift(`${new Date().toLocaleTimeString()} ${message}`);
}

// called by @submit.prevent: the browser does not send PAS the form to the
// server (no page reload); it’s our code that handles it
function ajouter(): void {
  const libelle = nouvelle.value.trim();
  if (libelle === '') {
    return;
  }
  taches.value.push({ id: prochainId++, libelle, faite: false });
  tracer(`ajout de « ${libelle} »`);
  nouvelle.value = '';
}

function supprimer(tache: Tache): void {
  taches.value = taches.value.filter((t) => t.id !== tache.id);
  tracer(`suppression de « ${tache.libelle} »`);
}

// $event: the native event (here, a MouseEvent), along with its coordinates
function position(evenement: MouseEvent): void {
  tracer(`clic en (${evenement.offsetX}, ${evenement.offsetY})`);
}
</script>

<template>
  <div class="container py-4">
    <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Exemple 04 - les événements</h1>

     <!-- @submit.prevent: Input in the OU field, click on the button -->
    <form class="d-flex gap-2 mb-3" @submit.prevent="ajouter">
      <input v-model="nouvelle" class="form-control" placeholder="nouvelle tâche" @keyup.esc="nouvelle = ''">
      <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">Ajouter</button>
    </form>

    <ul class="list-group mb-3">
      <li v-for="t in taches" :key="t.id" class="list-group-item d-flex align-items-center gap-2">
        <input v-model="t.faite" type="checkbox" class="form-check-input" @change="tracer(`« ${t.libelle} » : ${t.faite ? 'faite' : 'à faire'}`)">
        <span :class="{ 'text-decoration-line-through text-muted': t.faite }" class="flex-grow-1">{{ t.libelle }}</span>
         <!-- a handler with an argument: the task from CETTE line -->
        <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger" @click="supprimer(t)">Supprimer</button>
      </li>
    </ul>

    <div class="zone p-3 mb-3 rounded" @click="position($event)">Cliquez dans cette zone</div>

    <h2 class="h6">Journal</h2>
    <ul class="small">
      <li v-for="(ligne, i) in journal" :key="i">{{ ligne }}</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
.zone {
  background: #e9f2ff;
  height: 80px;
  cursor: crosshair;
}
</style>
  • Line 62: [v-on:submit], abbreviated as [@submit], listens for the [submit] event from the form (pressing Enter in a field or clicking a button). The modifier [.prevent] calls [event.preventDefault()]: the browser does not send the form to the server via PAS and does not reload the page; the function [ajouter] is the one that executes;
  • line 63: a key modifier: only pressing Esc triggers the handler. This is a simple instruction written in the template;
  • line 69: a handler can be a function call with arguments;
  • line 72: Each button passes the task from SA to [supprimer];
  • line 76: [$event] refers to the browser’s native event—in this case, a [MouseEvent]—along with the click coordinates;
  • lines 36–43: Adding a task means adding an object to the reactive array; clearing the field means clearing the data to which it is linked;
  • lines 46–47: the array is replaced with a filtered copy. [Vue.js] tracks both “in-place” modifications ([push], [splice]) and the complete replacement.

docs.title: 2.5. Example 05: Form Fields
docs.text:
Same form as Example 18 from the [NestJS] course, but everything happens in the browser here:

<!--
  =========================================================================
  05-formulaires/src/App.vue - tous les types de champs, reliés par v-model
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  v-model="donnee" relie un champ de formulaire à une donnée réactive, dans
  les DEUX sens : taper dans le champ modifie la donnée, et modifier la
  donnée (par le code) modifie le champ. La donnée reçue dépend du champ :
    - input texte, textarea            -> string
    - input + .number                   -> number
    - case à cocher seule               -> boolean
    - cases à cocher sur un même tableau -> string[] (les valeurs cochées)
    - boutons radio                     -> la valeur du bouton choisi
    - select / select multiple          -> la valeur / un tableau de valeurs
    - input type="date"                 -> string "yyyy-MM-dd"
  Modificateurs : .trim (espaces retirés), .number, .lazy (mise à jour à la
  sortie du champ plutôt qu'à chaque touche).
  Même formulaire que l'exemple 18 du cours NestJS ; mais ici, pas de
  serveur : tout se passe dans le navigateur.
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { reactive, ref } from 'vue';

const titres = ['Mr', 'Mme', 'Melle'];
const loisirsPossibles = ['sport', 'musique', 'lecture', 'cinéma'];
const pays = [
  { code: 'fr', libelle: 'France' },
  { code: 'be', libelle: 'Belgique' },
  { code: 'ch', libelle: 'Suisse' },
];

// all form values, in UN reactive object
const formulaire = reactive({
  titre: 'Mme',
  nom: '',
  age: 30,
  presentation: '',
  newsletter: false,
  loisirs: ['lecture'] as string[],
  pays: 'fr',
  langues: [] as string[],
  naissance: '',
});

const envoye = ref<string | null>(null);

function envoyer(): void {
   // JSON.stringify: what would be sent to a server (see Example 18)
  envoye.value = JSON.stringify(formulaire, null, 2);
}
</script>

<template>
  <div class="container py-4">
    <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Exemple 05 - les champs d'un formulaire</h1>
    <div class="row g-4">
      <form class="col-md-7" @submit.prevent="envoyer">
        <div class="mb-3">
          <span class="form-label d-block">Titre</span>
           <!-- radio buttons: same v-model, one value per button -->
          <div v-for="t in titres" :key="t" class="form-check form-check-inline">
            <input :id="'titre-' + t" v-model="formulaire.titre" type="radio" :value="t" class="form-check-input">
            <label :for="'titre-' + t" class="form-check-label">{{ t }}</label>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="row g-3 mb-3">
          <div class="col-8">
            <label class="form-label" for="nom">Nom</label>
             <!-- .trim: " martin " becomes "martin" -->
            <input id="nom" v-model.trim="formulaire.nom" class="form-control">
          </div>
          <div class="col-4">
            <label class="form-label" for="age">Âge</label>
             <!-- .number: the data is converted to a number, not the string "30" -->
            <input id="age" v-model.number="formulaire.age" type="number" class="form-control">
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="presentation">Présentation</label>
          <textarea id="presentation" v-model="formulaire.presentation" rows="2" class="form-control"></textarea>
        </div>
        <div class="mb-3 form-check">
           <!-- a single checkbox: true / false -->
          <input id="newsletter" v-model="formulaire.newsletter" type="checkbox" class="form-check-input">
          <label for="newsletter" class="form-check-label">Recevoir la lettre d'information</label>
        </div>
        <div class="mb-3">
          <span class="form-label d-block">Loisirs</span>
           <!-- multiple checkboxes on the same form: the checked values -->
          <div v-for="l in loisirsPossibles" :key="l" class="form-check form-check-inline">
            <input :id="'loisir-' + l" v-model="formulaire.loisirs" type="checkbox" :value="l" class="form-check-input">
            <label :for="'loisir-' + l" class="form-check-label">{{ l }}</label>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="row g-3 mb-3">
          <div class="col-6">
            <label class="form-label" for="pays">Pays</label>
            <select id="pays" v-model="formulaire.pays" class="form-select">
               <!-- :value: the transmitted value (the code); the displayed text is the label -->
              <option v-for="p in pays" :key="p.code" :value="p.code">{{ p.libelle }}</option>
            </select>
          </div>
          <div class="col-6">
            <label class="form-label" for="langues">Langues parlées</label>
            <select id="langues" v-model="formulaire.langues" multiple class="form-select" size="3">
              <option value="fr">français</option>
              <option value="en">anglais</option>
              <option value="es">espagnol</option>
            </select>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="naissance">Date de naissance</label>
          <input id="naissance" v-model="formulaire.naissance" type="date" class="form-control w-auto">
        </div>
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">Envoyer</button>
      </form>

      <div class="col-md-5">
        <h2 class="h6">Le modèle, en direct</h2>
         <!-- {{ object }} displays the object in JSON format -->
        <pre class="bg-light p-2 rounded small">{{ formulaire }}</pre>
        <template v-if="envoye">
          <h2 class="h6">Dernier envoi</h2>
          <pre class="bg-success-subtle p-2 rounded small">{{ envoye }}</pre>
        </template>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>
  • Lines 33–43: all form values, in a reactive object. The annotations [as string[]] specify to [TypeScript] the type of the arrays, which cannot be inferred from [[]];
  • line 62: radio buttons share the same [v-model]; the data receives the value ([:value]) of the selected button;
  • line 70: the modifier [.trim] removes leading and trailing spaces;
  • line 75: [.number] converts the input to a number. Without it, the data would be set to the string ["30"]: a HTML field contains only text;
  • line 84: a checkbox by itself returns a Boolean value;
  • Line 91: Multiple checkboxes linked to the same table: it contains the values of the checked checkboxes;
  • line 100: for a drop-down list, [:value] is the value transmitted (the country code); the text of the option is simply its label;
  • line 105: a multiple-choice list results in an array;
  • line 114: a date field returns a string ["yyyy-MM-dd"], regardless of how the browser displays it;
  • line 122: [{{ objet }}] displays an object in the format JSON: you can see the template change with each keystroke;
  • line 49: [JSON.stringify(objet, null, 2)] generates the text JSON for an object, indented by 2 spaces. This is what would be sent to a server (see Example 18).

docs.title: 2.6. Example 06: Form Validation
docs.text:
We’ll use the rules from the “Create a Customer Account” form on the [RdvMedecins] server and verify them in the browser as the user types:

<!--
  =========================================================================
  06-validation/src/App.vue - valider un formulaire dans le navigateur
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Les erreurs sont des COMPUTED : elles sont recalculées à chaque frappe.
  On ne les affiche pas d'emblée (un formulaire vide couvert de rouge est
  désagréable) : seulement pour un champ déjà quitté ("touché"), ou pour
  tous les champs après une tentative d'envoi.

  Mêmes règles que le serveur RdvMedecins (formulaire "Créer un compte") :
  titre dans la liste, prénom et nom obligatoires (20 caractères au plus),
  login en minuscules, mot de passe de 6 caractères au moins, confirmation.

  ATTENTION : cette validation n'est qu'un CONFORT pour l'utilisateur (une
  réponse immédiate, sans aller-retour avec le serveur). Elle ne protège
  rien : n'importe qui peut envoyer au serveur une requête fabriquée à la
  main (curl...). Le serveur revalide donc TOUJOURS tout (cf. exemple 20).
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, reactive, ref } from 'vue';

const TITRES = ['Mr', 'Mme', 'Melle'];
const FORMAT_LOGIN = /^[a-z0-9._-]{1,30}$/;
const MOT_DE_PASSE_MIN = 6;

type Champ = 'titre' | 'prenom' | 'nom' | 'login' | 'password' | 'confirmation';

const saisie = reactive<Record<Champ, string>>({
  titre: 'Mr',
  prenom: '',
  nom: '',
  login: '',
  password: '',
  confirmation: '',
});

// fields the user has already exited (blur event)
const touches = reactive(new Set<Champ>());
const envoiTente = ref(false);
const succes = ref(false);

// the error for each field ('' = no error), recalculated with each keystroke
const erreurs = computed<Record<Champ, string>>(() => ({
  titre: TITRES.includes(saisie.titre) ? '' : 'Choisissez un titre dans la liste.',
  prenom: obligatoire(saisie.prenom, 'Le prénom') || maximum(saisie.prenom, 'Le prénom', 20),
  nom: obligatoire(saisie.nom, 'Le nom') || maximum(saisie.nom, 'Le nom', 20),
  login:
    obligatoire(saisie.login, 'Le login') ||
    (FORMAT_LOGIN.test(saisie.login.trim())
      ? ''
      : 'Lettres minuscules non accentuées, chiffres, point, tiret, souligné.'),
  password:
    obligatoire(saisie.password, 'Le mot de passe') ||
    (saisie.password.length < MOT_DE_PASSE_MIN ? `Au moins ${MOT_DE_PASSE_MIN} caractères.` : ''),
  confirmation: saisie.confirmation === saisie.password ? '' : 'La confirmation ne correspond pas au mot de passe.',
}));

const formulaireValide = computed(() => Object.values(erreurs.value).every((e) => e === ''));

function obligatoire(valeur: string, nom: string): string {
  return valeur.trim() === '' ? `${nom} est obligatoire.` : '';
}
function maximum(valeur: string, nom: string, max: number): string {
  return valeur.trim().length > max ? `${nom} ne doit pas dépasser ${max} caractères.` : '';
}

// the error at AFFICHER for a field: only if it has been touched, or afterward
// an attempt to submit
function erreurVisible(champ: Champ): string {
  return touches.has(champ) || envoiTente.value ? erreurs.value[champ] : '';
}

function envoyer(): void {
  envoiTente.value = true;
  succes.value = formulaireValide.value;
}
</script>

<template>
  <div class="container py-4" style="max-width: 640px">
    <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Exemple 06 - la validation d'un formulaire</h1>
     <!-- novalidate: browser-specific validation is disabled, for
         afficher NOS messages, dans NOTRE style -->
    <form class="card p-4" novalidate @submit.prevent="envoyer">
      <div class="mb-3">
        <label class="form-label" for="titre">Titre</label>
        <select id="titre" v-model="saisie.titre" class="form-select" :class="{ 'is-invalid': erreurVisible('titre') }">
          <option v-for="t in TITRES" :key="t">{{ t }}</option>
        </select>
      </div>
      <div class="row g-3 mb-3">
        <div class="col-sm-6">
          <label class="form-label" for="prenom">Prénom</label>
           <!-- @blur: the user leaves the field, which is marked as “touched”;
               la classe Bootstrap is-invalid l'encadre de rouge et fait
               apparaître le .invalid-feedback qui suit -->
          <input id="prenom" v-model="saisie.prenom" class="form-control"
                 :class="{ 'is-invalid': erreurVisible('prenom') }" @blur="touches.add('prenom')">
          <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ erreurVisible('prenom') }}</div>
        </div>
        <div class="col-sm-6">
          <label class="form-label" for="nom">Nom</label>
          <input id="nom" v-model="saisie.nom" class="form-control"
                 :class="{ 'is-invalid': erreurVisible('nom') }" @blur="touches.add('nom')">
          <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ erreurVisible('nom') }}</div>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="mb-3">
        <label class="form-label" for="login">Login</label>
        <input id="login" v-model="saisie.login" class="form-control" autocomplete="username"
               :class="{ 'is-invalid': erreurVisible('login'), 'is-valid': touches.has('login') && !erreurs.login }"
               @blur="touches.add('login')">
        <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ erreurVisible('login') }}</div>
      </div>
      <div class="row g-3 mb-4">
        <div class="col-sm-6">
          <label class="form-label" for="password">Mot de passe</label>
          <input id="password" v-model="saisie.password" type="password" class="form-control" autocomplete="new-password"
                 :class="{ 'is-invalid': erreurVisible('password') }" @blur="touches.add('password')">
          <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ erreurVisible('password') }}</div>
        </div>
        <div class="col-sm-6">
          <label class="form-label" for="confirmation">Confirmation</label>
          <input id="confirmation" v-model="saisie.confirmation" type="password" class="form-control" autocomplete="new-password"
                 :class="{ 'is-invalid': erreurVisible('confirmation') }" @blur="touches.add('confirmation')">
          <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ erreurVisible('confirmation') }}</div>
        </div>
      </div>
      <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">Créer le compte</button>
      <div v-if="envoiTente && !formulaireValide" class="alert alert-danger mt-3 mb-0">Le formulaire contient des erreurs.</div>
      <div v-if="succes" class="alert alert-success mt-3 mb-0">Formulaire valide : il pourrait être envoyé au serveur.</div>
    </form>
  </div>
</template>
  • Line 27: the type of the field names. [Record<Champ, string>] is an object with exactly these properties: a typo in a field name would be detected at compile time;
  • line 39: the fields the user has already left. A responsive [Set]: [touches.add(...)] updates the page;
  • lines 44–57: the errors in the fields, recalculated with each keystroke. An empty string means “no error”; [a || b] returns [b] when [a] is empty: this allows us to chain the checks for a field, with the first one that fails triggering the message;
  • line 59: true if there are no errors;
  • lines 70–72: a field’s error is displayed only if it has been “touched,” or after an attempt to submit. A blank form highlighted in red before you’ve even started would be unpleasant;
  • line 85: [novalidate] disables the browser’s controls (attribute [required]...), so that only our messages are displayed, in our style;
  • line 99: the [blur] event: the user leaves the field;
  • line 99: the class [Bootstrap] [is-invalid] frames the field in red and displays the [<div class="invalid-feedback">] that follows it;
  • line 112: [is-valid], conversely, frames it in green.

After clicking “Create Account,” the form is empty:

then, once the form is filled out correctly:

An important note: this validation is merely a convenience. It responds immediately, without a round trip to the server, but it provides no protection: anyone can send a manually crafted request to the server (using [curl], for example), without going through our pages. The server must therefore revalidate what it receives. In Example 20, and later in the case study, we’ll look at another approach: letting the server handle validation and display messages.

docs.title: 9. Interim Conclusion
docs.text:
The twenty examples have introduced the concepts we need to write the [RdvMedecins] client:

ConceptWhere it will be used in the case studycomponents, props, [v-model], slotsthe navigation bar, form fields, windows[ref], [reactive], [computed], [watch]all pages; the calendar that follows its URLcustomizablethe confirmation window, formatting, and form errorsthe router and its guardsthe pages, the permissions for each role, the session to be restored after F5Piniathe logged-in user, success and error messagesi18n viewFrench and English, and the translation of server errorsfetch, httpOnly cookie, proxythe connection and all communication with the serverthe API access layera [rdvmedecins.api.ts] file, one function per route

The client will be the exact equivalent of the HTML application from the [NestJS] course, page by page. The difference lies elsewhere: the server no longer generates any pages; it responds in JSON, and everything related to display (pages, language, date formatting, messages) has been moved to the browser.

docs.title: 6.1. Example 16: A Bilingual Application
docs.text: In the [NestJS] course, the server translated the pages before sending them. Here, translation takes place in the browser using the [vue-i18n] library, and switching languages no longer requires any interaction with the server.

docs.title: 6.1.1. Dictionaries
docs.text:
One dictionary per language, in the JSON format. Each text has a key ([ACCUEIL.BONJOUR]):

{
  "APP": {
    "TITRE": "Exemple 16 - une application en deux langues",
    "LANGUE": "Langue"
  },
  "ACCUEIL": {
    "BONJOUR": "Bonjour {nom} !",
    "AUJOURDHUI": "Nous sommes le {date}.",
    "PRIX": "Une consultation coûte {prix}.",
    "RENDEZ_VOUS": "aucun rendez-vous | un rendez-vous | {n} rendez-vous",
    "AJOUTER": "Ajouter un rendez-vous",
    "RETIRER": "En retirer un"
  },
  "ERRORS": {
    "LOGIN_TAKEN": "Ce login est déjà utilisé par un autre compte.",
    "TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS": "Trop de tentatives infructueuses. Réessayez dans {minutes} minute(s)."
  },
  "SERVEUR": {
    "TITRE": "Traduire une réponse du serveur",
    "EXPLICATION": "Le serveur RdvMedecins ne renvoie que des clés. C'est le client qui les traduit :"
  }
}

{
  "APP": {
    "TITRE": "Example 16 - a two-language application",
    "LANGUE": "Language"
  },
  "ACCUEIL": {
    "BONJOUR": "Hello {nom}!",
    "AUJOURDHUI": "Today is {date}.",
    "PRIX": "A consultation costs {prix}.",
    "RENDEZ_VOUS": "no appointment | one appointment | {n} appointments",
    "AJOUTER": "Add an appointment",
    "RETIRER": "Remove one"
  },
  "ERRORS": {
    "LOGIN_TAKEN": "This login is already used by another account.",
    "TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS": "Too many failed attempts. Try again in {minutes} minute(s)."
  },
  "SERVEUR": {
    "TITRE": "Translating a server response",
    "EXPLICATION": "The RdvMedecins server only sends keys. The client translates them:"
  }
}
  • line 7: [{nom}] is a message parameter;
  • line 10: a plural message: its forms are separated by [|] (zero, one, multiple); [{n}] is the number;
  • Lines 14–17: These are the MÊMES keys that the server returns in its error responses (see the following chapter).

docs.title: 6.1.2. The configuration
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 16-i18n/src/i18n.ts - the vue-i18n configuration
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// view-i18n is the translation library for Vue.js. It is provided with:
//    - one DICTIONNAIRE per language (files in `locales/fr.json`, `locales/en.json`),
//      where each text has a CLÉ ("ACCUEIL.BONJOUR");
//    - the source language (here: the one stored in localStorage; otherwise
//      the browser’s language, otherwise French);
//    - date and number formats specific to each language.
// In components, t('ACCUEIL.BONJOUR', { name: 'Marie' }) returns the
// text in the language COURANTE; changing the language updates the entire page.
//
// On the client side, this works on the same principle as the NestJS course (dictionaries
// i18n/*.json + {{t}} helper) — but the translation now takes place in
// the browser, and changing the language no longer requires any server interaction.
// =========================================================================

import { createI18n } from 'vue-i18n';
import fr from './locales/fr.json';
import en from './locales/en.json';

export type Langue = 'fr' | 'en';
export const CLE_LANGUE = 'exemple16.langue';

function langueDeDepart(): Langue {
  const memorisee = localStorage.getItem(CLE_LANGUE);
  if (memorisee === 'fr' || memorisee === 'en') {
    return memorisee;
  }
  return navigator.language.startsWith('en') ? 'en' : 'fr';
}

// message type: that of the French dictionary (the “template”)
type Messages = typeof fr;

export const i18n = createI18n<[Messages], Langue>({
  legacy: false, // the "Composition" (API), that of <script setup>
  locale: langueDeDepart(),
  fallbackLocale: 'fr', // a key missing in English: we use the French one
  messages: { fr, en },
   // d(date, 'long') and n(number, 'euros'): language-specific formats
  datetimeFormats: {
    fr: { long: { dateStyle: 'full' } },
    en: { long: { dateStyle: 'full' } },
  },
  numberFormats: {
    fr: { euros: { style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' } },
    en: { euros: { style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' } },
  },
});
  • line 19: [Vite] can import a JSON file: this returns an object;
  • lines 25–31: the language stored in [localStorage], otherwise the browser’s language ([navigator.language]), otherwise French;
  • lines 36–50: the configuration object:
    • [legacy: false]: the API “Composition” ([useI18n]), that of [<script setup>];
    • [fallbackLocale: 'fr']: a key missing from the English dictionary is taken from the French dictionary;
    • [datetimeFormats], [numberFormats]: date and number formats specific to each language.
import { createApp } from 'vue';
import 'bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css';
import App from './App.vue';
import { i18n } from './i18n';

// app.use(i18n): t(), d(), and n() become available in all components
createApp(App).use(i18n).mount('#app');

docs.title: 6.1.3. The page
docs.text:
<!--
  =========================================================================
  16-i18n/src/App.vue - une page traduite
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    - t('CLE')                  un texte ;
    - t('CLE', { nom: ... })    un texte à paramètres ({nom} dans le dictionnaire) ;
    - t('CLE', n)               un pluriel : "aucun | un | {n}" selon n ;
    - d(date, 'long')           une date, au format de la langue ;
    - n(nombre, 'euros')        un nombre, au format de la langue ;
    - locale                    la langue courante : la modifier retraduit tout.
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref, watch } from 'vue';
import { useI18n } from 'vue-i18n';
import { CLE_LANGUE, type Langue } from './i18n';

const { t, d, n, locale } = useI18n();
const nombre = ref(2);

// Every time the language changes: it is saved, and the page is updated
// the page’s lang attribute (useful for screen readers and proofreaders)
watch(
  locale,
  (langue) => {
    localStorage.setItem(CLE_LANGUE, langue);
    document.documentElement.lang = langue;
    document.title = t('APP.TITRE');
  },
  { immediate: true },
);

function choisir(langue: Langue): void {
  locale.value = langue;
}

// what the server would return: RdvMedecins (see the chapter on the black box)
const reponsesServeur = [
  { statusCode: 409, cle: 'ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN' },
  { statusCode: 429, cle: 'ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS', params: { minutes: '15' } },
];
</script>

<template>
  <div class="container py-4" style="max-width: 720px">
    <div class="d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center mb-3">
      <h1 class="h3 mb-0">{{ t('APP.TITRE') }}</h1>
      <div class="btn-group btn-group-sm" role="group" :aria-label="t('APP.LANGUE')">
        <button class="btn" :class="locale === 'fr' ? 'btn-primary' : 'btn-outline-primary'" @click="choisir('fr')">FR</button>
        <button class="btn" :class="locale === 'en' ? 'btn-primary' : 'btn-outline-primary'" @click="choisir('en')">EN</button>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="card p-3 mb-3">
      <p>{{ t('ACCUEIL.BONJOUR', { nom: 'Marie' }) }}</p>
      <p>{{ t('ACCUEIL.AUJOURDHUI', { date: d(new Date(), 'long') }) }}</p>
      <p>{{ t('ACCUEIL.PRIX', { prix: n(1234.5, 'euros') }) }}</p>
       <!-- t(key, number) selects the correct plural form -->
      <p class="fw-bold">{{ t('ACCUEIL.RENDEZ_VOUS', nombre) }}</p>
      <div class="d-flex gap-2">
        <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-success" @click="nombre++">{{ t('ACCUEIL.AJOUTER') }}</button>
        <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" :disabled="nombre === 0" @click="nombre--">{{ t('ACCUEIL.RETIRER') }}</button>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="card p-3">
      <h2 class="h6">{{ t('SERVEUR.TITRE') }}</h2>
      <p>{{ t('SERVEUR.EXPLICATION') }}</p>
      <ul class="mb-0">
        <li v-for="r in reponsesServeur" :key="r.cle">
          <code>{{ JSON.stringify(r) }}</code><br>
           <!-- the server key EST is a dictionary key; params provides its parameters -->
          → {{ t(r.cle, r.params ?? {}) }}
        </li>
      </ul>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>
  • line 18: translation tools:
    • [t(clé, paramètres)]: a text;
    • [t(clé, nombre)]: a plural;
    • [d(date, 'long')]: a date, in the language's format;
    • [n(nombre, 'euros')]: a number, in the language's format;
    • [locale]: the current language, a [ref]. Changing it re-translates the entire page;
  • lines 23–30: Each time the language is changed, the selection is saved and the page’s [lang] attribute is updated (useful for screen readers and spell-checkers);
  • lines 38–41: two error responses, as returned by the server [RdvMedecins];
  • line 73: the key sent by the server is a dictionary key; its parameters are those of the message.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
The document’s PDF is HERE.

The document’s codes are HERE.

This document is a product of Anthropic’s IA Claude. It follows the course “Step-by-Step Introduction to the NestJS Web Framework,” from which it shifts the perspective:

  • In the course [NestJS], the server generates the pages HTML (view engine [Handlebars]); the browser simply displays them;
  • in this course, the pages are generated in the browser by an application [Vue.js]; the server, now reduced to a simple server JSON, provides only data.

The application’s pages, however, remain unchanged: they are those of the [RdvMedecins] application already presented with the other frameworks (login with CAPTCHA, doctor’s schedule, appointment window, patient portal, doctor and client management, account creation, French and English).

The document follows the same structure as its predecessors: first, numerous short examples, each focusing on a specific concept of [Vue.js], followed by a complete case study—the [Vue.js] client for the [RdvMedecins] application—with all files fully commented.

There are already two courses available on [Vue.js]: “Introduction to the VUE.JS Framework Through Examples” (2019), written for [Vue.js] 2, and “An Example of a Vue.js Client/Server / NestJS (2026), which covers both the server and the client. This document differs from those in its approach: the server is treated as a black box, with only the API and JSON of interest to us, and we learn [Vue.js] step by step before tackling the complete client.

docs.title: 1.1. The Role of Vue.js in a Web Application
docs.text:
The application has two parts, which communicate with each other only through HTTP requests:

  • 1: The [Vue.js] application, running in the browser, sends a HTTP request to the server, for example, [GET /api/agenda?idMedecin=1&jour=2026-10-05];
  • 2: The server responds with data JSON: this doctor’s schedule for that day. It does not generate any pages;
  • 3: Using this data, [Vue.js] updates the page displayed in the browser without reloading it.

The following diagram compares the two architectures:

The browser loads only a single, nearly empty page—HTML—at startup. Everything else is generated by [JavaScript] code: this is known as a single-page application (SPA, for [Single Page Application]). When the user clicks on an internal link, no page is requested from the server: the [Vue.js] router changes the displayed URL and replaces the page’s content.

[Vue.js] is a [JavaScript] framework created in 2014 by Evan You. It is based on two ideas:

  • components: the interface is broken down into reusable pieces (a navigation bar, a form field, a confirmation window, etc.), each written in a [.vue] file that combines its HTML, code, and style;
  • responsiveness: a component’s data is “observed.” When any of it changes, [Vue.js] automatically updates the parts of the page that display it. We never write code that directly modifies the page.

We will use [Vue.js] 3, written in [TypeScript], with its most recent version: the API Composition and the [<script setup>] tag.

docs.title: 1.2. Tools Used
docs.text:
The examples were written and tested using the following tools (their installation is described in the appendix):

  • [Node.js] 22 (or at least 20.19) and its package manager [npm];
  • the [Visual Studio Code] editor, with the [Vue (Official)] extension;
  • a recent browser ([Chrome], [Firefox], [Edge]), if possible with the extension [Vue.js devtools];
  • the command-line tool [curl], which displays the raw HTTP responses;
  • the SGBD [MySQL] (or [MariaDB]), for example, the one for [Laragon] under [Windows]: it is required for the JSON server, as described in the chapter introducing it.

The libraries are those for the [package.json] files: [Vue.js] 3.5, [Vite] 7 (the development and build tool), [vue-router] 4 (the router), [Pinia] 3 (shared state), [vue-i18n] 11 (languages), [TypeScript] 5.9, [Bootstrap] 5.3.

docs.title: 1.3. Examples
docs.text:
The codes in the document are organized into three folders:

livrable/
├── exemples-vuejs/          les 20 petits exemples de Vue.js
├── rdvmedecins-nestjs-json/ le serveur JSON RdvMedecins (la « boîte noire »)
└── rdvmedecins-vuejs/       le client Vue.js de l'étude de cas

The examples folder contains one subfolder per example:

exemples-vuejs/
├── 01-premiere-application/
├── 02-reactivite/
├── ...
├── 20-erreurs-serveur/
├── commun/              du code partagé par les exemples 19 et 20
├── node_modules/
├── index.html           le sommaire des exemples
├── package.json
├── tsconfig.json
└── vite.config.ts

All examples share the same libraries, which are declared in [exemples-vuejs/package.json]. They are installed once, in a console opened to the [exemples-vuejs] folder (in [VS Code]: Terminal menu / New Terminal):

npm install

Then launch the [Vite] development server:

npm run dev

A single server, on port 5173, serves all twenty examples. The address http://localhost:5173/ displays their summary:

You can navigate from one example to another by following the links (http://localhost:5173/01-premiere-application/, http://localhost:5173/02-reactivite/...). The [Vite] server does not need to be restarted: every file that is modified and saved is immediately recompiled, and the browser page updates automatically. You can stop it by entering [Ctrl-C] in the console.

Examples 17 through 20 query the JSON and [RdvMedecins] servers: you will need to have them installed and running, as explained in the chapter dedicated to them.
