Each example is presented with its complete code, commented line by line, and a screenshot of its execution. The code itself is extensively commented: these comments are part of the course.

docs.title: 4. Routing
docs.text: A [Vue.js] application loads only one page, HTML. However, the [RdvMedecins] application has a login page, a calendar page, a “My Account” page... Each has its own URL ([/login], [/agenda], [/mon-espace]), which can be bookmarked, and the browser’s Back and Forward buttons work. This is the work of the router, the [vue-router] library.

docs.title: 4.1. Example 13: The Router
docs.text:
The router is added to the application in [main.ts]:

// =========================================================================
// 13-router/src/main.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// app.use(router): the router is added to the application. The components
// <RouterLink> and <RouterView> can then be used anywhere.
// =========================================================================

import { createApp } from 'vue';
import 'bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css';
import App from './App.vue';
import { router } from './router';

createApp(App).use(router).mount('#app');
  • Line 13: [app.use(...)] installs an extension ([plugin]): The components [<RouterLink>] and [<RouterView>], and the functions [useRoute()] and [useRouter()], become available everywhere.

The example data, "hard-coded":

// "hard-coded" data, so as not to depend on a server in this example
export interface Medecin {
  id: number;
  titre: string;
  prenom: string;
  nom: string;
  specialite: string;
}

export const MEDECINS: Medecin[] = [
  { id: 1, titre: 'Mme', prenom: 'Marie', nom: 'PELISSIER', specialite: 'généraliste' },
  { id: 2, titre: 'Mr', prenom: 'Paul', nom: 'TATOU', specialite: 'pédiatre' },
  { id: 3, titre: 'Melle', prenom: 'Sophie', nom: 'DUPONT', specialite: 'généraliste' },
];

The routes:

// =========================================================================
// 13-router/src/router.ts - the application’s ROUTES
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A Vue.js application is a single-page application (SPA: Single
// Page Application): the browser loads only the UNE page HTML. When you
// clicks on an internal link; no request is sent to the server:
// the router changes the address displayed by the browser and replaces the
// component displayed in <RouterView>.
//
// A route associates a CHEMIN with a COMPOSANT (referred to as a “view,” in the
// in the context of an application screen):
//    '/doctors/:id'       :id is a parameter (/doctors/2 -> id = "2");
//    '/:pathMatch(.*)*   ' any path: the "page not found" page
//                          (the most specific path always takes precedence).
//
// createWebHashHistory: URLs are in the form /13-router/#/doctors/2.
// Everything after the # remains in the browser: reload the page (F5)
// always requests /13-router/ again, which exists. This is the simplest method
// when the server knows nothing about the router—in this case, the Vite server, which
// serves twenty examples at a time. The case study will use
// "clean" addresses (createWebHistory: /agenda, /doctors...).
// =========================================================================

import { createRouter, createWebHashHistory } from 'vue-router';
import Accueil from './views/Accueil.vue';
import ListeMedecins from './views/ListeMedecins.vue';
import DetailMedecin from './views/DetailMedecin.vue';
import Recherche from './views/Recherche.vue';
import PageIntrouvable from './views/PageIntrouvable.vue';

export const router = createRouter({
  history: createWebHashHistory(),
  routes: [
    { path: '/', name: 'accueil', component: Accueil },
    { path: '/medecins', name: 'medecins', component: ListeMedecins },
     // props: true -> the :id parameter is passed to the component as a PROP
     // (the component is no longer dependent on the router: easier to reuse)
    { path: '/medecins/:id', name: 'medecin', component: DetailMedecin, props: true },
    { path: '/recherche', name: 'recherche', component: Recherche },
     // a redirect: the old address leads to the new one
    { path: '/docteurs', redirect: '/medecins' },
    { path: '/:pathMatch(.*)*', name: 'introuvable', component: PageIntrouvable },
  ],
});
  • Lines 33–43: A route associates a path with a component, which is called a “view” (in the sense of an application screen; this has nothing to do with the [Handlebars] views from the [NestJS] course, except for their role);
  • line 34: a route can have a name, which is more stable than its path for creating links;
  • Line 38: [:id] is a parameter: [/medecins/2] displays [DetailMedecin] along with [id = "2"]. The option [props: true] passes it to the component as a prop: the component is then no longer dependent on the router;
  • line 41: a redirect: the address [/docteurs] leads to [/medecins];
  • line 42: an arbitrary path: the “page not found” page. It only receives addresses that no other route recognizes: [vue-router] sorts routes by the precision of their path; the most precise one takes precedence (it is still placed last for readability);
  • line 32: history mode. With [createWebHashHistory], the addresses take the form [/13-routeur/#/medecins/2]: anything following [#] is never sent to the server, and reloading the page (F5) always requests [/13-routeur/], which exists. This is the simplest approach when the server does not know the client’s routes, which is the case for the server at [Vite], which serves twenty examples at a time. The case study will use [createWebHistory] and “clean” addresses ([/agenda]), which requires a little extra effort on the server’s part.

The application’s “shell”:

<!--
  =========================================================================
  13-routeur/src/App.vue - la "coquille" de l'application
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    - <RouterLink to="..."> : un lien interne. Il produit une balise <a>,
      mais un clic ne recharge pas la page : c'est le routeur qui agit.
      Le lien de la page affichée reçoit la classe "router-link-active"
      (ici remplacée par "active", celle de Bootstrap) ;
    - <RouterView /> : l'emplacement où s'affiche le composant de la route
      courante.
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { RouterLink, RouterView, useRoute } from 'vue-router';

// useRoute(): the current route (path, parameters, query...), reactive
const route = useRoute();
</script>

<template>
  <div class="container py-4">
    <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Exemple 13 - le routeur</h1>
    <nav class="nav nav-pills mb-3">
      <RouterLink class="nav-link" active-class="active" to="/">Accueil</RouterLink>
       <!-- `to` can be an object: the NOM of the route rather than its path -->
      <RouterLink class="nav-link" active-class="active" :to="{ name: 'medecins' }">Médecins</RouterLink>
      <RouterLink class="nav-link" active-class="active" :to="{ name: 'recherche', query: { q: 'généraliste' } }">Recherche</RouterLink>
      <RouterLink class="nav-link" to="/docteurs">/docteurs (redirection)</RouterLink>
      <RouterLink class="nav-link" to="/page-inconnue">Lien cassé</RouterLink>
    </nav>
    <p class="small text-muted">route courante : <code>{{ route.fullPath }}</code> (nom : {{ String(route.name) }})</p>
    <div class="card p-3">
      <RouterView />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>
  • line 17: the current route (path, parameters, [query]...), which is dynamic: the template updates when it changes;
  • line 24: [<RouterLink>] generates a [<a>] tag, but clicking does not reload the page: the router changes the address and the displayed component. The link on the current page is assigned the class specified by [active-class] (here, [active], which is the class of [Bootstrap]);
  • line 26: the destination can be an object: the route name rather than its path;
  • line 27: a link with query parameters: [/recherche?q=généraliste];
  • line 33: the location where the current route component is displayed.

The pages. The list of doctors generates links with parameters:

<!-- 13-router/src/views/ListeMedecins.vue - links with parameters -->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { RouterLink } from 'vue-router';
import { MEDECINS } from '../donnees';
</script>

<template>
  <ul class="mb-0">
    <li v-for="m in MEDECINS" :key="m.id">
       <!-- { name, params }: the router generates the address /doctors/2 itself -->
      <RouterLink :to="{ name: 'medecin', params: { id: m.id } }">{{ m.titre }} {{ m.prenom }} {{ m.nom }}</RouterLink>
    </li>
  </ul>
</template>
  • line 11: the router itself constructs the address [/medecins/2] from the route name and its parameters.

A doctor’s page:

<!--
  13-routeur/src/views/DetailMedecin.vue - une page à paramètre
  L'id arrive en PROP (props: true dans router.ts), sous forme de chaîne.
  useRouter() donne le routeur lui-même, pour naviguer PAR LE CODE.
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed } from 'vue';
import { useRouter } from 'vue-router';
import { MEDECINS } from '../donnees';

const props = defineProps<{ id: string }>();
const router = useRouter();

// computed: if you navigate from /doctors/1 to /doctors/2, the RÉUTILISE view
// same component and only changes the prop—the computed follows
const medecin = computed(() => MEDECINS.find((m) => m.id === Number(props.id)) ?? null);
const suivant = computed(() => (Number(props.id) % MEDECINS.length) + 1);
</script>

<template>
  <div v-if="medecin">
    <h2 class="h5">{{ medecin.titre }} {{ medecin.prenom }} {{ medecin.nom }}</h2>
    <p>Spécialité : {{ medecin.specialite }}</p>
    <div class="d-flex gap-2">
       <!-- navigation via code: router.push(...) or router.back() -->
      <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" @click="router.back()">Retour</button>
      <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary" @click="router.push({ name: 'medecin', params: { id: suivant } })">Médecin suivant</button>
    </div>
  </div>
  <p v-else class="text-danger mb-0">Le médecin n° {{ id }} n'existe pas.</p>
</template>
  • Line 11: The parameter [:id] is passed as a prop, in string form;
  • line 12: the router itself, to navigate through the code;
  • line 16: switching from [/medecins/1] to [/medecins/2] does not recreate the component: [Vue.js] reuses the one that is displayed and only changes its prop. A [computed] follows this change; code placed in [onMounted] would, however, be executed only once;
  • lines 26 and 27: return to the previous page, go to another page.

The search is a page entirely described by its URL, just like the GET form from the [NestJS] course:

<!--
  13-routeur/src/views/Recherche.vue - une page pilotée par la QUERY de l'URL
  (/recherche?q=pédiatre). Comme avec le formulaire GET du cours NestJS, la
  page est entièrement décrite par son adresse : on peut la mettre en
  favori, la recharger, revenir en arrière.
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, ref, watch } from 'vue';
import { useRoute, useRouter } from 'vue-router';
import { MEDECINS } from '../donnees';

const route = useRoute();
const router = useRouter();

// the input field starts with the value from URL...
const saisie = ref(String(route.query.q ?? ''));
// ... and follows the URL if it changes (e.g., by clicking the Back button)
watch(() => route.query.q, (q) => (saisie.value = String(q ?? '')));

const resultats = computed(() => {
  const q = String(route.query.q ?? '').toLowerCase();
  return MEDECINS.filter((m) => `${m.prenom} ${m.nom} ${m.specialite}`.toLowerCase().includes(q));
});

function rechercher(): void {
   // The URL is changed; the display updates to match the URL (computed above)
  router.push({ name: 'recherche', query: { q: saisie.value } });
}
</script>

<template>
  <form class="d-flex gap-2 mb-3" @submit.prevent="rechercher">
    <input v-model="saisie" class="form-control" placeholder="nom ou spécialité">
    <button class="btn btn-primary">Rechercher</button>
  </form>
  <ul class="mb-0">
    <li v-for="m in resultats" :key="m.id">{{ m.prenom }} {{ m.nom }} ({{ m.specialite }})</li>
  </ul>
</template>
  • line 16: [route.query] contains the parameters of URL ([?q=...]);
  • line 18: if URL changes (Previous button), the field follows;
  • line 20: the results depend on URL, not on the field;
  • line 27: searching changes the URL; the display updates accordingly. You can bookmark the search, reload it, or go back.

docs.title: 4.2. Example 14: Navigation Restrictions
docs.text:
Some pages require you to be logged in, while others require a specific role. This example simulates a login without a server:

// =========================================================================
// 14-gardes/src/session.ts - a SIMULÉE session (without a server)
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The logged-in user, in a reference declared at the MODULE level: all
// files that import this module share the same one. (Example 15 will
// do the same thing, but better, with Pinia; Example 18 uses a real server.)
// =========================================================================

import { ref } from 'vue';

export type Role = 'ADMIN' | 'DOCTOR' | 'USER';

export interface Utilisateur {
  login: string;
  role: Role;
}

export const utilisateur = ref<Utilisateur | null>(null);

// three "hard-coded" accounts (password = login)
const COMPTES: Record<string, Role> = { admin: 'ADMIN', pelissier: 'DOCTOR', martin: 'USER' };

export function connecter(login: string, password: string): boolean {
  const role = COMPTES[login];
  if (role === undefined || password !== login) {
    return false;
  }
  utilisateur.value = { login, role };
  return true;
}

export function deconnecter(): void {
  utilisateur.value = null;
}
  • Line 18: a [ref] declared at the module level: all files that import [session.ts] share the same one.

The routes and their margins:

// =========================================================================
// 14-gardes/src/router.ts - routes PROTÉGÉES
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// meta: free information attached to a route. Here:
//    - meta.connexion: the page requires you to be logged in;
//    - meta.role    s : authorized roles (none = all).
//
// router.beforeEach(...): a GARDE DE NAVIGATION, executed before CHAQUE
// page change. It returns:
//    - tru               e : navigation continues;
//    - a different addr  ess : redirection;
// This is the client-side equivalent of the checks NestJS (JwtAuthGuard,
// RolesGuard) — with one difference: FONDAMENTALE. A client guard is
// merely a convenience. The client code is in the hands of the user, who
// can change it at will. True data protection remains that
// provided by the SERVEUR (see the chapter on the black box).
// =========================================================================

import { createRouter, createWebHashHistory } from 'vue-router';
import { utilisateur, type Role } from './session';
import Accueil from './views/Accueil.vue';
import Connexion from './views/Connexion.vue';
import Agenda from './views/Agenda.vue';

// we declare the meta properties we use to TypeScript
declare module 'vue-router' {
  interface RouteMeta {
    connexion?: boolean;
    roles?: Role[];
  }
}

export const router = createRouter({
  history: createWebHashHistory(),
  routes: [
    { path: '/', component: Accueil },
    { path: '/connexion', component: Connexion },
    { path: '/agenda', component: Agenda, meta: { connexion: true } },
    {
      path: '/administration',
       // loading DIFFÉRÉ: the code for this component is only downloaded
       // on the first visit to the page (Vite actually creates a separate file)
      component: () => import('./views/Administration.vue'),
      meta: { connexion: true, roles: ['ADMIN'] },
    },
  ],
});

router.beforeEach((vers) => {
  if (vers.meta.connexion && utilisateur.value === null) {
     // not logged in: on the login page, remembering where you wanted to go
    return { path: '/connexion', query: { redirect: vers.fullPath } };
  }
  if (vers.meta.roles && utilisateur.value && !vers.meta.roles.includes(utilisateur.value.role)) {
     // logged in, but not with the correct role: redirect to the home page, with a reason
    return { path: '/', query: { refus: vers.fullPath } };
  }
  return true;
});
  • Lines 26–31: We declare in [TypeScript] the properties that we will store in the [meta] field of the routes. [meta] accepts arbitrary data; declaring these properties allows them to be used without type casting;
  • line 38: the page requires the user to be logged in;
  • line 43: deferred loading: the code for this component is downloaded only on the first visit to the page. [Vite] stores it in a separate file. This way, an application loads only what it needs at startup;
  • Lines 49–59: a navigation guard, executed before CHAQUE a page change. It returns [true] to allow access, or another address to redirect to:
    • not logged in: redirects to [/connexion], retaining the requested page in the [redirect] parameter;
    • logged in without the correct role: returns to the home page, with the reason for denial.

The login page redirects the user to where they wanted to go:

<!--
  14-gardes/src/views/Connexion.vue
  Après la connexion, on renvoie l'utilisateur à la page qu'il voulait
  ouvrir (paramètre ?redirect=... déposé par le garde), ou à l'accueil.
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { useRoute, useRouter } from 'vue-router';
import { connecter } from '../session';

const route = useRoute();
const router = useRouter();
const login = ref('');
const password = ref('');
const erreur = ref(false);

function valider(): void {
  erreur.value = !connecter(login.value.trim(), password.value);
  if (!erreur.value) {
    const redirect = route.query.redirect;
     // only a path like INTERNE is accepted: it starts with /, but not with //
     // (//site.com/... refers to a AUTRE site) — no redirection to another site
    const interne = typeof redirect === 'string' && redirect.startsWith('/') && !redirect.startsWith('//');
    router.push(interne ? redirect : '/');
  }
}
</script>

<template>
  <p v-if="route.query.redirect" class="alert alert-warning">Connectez-vous pour ouvrir {{ route.query.redirect }}.</p>
  <form class="d-flex flex-wrap gap-2" @submit.prevent="valider">
    <input v-model="login" class="form-control w-auto" placeholder="login" autocomplete="username">
    <input v-model="password" type="password" class="form-control w-auto" placeholder="mot de passe" autocomplete="current-password">
    <button class="btn btn-primary">Se connecter</button>
  </form>
  <p v-if="erreur" class="text-danger mt-2 mb-0">Login ou mot de passe incorrect.</p>
</template>
  • Line 23: Only a path like INTERNE is accepted: it starts with [/], but not with [//] ([//site.com/...] refers to a AUTRE site). Redirecting to a full URL received in the URL would allow a malicious link to send the user, immediately after logging in, to another site imitating ours (a vulnerability known as [open redirect]).

The other files are very short:

<script setup lang="ts">
import { RouterLink, RouterView, useRouter } from 'vue-router';
import { deconnecter, utilisateur } from './session';

const router = useRouter();

function seDeconnecter(): void {
  deconnecter();
  router.push('/');
}
</script>

<template>
  <div class="container py-4" style="max-width: 720px">
    <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Exemple 14 - les gardes de navigation</h1>
    <nav class="d-flex gap-3 align-items-center mb-3">
      <RouterLink to="/">Accueil</RouterLink>
      <RouterLink to="/agenda">Agenda (connecté)</RouterLink>
      <RouterLink to="/administration">Administration (ADMIN)</RouterLink>
      <span class="ms-auto">
        <template v-if="utilisateur">
          {{ utilisateur.login }} <span class="badge text-bg-primary">{{ utilisateur.role }}</span>
          <button class="btn btn-sm btn-link" @click="seDeconnecter">déconnexion</button>
        </template>
        <RouterLink v-else to="/connexion">connexion</RouterLink>
      </span>
    </nav>
    <div class="card p-3"><RouterView /></div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup lang="ts">
import { useRoute } from 'vue-router';
const route = useRoute();
</script>

<template>
   <!-- ?refus=...: submitted by the guard when the role is inappropriate -->
  <p v-if="route.query.refus" class="alert alert-danger">Votre rôle ne permet pas d'ouvrir {{ route.query.refus }}.</p>
  <p class="mb-0">Page publique. Essayez les deux autres liens, connecté ou non (admin, pelissier, martin - mot de passe = login).</p>
</template>

Clicking on “Administration (ADMIN)” while not logged in takes you to the login page:

When logged in with the account [martin] (role [USER]), the guard denies access to the administration page:

A note on FONDAMENTAL: a navigation guard is merely a convenience (to avoid displaying an unnecessary page). The client-side code is in the user’s hands; they can read and modify it in their browser. True data protection comes from the server, which verifies the user’s identity and role with every request. We’ll see this with the [RdvMedecins] server.

docs.title: 5.1. Example 15: Shared State with Pinia
docs.text:
In an application, certain data is relevant to many components: the logged-in user, the shopping cart, etc. Example 11 shared this data with [provide] / [inject], while Example 14 used a [ref] module. [Pinia], the official library for [Vue.js] for shared state, organizes this into stores and makes them visible in the [Vue.js devtools] extension.

It is installed in [main.ts]:

// =========================================================================
// 15-pinia/src/main.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// app.use(createPinia()) : Pinia, the official library for
// PARTAGÉ state management library from Vue.js. The "stores" (magazines) that we define
// can then be accessed from any component.
// =========================================================================

import { createApp } from 'vue';
import { createPinia } from 'pinia';
import 'bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css';
import App from './App.vue';

createApp(App).use(createPinia()).mount('#app');

The first store, the shopping cart:

// =========================================================================
// 15-pinia/src/stores/panier.ts - a STORE Pinia
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// defineStore('cart', () => { ... }): a store written as a composable
// (style "setup"):
//    - the refs are the ÉTAT of the store;
//    - the computed properties, its GETTERS (computed values);
//    - the functions, which are ACTIONS (what changes the state).
// Difference from a composable (Example 11): the store exists only as a single instance (UN
// instance for the entire application. All components that call
// usePanierStore() receive the MÊME shopping cart. It persists as long as the application
// is alive: it survives the removal of a component... but not the reloading of
// the page (F5), which restarts the application.
// =========================================================================

import { computed, ref } from 'vue';
import { defineStore } from 'pinia';

export interface Article {
  libelle: string;
  prix: number;
}

export const usePanierStore = defineStore('panier', () => {
  const articles = ref<Article[]>([]);

  const nombre = computed(() => articles.value.length);
  const total = computed(() => articles.value.reduce((s, a) => s + a.prix, 0));

  function ajouter(article: Article): void {
    articles.value.push(article);
  }
  function vider(): void {
    articles.value = [];
  }

   // Everything that is returned is part of the store
  return { articles, nombre, total, ajouter, vider };
});
  • lines 24–39: [defineStore(nom, fonction)] defines a store in the “setup” style, like a composable: the [ref] are its state, the [computed] are its getters, and the functions are its actions; it exposes what the function returns;
  • The difference from a composable: there is only one instance of the store for the entire application. All components that call [usePanierStore()] receive the MÊME shopping cart. It lives as long as the application lives: it survives the removal of a component... but not a page reload (F5), which restarts the application.

A second store, however, survives the page reload:

// =========================================================================
// 15-pinia/src/stores/preferences.ts—a store that survives F5
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// For data to survive a page reload or when the
// the browser, it must be stored DANS in the browser: localStorage (a
// small key-to-string dictionary, unique to each site).
//    - on startup, the store re-reads localStorage;
//    - `watch(..., { deep: true })` rewrites `localStorage` with every change.
// No sensitive data (passwords, tokens) is stored there: any script
// on the page can read localStorage.
// =========================================================================

import { ref, watch } from 'vue';
import { defineStore } from 'pinia';

const CLE = 'exemple15.preferences';

interface Preferences {
  sombre: boolean;
  taille: number; // text size, in px
}

function lire(): Preferences {
  try {
    return { sombre: false, taille: 16, ...JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(CLE) ?? '{}') };
  } catch {
    return { sombre: false, taille: 16 }; // unreadable content: default values
  }
}

export const usePreferencesStore = defineStore('preferences', () => {
  const preferences = ref<Preferences>(lire());

  watch(preferences, (p) => localStorage.setItem(CLE, JSON.stringify(p)), { deep: true });

  return { preferences };
});
  • Lines 23–29: Upon startup, the browser re-reads [localStorage], a small key/value dictionary that the browser stores for each site, even after the browser is closed. If the content is unreadable, the default values are used;
  • Line 34: [{ deep: true }]: [watch] also reacts to changes in the object’s properties. Each change is rewritten to [localStorage].

Do not store sensitive data (passwords, tokens) in JAMAIS: any script executed on the page can read [localStorage].

The components:

<!-- 15-pinia/src/components/Boutique.vue - AJOUTE to the shared cart -->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { usePanierStore, type Article } from '../stores/panier';

const panier = usePanierStore();
const produits: Article[] = [
  { libelle: 'Consultation', prix: 30 },
  { libelle: 'Vaccin', prix: 12.5 },
];
</script>

<template>
  <div class="card p-3 h-100">
    <h2 class="h6">Boutique</h2>
    <button v-for="p in produits" :key="p.libelle" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary mb-2" @click="panier.ajouter(p)">
      + {{ p.libelle }} ({{ p.prix }} €)
    </button>
  </div>
</template>
  • Line 5: The store is used as a reactive object: [panier.ajouter(p)];
<!--
  15-pinia/src/components/ResumePanier.vue - LIT le même panier
  storeToRefs : pour DÉSTRUCTURER un store sans perdre la réactivité
  (const { nombre } = panier donnerait une simple copie, figée).
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { storeToRefs } from 'pinia';
import { usePanierStore } from '../stores/panier';

const panier = usePanierStore();
const { nombre, total } = storeToRefs(panier);
</script>

<template>
  <div class="card p-3 h-100">
    <h2 class="h6">Panier</h2>
    <p class="mb-2">{{ nombre }} article(s), {{ total }} €</p>
     <!-- actions, on the other hand, are deconstructed or called directly -->
    <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger align-self-start" :disabled="nombre === 0" @click="panier.vider()">Vider</button>
  </div>
</template>
  • line 11: to unpack a store without losing reactivity. [const { nombre } = panier] would return a simple copy, frozen at the current value; [storeToRefs] returns [ref] instances linked to the store. Actions, on the other hand, are either unbound or called directly.
<!-- 15-pinia/src/components/CompteurLocal.vue - a state LOCAL, which disappears with the component -->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
const clics = ref(0);
</script>

<template>
  <div class="card p-3 h-100">
    <h2 class="h6">État local</h2>
    <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary align-self-start" @click="clics++">{{ clics }} clic(s)</button>
  </div>
</template>

<!--
  =========================================================================
  15-pinia/src/App.vue - trois "portées" de données côté client
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Même question que l'exemple 23 du cours NestJS (portée application,
  requête, client), transposée dans le navigateur :
    - l'état LOCAL d'un composant (CompteurLocal) disparaît avec lui ;
    - l'état d'un STORE (le panier) est partagé par tous les composants et
      survit à leur retrait - mais pas à F5 ;
    - l'état rangé dans localStorage (les préférences) survit à F5 et à la
      fermeture du navigateur.
  Décochez puis recochez la case, puis rechargez la page : comparez.
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { usePreferencesStore } from './stores/preferences';
import Boutique from './components/Boutique.vue';
import ResumePanier from './components/ResumePanier.vue';
import CompteurLocal from './components/CompteurLocal.vue';

const prefs = usePreferencesStore();
const zoneVisible = ref(true);
</script>

<template>
  <div :class="{ 'bg-dark text-light': prefs.preferences.sombre }" :style="{ fontSize: prefs.preferences.taille + 'px' }" class="min-vh-100">
    <div class="container py-4">
      <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Exemple 15 - un état partagé avec Pinia</h1>
      <div class="d-flex flex-wrap gap-4 mb-3">
        <label class="form-check-label"><input v-model="prefs.preferences.sombre" type="checkbox" class="form-check-input"> thème sombre</label>
        <label>taille du texte <input v-model.number="prefs.preferences.taille" type="range" min="12" max="22"> {{ prefs.preferences.taille }} px</label>
        <label class="form-check-label"><input v-model="zoneVisible" type="checkbox" class="form-check-input"> afficher la zone</label>
      </div>
      <div v-if="zoneVisible" class="row g-3 text-body">
        <div class="col-md-4"><Boutique /></div>
        <div class="col-md-4"><ResumePanier /></div>
        <div class="col-md-4"><CompteurLocal /></div>
      </div>
      <p class="mt-3 mb-2">Hors de la zone, un second résumé du MÊME panier (il reste là quand la zone disparaît) :</p>
      <div class="text-body"><ResumePanier /></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>
  • Line 35: Unchecking “Show Zone” removes the three components from the page;
  • line 41: a second summary of the same shopping cart, outside the area.

Same question as Example 23 from course [NestJS] (application, query, and client scopes), adapted for the browser:

DataWhere?LifetimeThe counter for CompteurLocalthe component's local statedisappears along with the componentthe shopping cartA Pinia blindthe entire application, up to F5preferencesa Pinia store + localStoragesurvives F5 and browser closure

Two items added and two clicks:

The section was removed and the dark theme was selected: the shopping cart is still there; if the section is displayed again, the local counter resets to zero:

docs.title: 3. The Components
docs.text: So far, each example has fit into a single component, [App.vue]. A real application contains dozens of them: a navigation bar, forms, windows... Each component is a self-contained piece of the interface (its HTML, its code, its style) and is reusable. This chapter shows how components fit together and communicate.

docs.title: 3.1. Example 07: Components and Their Props
docs.text:
The example displays one card per doctor. The card is a component, [CarteMedecin.vue], used three times by its parent, [App.vue].

The doctor type, shared by both components, is in a regular file named [TypeScript]:

// the data type shared by the parent (App.vue) and the child (CarteMedecin.vue)
export interface Medecin {
  id: number;
  titre: string;
  prenom: string;
  nom: string;
  specialite: string;
  disponible: boolean;
}

The child component:

<!--
  =========================================================================
  07-composants/src/components/CarteMedecin.vue - un composant ENFANT
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Il reçoit ses données de son parent par des PROPS (propriétés), déclarées
  avec defineProps. Le type TypeScript des props est vérifié à la
  compilation : <CarteMedecin :medecin="42"> serait refusé.

  Règle d'or : un composant ne MODIFIE JAMAIS ses props. Les données
  descendent du parent vers l'enfant ("one-way data flow") ; pour
  demander un changement, l'enfant émet un événement (cf. exemple 08).
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed } from 'vue';
import type { Medecin } from '../medecin';

// withDefaults: a default value for optional props (?)
const props = withDefaults(
  defineProps<{
    medecin: Medecin;
    rang: number;
    compact?: boolean;
  }>(),
  { compact: false },
);

// A computed property based on a prop: recalculated if the parent changes the prop
const initiales = computed(() => `${props.medecin.prenom[0]}${props.medecin.nom[0]}`);
</script>

<template>
  <div class="card h-100" :class="{ 'border-success': medecin.disponible }">
    <div class="card-body d-flex gap-3 align-items-center">
      <div class="initiales">{{ initiales }}</div>
      <div>
         <!-- In the template, props are used directly by name -->
        <h2 class="h6 mb-1">{{ rang }}. {{ medecin.titre }} {{ medecin.prenom }} {{ medecin.nom }}</h2>
        <p v-if="!compact" class="mb-0 text-muted small">{{ medecin.specialite }}</p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
.initiales {
  width: 2.5rem;
  height: 2.5rem;
  border-radius: 50%;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  background: #0d6efd;
  color: white;
  font-weight: bold;
}
</style>
  • Line 16: [import type] imports only one type: nothing from this import remains in the resulting [JavaScript];
  • Lines 19–26: [defineProps<{...}>()] declares the component’s props—that is, the data it receives from its parent—along with their types. A prop followed by [?] is optional; [withDefaults] gives it a default value. [defineProps] does not need to be imported: it is a “macro” recognized by the [.vue] file compiler;
  • Line 29: In the script, the props are read via the [props] object. [computed] tracks the props: if the parent changes the assigned doctor, the initials are recalculated;
  • line 38: In the template, props are used directly by name;
  • line 39: a prop can modify the display.

The parent:

<!--
  =========================================================================
  07-composants/src/App.vue - le composant PARENT
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Il importe le composant CarteMedecin et l'utilise comme une nouvelle
  balise HTML, <CarteMedecin>, autant de fois qu'il le faut : un composant
  est un morceau d'interface RÉUTILISABLE, avec ses propres données, son
  template et son style.
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
// In <script setup>, an imported component is immediately available in the template
import CarteMedecin from './components/CarteMedecin.vue';
import type { Medecin } from './medecin';

const medecins = ref<Medecin[]>([
  { id: 1, titre: 'Mme', prenom: 'Marie', nom: 'PELISSIER', specialite: 'généraliste', disponible: true },
  { id: 2, titre: 'Mr', prenom: 'Paul', nom: 'TATOU', specialite: 'pédiatre', disponible: false },
  { id: 3, titre: 'Melle', prenom: 'Sophie', nom: 'DUPONT', specialite: 'généraliste', disponible: true },
]);
const compact = ref(false);

// the parent modifies SES data: the affected children are updated
function inverserDisponibilite(): void {
  for (const m of medecins.value) {
    m.disponible = !m.disponible;
  }
}
</script>

<template>
  <div class="container py-4">
    <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Exemple 07 - les composants et leurs props</h1>
    <div class="d-flex gap-3 mb-3">
      <label class="form-check-label"><input v-model="compact" type="checkbox" class="form-check-input"> affichage compact</label>
      <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary" @click="inverserDisponibilite">Inverser les disponibilités</button>
    </div>
    <div class="row g-3">
      <div v-for="(m, i) in medecins" :key="m.id" class="col-md-4">
         <!-- :medecin="m" passes the OBJET m (an expression);
             compact, sans deux-points, transmettrait la CHAÎNE "compact" -->
        <CarteMedecin :medecin="m" :rang="i + 1" :compact="compact" />
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>
  • line 14: in [<script setup>], an imported component is immediately usable in the template, like a new tag;
  • line 43: Each card receives the doctor SON. [:medecin="m"] (with a colon) passes the value of the expression [m]; without the colon, the character string ["m"] would be passed, which [TypeScript] would reject here. Component tag names are written as [PascalCase] to distinguish them from HTML tags;
  • lines 25–29: the parent modifies SES data; the affected maps update.

The golden rule: a component never modifies its own props. Data flows from the parent to the child ([one-way data flow]): the parent owns it. To request a change, the child emits an event, which the parent processes: this is the subject of the following example.

docs.title: 3.2.1. Triggering an Event
docs.text:
The [Compteur] component notifies its parent every time its button is clicked:

<!--
  =========================================================================
  08-evenements-composants/src/components/Compteur.vue
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Un enfant qui PRÉVIENT son parent : defineEmits déclare les événements
  qu'il peut émettre, avec le type de leurs données. Le parent les écoute
  comme des événements HTML : <Compteur @change="..." @limite="...">.
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';

const props = defineProps<{ libelle: string; max: number }>();

// two events: 'change' (with the new value) and 'limit' (without data)
const emit = defineEmits<{
  change: [valeur: number];
  limite: [];
}>();

const valeur = ref(0);

function plus(): void {
  if (valeur.value >= props.max) {
    emit('limite');
    return;
  }
  valeur.value++;
  emit('change', valeur.value);
}
</script>

<template>
  <div class="d-flex align-items-center gap-2 mb-2">
    <span class="w-25">{{ libelle }}</span>
    <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary" @click="plus">+1</button>
    <span class="badge text-bg-secondary">{{ valeur }} / {{ max }}</span>
  </div>
</template>
  • Lines 16–19: [defineEmits] declares the events that the component can trigger, along with their data types: [change] carries a number, [limite] carries nothing;
  • Lines 25 and 29: Emitting an event. [TypeScript] verifies the event name and its data type;
  • Line 21: The child is allowed to have its own state: [valeur] belongs to it, not to the parent.

docs.title: 3.2.2. v-model on a component
docs.text:
The component [ChampTexte] is a “custom” form field: a label, the field itself, a tooltip, and a character counter. We want to use it with [v-model], just like a regular [<input>]:

<!--
  =========================================================================
  08-evenements-composants/src/components/ChampTexte.vue
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Un champ de formulaire "maison" (libellé + champ + aide + compteur de
  caractères) qui accepte v-model, comme un <input> ordinaire :
      <ChampTexte v-model="nom" libelle="Nom" :max="20" />

  defineModel() crée une ref reliée au v-model du parent : la LIRE donne la
  valeur du parent, l'ÉCRIRE émet l'événement 'update:modelValue', que le
  parent traite en mettant à jour sa donnée. Les données restent donc bien
  la propriété du parent.
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useId } from 'vue';

const modele = defineModel<string>({ required: true });
defineProps<{ libelle: string; max: number; aide?: string }>();

// a unique identifier per instance, to link <label for> and <input id>
const id = useId();
</script>

<template>
  <div class="mb-3">
    <label class="form-label" :for="id">{{ libelle }}</label>
     <!-- v-model="model": the native field is linked to the ref of defineModel -->
    <input :id="id" v-model="modele" class="form-control" :maxlength="max" :class="{ 'is-invalid': modele.length === max }">
    <div class="form-text">{{ aide }} ({{ modele.length }} / {{ max }})</div>
  </div>
</template>
  • Line 18: [defineModel] creates a [ref] linked to the parent’s [v-model]. Reading it returns the parent’s value; writing to it triggers the [update:modelValue] event, which the parent handles by modifying the given SA. [v-model="nom"] on a component is simply a shortcut for the [modelValue] property and this event: the data remains the property of the parent;
  • line 22: [useId()] provides a unique identifier per component instance: the two [ChampTexte] instances on the page will not have the same [id], and each [<label for>] correctly refers to the SON field;
  • Line 29: The native field is linked to the [ref] from [defineModel].

docs.title: 3.2.3. The parent
docs.text:
<!--
  =========================================================================
  08-evenements-composants/src/App.vue - le parent écoute ses enfants
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Deux façons pour un enfant de faire remonter une information :
    1. émettre un événement, que le parent écoute avec @ (Compteur) ;
    2. v-model sur un composant (ChampTexte) : un raccourci pour la prop
       modelValue + l'événement update:modelValue.
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, ref } from 'vue';
import Compteur from './components/Compteur.vue';
import ChampTexte from './components/ChampTexte.vue';

const total = ref(0);
const message = ref('');
const prenom = ref('Marie');
const nom = ref('PELISSIER');
const nomComplet = computed(() => `${prenom.value} ${nom.value.toUpperCase()}`);

// the 'change' event handler: it receives the data sent
function surChange(libelle: string, valeur: number): void {
  total.value++;
  message.value = `${libelle} vaut maintenant ${valeur}`;
}
</script>

<template>
  <div class="container py-4" style="max-width: 640px">
    <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Exemple 08 - événements et v-model sur un composant</h1>

    <div class="card p-3 mb-4">
      <h2 class="h6">1. Des événements émis par les enfants</h2>
      <Compteur libelle="Cafés" :max="3" @change="(v) => surChange('Cafés', v)" @limite="message = 'Pas plus de 3 cafés !'" />
      <Compteur libelle="Verres d'eau" :max="8" @change="(v) => surChange(`Verres d'eau`, v)" @limite="message = 'Assez bu.'" />
      <p class="mb-0">Total des clics : {{ total }} - <em>{{ message }}</em></p>
    </div>

    <div class="card p-3">
      <h2 class="h6">2. v-model sur un composant</h2>
      <ChampTexte v-model="prenom" libelle="Prénom" :max="20" aide="Obligatoire" />
      <ChampTexte v-model="nom" libelle="Nom" :max="20" aide="Mis en majuscules à l'affichage" />
      <p class="mb-0">Données du parent : <strong>{{ nomComplet }}</strong></p>
      <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary mt-2 align-self-start" @click="prenom = ''; nom = ''">Vider (depuis le parent)</button>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>
  • Line 35: The parent listens for events from its children using [@], just like HTML events. The arrowed function [(v) => surChange('Cafés', v)] receives the event data; [@limite] executes a single instruction;
  • line 42: [v-model] on a component;
  • line 45: when PARENT empties its data, the fields follow: the link works both ways.

docs.title: 3.3. Example 09: Templates and Slots
docs.text:
Props pass data; slots pass content: from HTML, other components. The [Carte] component sets the frame (border, header, footer), and its parent determines what goes inside it:

<!--
  =========================================================================
  09-slots/src/components/Carte.vue - un GABARIT réutilisable
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Les props transmettent des DONNÉES ; les slots transmettent du CONTENU
  (du HTML, d'autres composants). Carte fixe le cadre (bordure, en-tête,
  pied), le parent fournit ce qu'il y a dedans :
    - <slot />              le slot par défaut : le contenu "principal" ;
    - <slot name="entete">  un slot nommé, rempli par <template #header> ;
    - le texte placé ENTRE <slot> et </slot> est affiché si le parent ne
      fournit rien (contenu par défaut).
  C'est l'équivalent, côté client, du gabarit layout.hbs et de son {{{body}}}
  dans le cours NestJS.
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
defineProps<{ couleur?: 'primary' | 'success' | 'danger' }>();
</script>

<template>
  <div class="card mb-3" :class="couleur ? `border-${couleur}` : ''">
    <div class="card-header" :class="couleur ? `text-bg-${couleur}` : ''">
      <slot name="entete">Sans titre</slot>
    </div>
    <div class="card-body">
      <slot />
    </div>
     <!-- $slots.footer: Did the parent provide a footer? If not, no empty <div> -->
    <div v-if="$slots.pied" class="card-footer text-muted small">
      <slot name="pied" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>
  • line 23: a named slot; the text between [<slot>] and [</slot>] is displayed if the parent provides nothing;
  • line 26: the default slot: the “main” content;
  • line 29: [$slots] specifies which slots the parent has filled: without a footer, there is no empty [<div>].

This is the client-side equivalent of the [layout.hbs] template and its [{{{body}}}] in the [NestJS] course.

A second component, [Tableau], displays lines of any type:

<!--
  =========================================================================
  09-slots/src/components/Tableau.vue - un tableau GÉNÉRIQUE, à slot "scopé"
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  generic="T" : un composant générique, comme une classe générique
  TypeScript - il affiche des lignes de n'importe quel type T.

  Le tableau sait parcourir les lignes, mais pas comment afficher une
  ligne : il PASSE chaque ligne à son slot (<slot name="ligne" :ligne="l">),
  et c'est le parent qui dit quoi en faire (<template #line="{ line }">).
  On parle de slot "scopé" : le contenu fourni par le parent utilise des
  données qui appartiennent à l'enfant.
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts" generic="T extends { id: number }">
defineProps<{ lignes: T[]; colonnes: string[] }>();
</script>

<template>
  <table class="table table-sm align-middle mb-0">
    <thead>
      <tr><th v-for="c in colonnes" :key="c">{{ c }}</th></tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr v-for="(l, i) in lignes" :key="l.id">
        <slot name="ligne" :ligne="l" :index="i" />
      </tr>
      <tr v-if="lignes.length === 0">
        <td :colspan="colonnes.length" class="text-muted"><slot name="vide">Aucune donnée.</slot></td>
      </tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
</template>
  • line 15: a generic component, such as a generic class [TypeScript]: [T] is the type of the lines, for which only one property is required: [id] (for the key of [v-for]);
  • Line 26: The array knows how to iterate through the lines, but not how to display a line. It passes each line to its slot, and the parent displays it. This is referred to as a “scoped” slot: the content provided by the parent uses data that belongs to the child.

The parent:

<!--
  =========================================================================
  09-slots/src/App.vue - utiliser les gabarits Carte et Tableau
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
import Carte from './components/Carte.vue';
import Tableau from './components/Tableau.vue';

interface Creneau {
  id: number;
  horaire: string;
  patient: string | null;
}

const creneaux = ref<Creneau[]>([
  { id: 1, horaire: '8:00 - 8:20', patient: null },
  { id: 2, horaire: '8:20 - 8:40', patient: 'Mme Alice DURAND' },
  { id: 3, horaire: '8:40 - 9:00', patient: null },
]);
</script>

<template>
  <div class="container py-4" style="max-width: 720px">
    <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Exemple 09 - gabarits et slots</h1>

     <!-- #header is short for v-slot:header -->
    <Carte couleur="primary">
      <template #header>Ms. PELISSIER's Calendar</template>
       <!-- the default slot: everything that is not inside a <template #...> -->
      <Tableau :lignes="creneaux" :colonnes="['#', 'Créneau', 'Statut']">
         <!-- we retrieve the data passed by the Table: { row, index } -->
        <template #row="{ row, index }">
          <td>{{ index + 1 }}</td>
          <td>{{ ligne.horaire }}</td>
          <td>
            <span v-if="ligne.patient" class="badge text-bg-secondary">{{ ligne.patient }}</span>
            <span v-else class="badge text-bg-success">Libre</span>
          </td>
        </template>
      </Tableau>
      <template #footer>{{ creneaux.filter((c) => c.patient === null).length }} available slot(s)</template>
    </Carte>

    <Carte couleur="success">
      <template #header>A map without a footer</template>
      <p class="mb-0">Le pied n'est pas fourni : la carte ne l'affiche pas.</p>
    </Carte>

    <Carte>
       <!-- No header provided: the slot’s default content, “Untitled” -->
      <Tableau :lignes="[]" :colonnes="['Nom']">
        <template #empty>No one at this time.</template>
      </Tableau>
    </Carte>
  </div>
</template>
  • line 30: [<template #entete>] (short for [v-slot:entete]) fills the slot named [entete];
  • line 32: anything not in a [<template #...>] goes into the default slot;
  • line 34: the data passed through the array is retrieved. Thanks to the generic component, [TypeScript] knows that [ligne] is a [Creneau];
  • line 51: a card without a header: the default content, “Untitled,” is displayed.

docs.title: 3.4. Example 10: The Lifecycle of a Component
docs.text:
A component is created, displayed, updated, and then removed. [Vue.js] allows code to be executed at each of these stages. The [Horloge] component:

<!--
  =========================================================================
  10-cycle-de-vie/src/components/Horloge.vue
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Le cycle de vie d'un composant :
    1. setup      : le code de <script setup> s'exécute (création) ;
    2. onMounted  : le composant est AFFICHÉ, ses éléments HTML existent ;
    3. onUpdated  : son affichage vient d'être mis à jour ;
    4. onUnmounted: le composant a été RETIRÉ de la page.
  Une horloge lance une minuterie (setInterval) à l'affichage... et doit
  impérativement l'arrêter quand elle disparaît : sinon la minuterie
  continuerait de tourner pour rien (fuite de mémoire).
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { onMounted, onUnmounted, ref } from 'vue';

const emit = defineEmits<{ journal: [message: string] }>();

const heure = ref(new Date().toLocaleTimeString());
let minuterie: number | undefined;

emit('journal', 'Horloge : setup (création)');

onMounted(() => {
  emit('journal', 'Horloge : onMounted - démarrage de la minuterie');
  minuterie = window.setInterval(() => {
    heure.value = new Date().toLocaleTimeString();
  }, 1000);
});

onUnmounted(() => {
  window.clearInterval(minuterie);
  emit('journal', 'Horloge : onUnmounted - minuterie arrêtée');
});
</script>

<template>
  <div class="display-6 font-monospace">{{ heure }}</div>
</template>
  • line 23: the code for [<script setup>] runs once when the component is created;
  • lines 25–30: [onMounted]: the component is displayed, and its HTML elements exist. The timer is started;
  • lines 32–35: [onUnmounted]: the component has been removed from the page. The timer must be stopped; otherwise, it would continue to run for a component that no longer exists (a “memory leak”).

The parent:

<!--
  =========================================================================
  10-cycle-de-vie/src/App.vue
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    - v-if sur <Horloge> : cocher / décocher la case crée / détruit le
      composant (onMounted / onUnmounted, cf. Horloge.vue) ;
    - une "template ref" : ref="champ" donne accès à l'élément HTML <input>
      lui-même, une fois le composant affiché (pour lui donner le focus) ;
    - watch avec { immediate: true } : exécuté tout de suite, puis à chaque
      changement ;
    - nextTick : attendre que Vue ait mis la page à jour.
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { nextTick, onMounted, ref, useTemplateRef, watch } from 'vue';
import Horloge from './components/Horloge.vue';

const avecHorloge = ref(true);
const journal = ref<string[]>([]);
const recherche = ref('');
const afficherRecherche = ref(false);

// the <input ref="field"> element in the template (null until it is displayed)
const champ = useTemplateRef<HTMLInputElement>('champ');

function tracer(message: string): void {
  journal.value.push(`${new Date().toLocaleTimeString()} ${message}`);
}

onMounted(() => tracer('App : onMounted'));

watch(
  recherche,
  (valeur) => {
    document.title = valeur ? `Recherche : ${valeur}` : 'Exemple 10';
  },
  { immediate: true },
);

async function ouvrirRecherche(): Promise<void> {
  afficherRecherche.value = true;
   // At this moment, the <input> does not yet exist: Vue will update the page
   // a little later. nextTick() is waiting for this update.
  await nextTick();
  champ.value?.focus();
}
</script>

<template>
  <div class="container py-4" style="max-width: 720px">
    <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Exemple 10 - le cycle de vie d'un composant</h1>

    <div class="card p-3 mb-3">
      <label class="form-check-label mb-2">
        <input v-model="avecHorloge" type="checkbox" class="form-check-input"> afficher l'horloge
      </label>
      <Horloge v-if="avecHorloge" @journal="tracer" />
    </div>

    <div class="card p-3 mb-3">
      <button v-if="!afficherRecherche" class="btn btn-outline-primary align-self-start" @click="ouvrirRecherche">
        Rechercher...
      </button>
      <input v-else ref="champ" v-model="recherche" class="form-control" placeholder="le titre de l'onglet suit la saisie">
    </div>

    <h2 class="h6">Journal</h2>
    <ol class="small">
      <li v-for="(ligne, i) in journal" :key="i">{{ ligne }}</li>
    </ol>
  </div>
</template>
  • Line 57: Checking and unchecking the box creates and destroys the clock: the log shows [setup], [onMounted], [onUnmounted];
  • Line 24: A template reference: The [ref="champ"] attribute of the [<input>] element provides access to the HTML element itself. It is equal to [null] as long as the element is not displayed;
  • lines 32–37: [watch] with [{ immediate: true }] runs immediately, then on every change: the tab title updates as text is entered;
  • lines 40–45: After [afficherRecherche.value = true], the field does not yet exist: [Vue.js] batches the page updates and performs them a little later. [await nextTick()] waits for this update; only then can focus be given to the field.

docs.title: 3.5. Example 11: Composables, provide, and inject
docs.text:
How can logic be shared between components? On the server side, [NestJS] had its services injected into the controllers. [Vue.js] has its composables: simple functions, whose names begin with [use], that combine reactive state and the accompanying code.

// =========================================================================
// 11-composables/src/composables/useHorloge.ts - a COMPOSABLE
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A composable is a simple function whose name begins with "use"
// by convention, which combines a reactive state ET with the corresponding logic
// (in this case: the timer, its start, and its stop). Any component that
// calls it gets SA its own timer, without having to duplicate the code.
//
// This is the way Vue.js to share logic between components—the
// role previously played, on the server side, by the NestJS services.
// =========================================================================

import { onMounted, onUnmounted, ref, type Ref } from 'vue';

export function useHorloge(periodeMs = 1000): { maintenant: Ref<Date> } {
  const maintenant = ref(new Date());
  let minuterie: number | undefined;

   // Lifecycle hooks attach to the component that APPELLE the composable
  onMounted(() => {
    minuterie = window.setInterval(() => (maintenant.value = new Date()), periodeMs);
  });
  onUnmounted(() => window.clearInterval(minuterie));

  return { maintenant };
}
  • line 15: the function returns an object containing [ref] [maintenant];
  • lines 20–22: The lifecycle functions called within a composable are attached to the component that calls the composable: each component has its own timer, which stops when the component is destroyed.

A second composable, without a lifecycle:

// =========================================================================
// 11-composables/src/composables/usePanier.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A second composable, SANS, with a lifecycle: a shopping cart (list of items,
// total, add, remove). Each call to usePanier() creates a NOUVEAU
// shopping cart: the two components that call it each have their own.
// (For a single PARTAGÉ shopping cart shared across the entire application, see provide / inject
// below, and Pinia in Example 15.)
// =========================================================================

import { computed, ref } from 'vue';

export interface Article {
  libelle: string;
  prix: number;
}

export function usePanier() {
  const articles = ref<Article[]>([]);
  const total = computed(() => articles.value.reduce((somme, a) => somme + a.prix, 0));

  function ajouter(article: Article): void {
    articles.value.push(article);
  }
  function retirer(index: number): void {
    articles.value.splice(index, 1);
  }

  return { articles, total, ajouter, retirer };
}

// the type of what usePanier returns: useful for provide / inject
export type Panier = ReturnType<typeof usePanier>;
  • line 19: each call to [usePanier()] creates a NOUVEAU shopping cart;
  • line 33: the type of what [usePanier] returns, inferred by [TypeScript].

To allow multiple components to share the LE and MÊME shopping carts, we use [provide] and [inject], a form of dependency injection:

// =========================================================================
// 11-composables/src/cles.ts - the keys for `provide` / `inject`
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// provide(key, value): a component MET assigns a value to
// all its descendants, regardless of their depth;
// inject(key): a descendant retrieves it—without the intermediate components
// having to pass it from props to props.
// This is a form of dependency injection, as in NestJS.
//
// A InjectionKey<T> (a typed Symbol) ensures that inject() returns a
// value of the correct type.
// =========================================================================

import type { InjectionKey } from 'vue';
import type { Panier } from './composables/usePanier';

export const CLE_PANIER: InjectionKey<Panier> = Symbol('panier');
  • Line 17: the key under which the shopping cart is provided: a [Symbol] (unique value) typed by [InjectionKey<Panier>], so that [inject] returns an object of the correct type.

The root component creates the shopping cart and provides it:

<!--
  =========================================================================
  11-composables/src/App.vue
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    - useHorloge() : App a son horloge (1 s), ResumePanier la sienne (5 s) ;
    - usePanier() + provide : App crée UN panier et le fournit à tous ses
      descendants ; Catalogue et ResumePanier l'injectent et partagent
      donc le même.
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { provide } from 'vue';
import { useHorloge } from './composables/useHorloge';
import { usePanier } from './composables/usePanier';
import { CLE_PANIER } from './cles';
import Catalogue from './components/Catalogue.vue';
import ResumePanier from './components/ResumePanier.vue';

const { maintenant } = useHorloge();
provide(CLE_PANIER, usePanier());
</script>

<template>
  <div class="container py-4" style="max-width: 720px">
    <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Exemple 11 - composables et provide / inject</h1>
    <p class="text-muted">Horloge de App : {{ maintenant.toLocaleTimeString() }}</p>
    <div class="row g-3">
      <div class="col-md-6"><Catalogue /></div>
      <div class="col-md-6"><ResumePanier /></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>
  • line 19: App has its own clock, refreshed every second;
  • line 20: The app makes a shopping cart available to TOUS and its descendants, regardless of their depth, without having to pass it from props to props.

Two descendants inject it:

<!--
  11-composables/src/components/Catalogue.vue - un descendant qui INJECTE le panier
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { inject } from 'vue';
import { CLE_PANIER } from '../cles';
import type { Article } from '../composables/usePanier';

// the basket provided by App.vue (provide); explicit error if missing
const panier = inject(CLE_PANIER);
if (!panier) {
  throw new Error('Catalogue doit être placé sous un composant qui fournit le panier');
}

const catalogue: Article[] = [
  { libelle: 'Consultation', prix: 30 },
  { libelle: 'Vaccin', prix: 12.5 },
  { libelle: 'Certificat', prix: 5 },
];
</script>

<template>
  <ul class="list-group">
    <li v-for="a in catalogue" :key="a.libelle" class="list-group-item d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center">
      {{ a.libelle }} ({{ a.prix }} €)
      <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary" @click="panier.ajouter(a)">Ajouter</button>
    </li>
  </ul>
</template>
  • line 10: The basket provided by an ancestor is retrieved; [inject] returns [undefined] if no ancestor has provided it: this is indicated by an explicit error.
<!--
  11-composables/src/components/ResumePanier.vue - un autre descendant, le MÊME panier
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { inject } from 'vue';
import { CLE_PANIER } from '../cles';
import { useHorloge } from '../composables/useHorloge';

const panier = inject(CLE_PANIER)!;
// this component has its own clock, SA, which refreshes every 5 seconds
const { maintenant } = useHorloge(5000);
</script>

<!-- panier.articles.value: in a template, Vue does not "unwrap" (.value
     implicite) que les ref de PREMIER niveau du script, comme maintenant.
     Les ref rangées DANS un objet (panier.articles) s'écrivent avec .value -->
<template>
  <div class="card p-3">
    <h2 class="h6">Panier ({{ panier.articles.value.length }} article(s)) - {{ maintenant.toLocaleTimeString() }}</h2>
    <ul class="mb-2">
      <li v-for="(a, i) in panier.articles.value" :key="i">
        {{ a.libelle }} <a href="#" @click.prevent="panier.retirer(i)">retirer</a>
      </li>
    </ul>
    <strong>Total : {{ panier.total.value }} €</strong>
  </div>
</template>
  • Line 9: Same injection; [!] confirms to [TypeScript] that the value exists;
  • line 11: this component has its own SA clock, refreshed every 5 seconds;
  • line 19: in a template, [Vue.js] automatically “unpacks” only the top-level [ref] elements of the script. A [ref] that contains a DANS object ([panier.articles]) is written as [.value].

Both components display the same shopping cart; the two clocks run at their own pace:

docs.title: 3.6. Example 12: A Reusable Confirmation Window
docs.text:
Before deleting an item, the system asks, “Are you sure?” The browser function [window.confirm()] exists, but its dialog box cannot be formatted, nor can its buttons be translated. We replace it with a [Bootstrap] window, controlled by a composable. This is the [Vue.js] version of Example 21 from the [NestJS] course.

// =========================================================================
// 12-confirmation/src/composables/useConfirmation.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// "Are you sure?": window.confirm() exists, but we can neither
// style it or translate its buttons. We replace it with a window
// Bootstrap window (FenetreConfirmation.vue), controlled by this composable.
//
// Tip: confirm(message) returns a PROMESSE, which evaluates to true (Yes)
// or false (No) when the user responds. The calling code is written
// just as simply as with window.confirm:
//
//      if (await confirm('Delete this doctor?'')) { ... }
//
// The state (displayed message, function to call upon response) is declared
// HORS of the function: it is therefore UNIQUE for the entire application. A
// A single window, created once in App.vue, serves all components.
// =========================================================================

import { readonly, ref } from 'vue';

const message = ref<string | null>(null); // null: window closed
let repondre: ((reponse: boolean) => void) | null = null;

export function useConfirmation() {
  function confirmer(texte: string): Promise<boolean> {
    message.value = texte;
    return new Promise<boolean>((resolve) => {
      repondre = resolve;
    });
  }

  function reponse(oui: boolean): void {
    message.value = null;
    repondre?.(oui);
    repondre = null;
  }

   // readonly: components read the message; only the composable modifies it
  return { message: readonly(message), confirmer, reponse };
}
  • Lines 21 and 22: The state is declared as HORS for the function [useConfirmation] at the module level. It is therefore unique across the entire application: a single window serves all components;
  • Lines 25–30: [confirmer] opens the window (by assigning a value to the message) and returns a promise. It stores the function [resolve] from this promise in [repondre]: the promise will not be resolved until the user has responded;
  • lines 32–35: The user’s response closes the window and resolves the promise to [true] or [false];
  • line 39: components can read the message, but not modify it.

The window:

<!--
  =========================================================================
  12-confirmation/src/components/FenetreConfirmation.vue
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  La fenêtre modale, placée UNE fois dans App.vue.
    - <Teleport to="body"> : son HTML est inséré à la fin de <body>, hors
      de l'arborescence des composants - une fenêtre modale doit passer
      au-dessus de tout, quel que soit l'endroit où elle est déclarée ;
    - mêmes classes Bootstrap qu'une vraie modale (.modal, .modal-backdrop),
      affichées "en dur" (show d-block) : pas besoin du JavaScript de Bootstrap ;
    - clavier : Échap = Non ; le focus est placé sur le bouton "Non" (le
      choix le moins dangereux) à l'ouverture.
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { nextTick, onUnmounted, useTemplateRef, watch } from 'vue';
import { useConfirmation } from '../composables/useConfirmation';

const { message, reponse } = useConfirmation();
const boutonNon = useTemplateRef<HTMLButtonElement>('boutonNon');

function clavier(e: KeyboardEvent): void {
  if (e.key === 'Escape') {
    reponse(false);
  }
}

// on open: focus on "No," listen for the Esc key; on close: stop listening
watch(message, async (valeur) => {
  if (valeur !== null) {
    document.addEventListener('keydown', clavier);
    await nextTick();
    boutonNon.value?.focus();
  } else {
    document.removeEventListener('keydown', clavier);
  }
});
onUnmounted(() => document.removeEventListener('keydown', clavier));
</script>

<template>
  <Teleport to="body">
    <template v-if="message !== null">
      <div class="modal-backdrop fade show"></div>
      <div class="modal fade show d-block" tabindex="-1" role="alertdialog" aria-modal="true" @click.self="reponse(false)">
        <div class="modal-dialog modal-dialog-centered">
          <div class="modal-content">
            <div class="modal-header">
              <h5 class="modal-title">Confirmation</h5>
              <button type="button" class="btn-close" aria-label="Fermer" @click="reponse(false)"></button>
            </div>
            <div class="modal-body">
              <p class="mb-0">{{ message }}</p>
            </div>
            <div class="modal-footer">
              <button ref="boutonNon" type="button" class="btn btn-secondary" @click="reponse(false)">Non, revenir</button>
              <button type="button" class="btn btn-danger" @click="reponse(true)">Oui, confirmer</button>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </template>
  </Teleport>
</template>
  • line 42: the window’s HTML is inserted at the end of [<body>], outside the component tree: a modal window must take precedence over everything else, regardless of where it is declared;
  • line 45: the [Bootstrap] classes of a modal window, displayed “hard-coded” ([show d-block]): no need for the [JavaScript] from [Bootstrap];
  • line 45: the modifier [.self]: only a click on the element itself (the shaded area), and not on the window containing it, triggers the “No” response;
  • Lines 29–37: Upon opening, the program listens for the Esc key and sets the focus to the “No” button (the safest option: an accidental press of Enter won’t delete anything); upon closing, the program stops listening for keyboard input.

The component that uses it:

<!--
  =========================================================================
  12-confirmation/src/App.vue - utiliser la fenêtre de confirmation
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Même page que l'exemple 21 du cours NestJS (liens, boutons, confirmation),
  mais sans aucun aller-retour avec un serveur.
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
import FenetreConfirmation from './components/FenetreConfirmation.vue';
import { useConfirmation } from './composables/useConfirmation';

interface Contact {
  id: number;
  nom: string;
}

const contacts = ref<Contact[]>([
  { id: 1, nom: 'Jean MARTIN' },
  { id: 2, nom: 'Alice DURAND' },
  { id: 3, nom: 'Luc GERMAN' },
]);
const message = ref('');
const { confirmer } = useConfirmation();

// an async function: it "waits" for the user's response
async function supprimer(c: Contact): Promise<void> {
  if (!(await confirmer(`Supprimer le contact ${c.nom} ?`))) {
    message.value = 'Suppression abandonnée.';
    return;
  }
  contacts.value = contacts.value.filter((x) => x.id !== c.id);
  message.value = `${c.nom} a été supprimé.`;
}

async function toutSupprimer(): Promise<void> {
  if (await confirmer(`Supprimer les ${contacts.value.length} contacts ?`)) {
    contacts.value = [];
    message.value = 'Tous les contacts ont été supprimés.';
  }
}
</script>
